notes.1: (tn, Heb): “was old, coming into the days” (i.e., advancing in years).

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא יִחַם לוֹ.* 
אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ: כָּל הַמְבַזֶּה בְּגָדִים, אֵינוֹ נֶהֶנָה מֵהֶם לַסוֹף, לְפִי שֶׁקָּרַע אֶת כְּנַף הַמְּעִיל לְשָׁאוּל. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחֲמָנִי: כְּשֶׁרָאָה דָוִד אֶת הַמַּלְאָךְ עוֹמֵד בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וְחַרְבּוֹ בְּיָדוֹ, נִצְטַנֵּן דָּמוֹ מִיִּרְאָתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *But he was not warmed.* Our Rabbis concluded and said: “He who disgraces clothing will ultimately be deprived of their pleasures. Because David tore the skirt of Saul’s robe (Samuel I 24:5) consequently, they did not warm him” (Berachoth 62b). As David saw the angel of death standing in Jerusalem and his sword in his hand, his blood became cold from fear of him.

notes.4: (tn, Heb): “let them seek for my master, the king, a young girl, a virgin.” The third person plural subject of the verb is indefinite (see GKC 460 �144.f). The appositional expression, “a young girl, a virgin,” is idiomatic; the second term specifically defines the more general first term (see IBHS 230 �12.3b).
notes.5: (tn, Heb): “and she will stand before the king.” The Hebrew phrase “stand before” can mean “to attend; to serve” (BDB 764 s.v. עָמַד).
notes.6: (tn, Heb): “and she will lie down in your bosom.” The expression might imply sexual intimacy (see 2 Sam 12:3 [where the lamb symbolizes Bathsheba] and Mic 7:5), though v. 4b indicates that David did not actually have sex with the young woman.
notes.7: (tn, Heb): “and my master, the king, will be warm.”

rashi.heb:
*בְתוּלָה.* 
בְּתוּלֶיהָ מְחַמְּמִין אֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ.
rashi.eng: *A virgin.* her virginity warms her flesh.

rashi.heb:
*סֹכֶנֶת.* 
מְחַמֶּמֶת, וְכֵן: וּבוֹקֵעַ עֵצִים יִסָּכֶן בָּם.
rashi.eng: *A warmer.* Heb. סכנת a warmer, and similarly “and he who chops wood is warmed (יסכן) by them” (Eccl. 10:9).

notes.8: (tn, Heb): “through all the territory of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*לֹא יְדָעָהּ.* 
שֶׁהַבְּתוּלָה יָפָה לְחַמֵּם מִן הַבְּעוּלָה. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: מִשּׁוּם לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ נָשִׁים, וּכְבָר הָיוּ לוֹ שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר.
rashi.eng: *did not know her.*

notes.10: (tn): Heb “son of Haggith,” but since this formula usually designates the father (who in this case was David), the translation specifies that David was Adonijah’s father. Haggith was one of David’s wives (2 Sam 3:4; 2 Chr 3:2).

rashi.heb:
*מִתְנַשֵּׂא.* 
מִתְפָּאֵר.
rashi.eng: *Exalted himself.* He exalted himself.

rashi.heb:
*וַחֲמִשִּׁים אִישׁ.* 
נְטוּלֵי טְחוֹל וַחֲקוּקֵי כַּפּוֹת רַגְלַיִם.
rashi.eng: *And fifty men.* had their spleens removed and the soles of their feet were scraped.

notes.16: (tn, Heb): “did not correct him from his days.” The phrase “from his days” means “from his earliest days,” or “ever in his life.” See GKC 382 �119.w, n. 2.
notes.17: (tn, Heb): “and she gave birth to him after Absalom.” This does not imply they had the same mother; Absalom’s mother was Maacah, not Haggith (2 Sam 3:4).

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא עֲצָבוֹ.* 
לֹא הִכְעִיסוֹ, לִמֶּדְךָ שֶׁהַמּוֹנֵעַ תּוֹכָחָה מִבְּנוֹ, מְבִיאוֹ לִידֵי מִיתָה.
rashi.eng: *And his father had not angered him.* His father never angered him. This episode teaches you that “he who refrains from rebuking his child brings him to his death.”

rashi.heb:
*וְגַם הוּא טוֹב תֹּאַר.* 
כְּאַבְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וּכְאַבְשָׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה אִישׁ יָפֶה, הִיא גָּרְמָה לָהֶם שֶׁנִּתְגָּאוּ.
rashi.eng: *And he too was of very handsome appearance.* Absalom about whom it is written (Samuel II 14:25) “And as Absalom there was none so handsome.” This caused them, [Absalom and Adoniahu], to be proud.

rashi.heb:
*וְאֹתוֹ יָלְדָה.* 
אִמּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And she bore him.* his mother.

rashi.heb:
*אַחֲרֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם.* 
כְּלוֹמַר גִּדְּלַתּוֹ אַחַר תַּרְבּוּת שֶׁגִּדְלָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁל אַבְשָׁלוֹם.
rashi.eng: *After Absalom.* This is to say that his mother reared him in the same spoiled manner that Absalom’s mother reared him.

notes.20: (tn, Heb): “Adonijah.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*עִם יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה.* 
לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁבְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד עָלָיו, עַל שֶׁהָרַג אֶת אַבְנֵר וַעֲמָשָׂא וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם, וְסוֹפוֹ שֶׁיְּצַוֶּה אֶת בְּנוֹ הַמּוֹלֵךְ תַּחְתָּיו עָלָיו, לְפִיכָךְ הָיָה רוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּמְלֹךְ זֶה עַל יָדוֹ, וְיֶאֱהָבֶנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *With Joab the son of Zeruiah.* Because he knew that David bore a grudge against him for having killed Abner, Amasa, and Absalom, and that he would eventually charge his son, who would reign in his place, to deal with him. Joab, therefore, preferred that this one, [Adoniahu] should reign through his help and so that Adoniahu should favor him.

rashi.heb:
*וְעִם אֶבְיָתָר הַכֹּהֵן.* 
שֶׁנִּסְתַּלֵּק מִן הַכְּהֻנָּה מִשֶּׁבָּרַח דָּוִד מִירוּשָׁלַיִם מִפְּנֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁשָּׁאַל בָּאוּרִים וְתֻמִּים וְלֹא עָלְתָה לּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּעַל אֶבְיָתָר, וְהָיָה מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל עֵלִי, וְיָדַע שֶׁלֹּא יְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה, שֶׁהֲרֵי נֶאֱמַר לְעֵלִי: וַהֲקִימֹתִי לִי כֹּהֵן נֶאֱמָן וְהִתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵי מְשִׁיחִי, וְהָיָה חָפֵץ שֶׁיַּעֲמֹד זֶה עַל יָדוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And with Abiathar the priest.* Because he was dismissed from the priesthood at the time when David was escaping from Jerusalem because of Absalom. When Abiathar consulted the Urim and Tumim and was unsuccessful, as it is said, (Samuel II 15:24) “And Abiathar went up.” And he was a descendent of Eli. And Abiathar knew that he would not serve in the days of Solomon, for it was said to Eli “And I will raise Me up a faithful priest and he shall walk before My anointed one” (Samuel I 2:35). Abiathar preferred [therefore,] that Adoniahu become king through his assistance.

rashi.heb:
*וְנָתָן הַנָּבִיא.* 
שֶׁנִּבֵּא לְדָוִד שֶׁשְּׁלֹמֹה יִמְלֹךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: וּשְׁלֹמֹה יִהְיֶה שְׁמוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And Nathan the prophet.* who prophesied to David that Solomon would reign, as it is said in (Chronicles I 22:9) “and Solomon shall be his name.”

notes.23: (tc): The ancient Greek version omits this appositional phrase.

rashi.heb:
*וּמְרִיא.* 
שׁוֹר שֶׁל פְּטָם.
rashi.eng: *And fatlings.* [These are sheep and] oxen which have been fattened by forceful feeding.

rashi.heb:
*אֶבֶן הַזֹּחֶלֶת.* 
אֶבֶן גְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁהָיוּ הַבַּחוּרִים מְנַסִּין בָּהּ אֶת כֹּחָם לַהֲזִיזָהּ וּלְגָרְרָהּ, לְשׁוֹן מַיִם זוֹחֲלִין: זוֹחֲלֵי עָפָר. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: אֶבֶן סְכוּתָא, שֶׁעוֹמְדִין עָלֶיהָ וְצוֹפִין לְמֵרָחוֹק.
rashi.eng: *The stone of Zoheleth.* A huge stone with which the young men would test their strength to move or drag it. [Zoheleth is] an expression similar to moving water (זוחלין) or “those that move (זוחלי) on the dust” (Deut. 32:24). Targum Jonathan renders this word זוֹחֶלֶת a ‘lookout stone,’ upon which one could stand and look far into the distance.

rashi.heb:
*עֵין רֹגֵל.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: עֵין קַצְרָא, הוּא כּוֹבֵס, שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן בִּגְדֵי צֶמֶר בְּרַגְלָיו, עַל יְדֵי בְּעִיטָה.
rashi.eng: *En-Rogel.* which was a well used by a clothes washer who would press the woolen clothes which he washed, with his feet, by stamping [on them].

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת שְׁלֹמֹה אָחִיו לֹא קָרָא.* 
שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ הָיָה, שֶׁהִתְנַבֵּא עָלָיו הַנָּבִיא לִמְלֹךְ.
rashi.eng: *And his brother Solomon, he did not call.* for he knew that the prophet had prophesied about him that he would reign [after David’s death].

notes.26: (tn, Heb): “and our master David does not know.”

notes.27: (tn, Heb): “now, come.” The imperative of הָלַךְ (halakh) is here used as an introductory interjection. See BDB 234 s.v. חָלַךְ.

rashi.heb:
*וּמַלְּטִי אֶת נַפְשֵׁךְ.* 
מִן הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת לְאַחַר מוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ, שֶׁיִּרְצֶה בְּנֵךְ לִמְלֹךְ, כְּמָה שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
rashi.eng: *And you shall save your life.* and save your soul from the rivalry which will follow the death of the king, for your son will wish to reign as the Holy One, Blessed be He, promised him.

notes.29: (tn, Heb): “come, go to.” The imperative of הָלַךְ (halakh) is here used as an introductory interjection. See BDB 234 s.v. חָלַךְ.

notes.31: (tn): In the Hebrew text the sentence is introduced by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”), which here draws attention to Nathan’s concluding word of assurance and support. For this use of the word, see HALOT 252 s.v. הִנֵּה.
notes.32: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “I will come after you.”

notes.35: (tn, Heb): “bowed low and bowed down to.”

notes.36: (tc): Instead of עַתָּה (’attah, “now”) many Hebrew mss, along with the Old Greek, Syriac Peshitta, and Latin Vulgate, have the similar sounding independent pronoun אַתָּה (’attah, “you”). This reading is followed in the present translation.

notes.38: (tc): Many Hebrew mss have עַתָּה (’attah, “now”) rather than the similar sounding independent pronoun אַתָּה (’attah, “you”).
notes.39: (tn, Heb): “the eyes of all Israel are upon you to declare to them who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him.”

notes.40: (tn): The words “if a decision is not made” are added for clarification.
notes.42: (tn, Heb): “I and my son Solomon.” The order has been reversed in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.43: (tn, Heb): “will be guilty”; NASB “considered offenders”; TEV “treated as traitors.”

rashi.heb:
*חַטָּאִים.* 
חֲסֵרִים וּמְנוּעִין מִן הַגְּדֻלָּה, כְּמוֹ: אֶל הַשַּׂעֲרָה וְלֹא יַחֲטִא.
rashi.eng: *And I and my son shall be considered offenders.* Instead they will always be lacking and restrained from any greatness.

notes.44: (tn, Heb): “look.” The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) here draws attention to Nathan’s arrival and invites the audience to view the scene through the eyes of the participants.

notes.45: (tn, Heb): “ground.” Since this was indoors, “floor” is more appropriate than “ground.”

rashi.heb:
*אַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ.* 
בִּתְמִיָּה.
rashi.eng: *Did you say.* The interrogative.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי יָרַד הַיּוֹם.* 
שֶׁהָעִיר הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה, וְאֶבֶן הַזּוֹחֶלֶת לְמַטָּה בַּגַּיְא.
rashi.eng: *For he went down on this day.* The city was on higher ground and the אֶבֶן הַזוֹחֶלֶת was below in a valley.

notes.49: (tc): Many Hebrew mss and ancient textual witnesses agree with the Qere in reading this as singular, “your servant.”
notes.50: (tn, Heb): “From my master the king is this thing done, and you did not make known to your servants who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him?”

notes.52: (sn): Summon Bathsheba. Bathsheba must have left the room when Nathan arrived (see 1:22).
notes.53: (tn, Heb): “she came before the king and stood before the king.”

notes.56: (tn, Heb): “bowed low, face [to] the ground, and bowed down to the king.”

notes.57: (sn): Summon…Nathan. Nathan must have left the room when Bathsheba reentered.

notes.59: (tn): The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.
notes.60: (tn, Heb): “mount Solomon my son on the mule that belongs to me and take him down to Gihon.”

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַפִּרְדָּה אֲשֶׁר לִי.* 
הוּא סִימָן לוֹ שֶׁיִּמְלֹךְ, וּתְחִלַּת הַגְּדֻלָּה, שֶׁאֵין הֶדְיוֹט רוֹכֵב עַל סוּסוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *On my own mule.* This will be a positive sign that he will reign and the beginning of his advancement to greatness since a commoner is forbidden to ride on the king’s horse.

rashi.heb:
*אֶל גִּחוֹן.* 
הוּא מַעְיַן הַשִּׁלּוֹחַ, מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים אֶלָּא עַל הַמַּעְיָן, סִימָן שֶׁתִּמָּשֵׁךְ מַלְכוּתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *To Gihon.* Gihon and Shiloah are synonymous. From this is derived the custom not to anoint the kings except at the well, to symbolize thereby that his kingdom shall be endless as the waters of a well.

rashi.heb:
*וּמָשַׁח אֹתוֹ.* 
נוֹתֵן לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו, כְּמִין נֵזֶר.
rashi.eng: *And he shall anoint him.* To anoint him between the lids of his eyes in the form of a crown.

notes.65: (tn, Heb): “So may the Lord God of my master the king say.”

rashi.heb:
*אָמֵן.* 
שֶׁיִּחְיֶה שְׁלֹמֹה.
rashi.eng: *Amen.* “Long live king Solomon.”

notes.66: (tn, Heb): “and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my master King David.”

rashi.heb:
*מִכִּסֵּא אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ.* 
מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מִתְקַנֵּא בִּבְנוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Than the throne of my lord king David.* From this we may derive that a father does not feel envy when his son surpasses him.

notes.67: (sn): The Kerethites and Pelethites were members of David’s royal guard (see 2 Sam 8:18). The Kerethites may have been descendants of an ethnic group originating in Crete.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַכְּרֵתִי וְהַפְּלֵתִי.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וְקַשָּׁתַיָּא וְקַלָּעַיָּא. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: אוּרִים וְתֻמִּים.
rashi.eng: *And the archers and the slingers.* The Targum renders this, the archers and the slingers. Our Sages however, maintain that this refers to the אוּרִים וְתֻּמִים.

notes.68: (tn, Heb): “the horn of oil.” This has been specified as olive oil in the translation for clarity. A horn filled with oil. An animal’s horn was used as an oil flask in the anointing ceremony.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת קֶרֶן הַשֶּׁמֶן.* 
מִשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעָשָׂה משֶׁה.
rashi.eng: *And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil.* The special holy oil compounded by Moses in the desert.

rashi.heb:
*מִן הָאֹהֶל.* 
שֶׁהָאָרוֹן נָתוּן בְּעִיר דָּוִד, וּצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה לִפְנֵי הָאָרוֹן (יומא נב ב).
rashi.eng: *From the tent.* Since the Holy Ark was in Jerusalem which was known as the city of David, and the jug of oil of anointment was before it, both were, therefore, in Jerusalem, as we have learned in the Tractate Yoma (52b).

notes.70: (tn, Heb): “and all the people went up after him, and the people were playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy and the ground split open at the sound of them.” The verb בָּקַע (baqa’, “to split open”), which elsewhere describes the effects of an earthquake, is obviously here an exaggeration for the sake of emphasis.

rashi.heb:
*בַּחֲלִלִים.* 
פלאוט"י בְּלַעַ"ז (חָלִיל).
rashi.eng: *The flutes.* A flute also in old French.

rashi.heb:
*וַתִּבָּקַע הָאָרֶץ.* 
דִּבְּרוּ הַנְּבִיאִים בִּלְשׁוֹן הֲבַאי, כִּלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם.
rashi.eng: *And the earth was rent.* Prophets [who] made use of exaggerations [in descriptions], as is common by most people.

notes.71: (tn, Heb): “And Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard, now they had finished eating.”
notes.72: (tn, Heb): “Why is the city’s sound noisy?”

notes.73: (tn): The Hebrew text has “look” at this point. The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh), “look draws attention to Jonathan’s arrival and invites the audience to view the scene through the eyes of the participants.
notes.75: (tn, Heb): “you are a man of strength [or “ability”] and you bring a message [that is] good.” Another option is to understand the phrase אִישׁ חַיִל (’ish khayil) in the sense of “a worthy man,” that is “loyal.” See also 1 Kgs 1:52 and HALOT 311 s.v. חַיִל.

notes.77: (tn): For a similar use of אֲבָל (’aval), see Gen 17:19, where God rejects Abraham’s proposal and offers an alternative.
notes.78: (tn): The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.

rashi.heb:
*אֲבָל אֲדֹנֵינוּ.* 
כְּלוֹמַר, עַכְשָׁיו אֵין בְּשׂוֹרָתִי טוֹבָה לְךָ.
rashi.eng: *But our lord.* Jonathan replied, “… at this moment my report is not of good tidings for you.”

notes.79: (tn): I.e., designated by anointing with oil.

notes.80: (tn, Heb): “And also Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.”

notes.82: (tn): The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.
notes.83: (tc): Many Hebrew mss agree with the Qere in reading simply “God.”
notes.84: (tn, Heb): “make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.” The term שֵׁם (shem, “name”) is used here of one’s fame and reputation.

notes.86: (tn): The Hebrew text reads, “and the king said.”
notes.87: (tn): Or “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who….” In this blessing formula אֲשֶׁר (’asher, “who; because”) introduces the reason why the one being blessed deserves the honor.

notes.90: (sn): Grabbed hold of the horns of the altar. The “horns” of the altar were the horn-shaped projections on the four corners of the altar (see Exod 27:2). By going to the holy place and grabbing hold of the horns of the altar, Adonijah was seeking asylum from Solomon.

rashi.heb:
*בְּקַרְנוֹת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.* 
שֶׁהָיָה בְּגִבְעוֹן, אָמַר: הֲרוּגֵי בֵּית דִּין נִקְבָּרִין בְּקִבְרֵי בֵּית דִּין, אָמוּת כָּאן, וְאֶקָּבֵר בְּקִבְרֵי אֲבוֹתַי (תנחומא מסעי יב).
rashi.eng: *And he rose up and took hold of the horns of the altar.* which was in Gibeon. He said, "Those put to death by Beth Din are buried in the graves of Beth Din. I shall die here, and be buried in the graves of my forefathers." Thus did Rabbi Tanhuma expound.

notes.91: (tn, Heb): “King Solomon.” The name and title have been replaced by the pronoun (“you”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.93: (tn, Heb): “if he is a man of strength [or ability].” In this context, where Adonijah calls himself a “servant,” implying allegiance to the new king, the phrase אִישׁ חַיִל (’ish khayil) probably carries the sense of “a worthy man,” that is, “loyal” (see HALOT 311 s.v. חַיִל).
notes.94: (tn, Heb): “but if evil is found in him.”

notes.95: (tn, Heb): “sent and they brought him down.”

notes.97: (tn, Heb): “and the days of David approached to die.”

notes.99: (tn, Heb): “going the way of all the earth.”

notes.100: (tn, Heb): “keep the charge of the Lord your God.”
notes.103: (tn, Heb): “then you will cause to succeed all which you do and all which you turn there.”

notes.104: (tn, Heb): “then the Lord will establish his word which he spoke to me, saying.”
notes.106: (tn, Heb): “by walking before me in faithfulness.”
notes.109: (tn, Heb): “there will not be cut off from you a man from upon the throne of Israel.”

notes.110: (tn, Heb): “what he did to the two commanders…and he killed them.”
notes.111: (tn, Heb): “he shed the blood of battle in peace.”
notes.112: (tn, Heb): “and he shed the blood of battle when he killed which is on his waist and on his sandal[s] which are on his feet.” That is, he covered himself with guilt and his guilt was obvious to all who saw him.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לִי.* 
שֶׁהֶרְאָה הַסֵּפֶר שֶׁשָּׁלַח דָּוִד בְּיַד אוּרִיָּה. (במדרש רבי תנחומא שם)
rashi.eng: *You also know what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me.* by showing them the letter which David had sent through Uriah.

rashi.heb:
*דְּמֵי מִלְחָמָה בְּשָׁלֹם.* 
שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם שָׁלוֹם עִמּוֹ, וְלֹא הָיוּ נִשְׁמָרִים מִמֶּנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *And shed the blood of war in peace.* Since they were at peace with him, they were not on guard against him.

rashi.heb:
*בַּחֲגֹרָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר בְּמָתְנָיו.* 
שֶׁחָגַר חַרְבּוֹ מְצֻמֶּדֶת עַל מָתְנָיו, שֶׁלֹּא כְּדֶרֶךְ הַחוֹגְרִים, בְּצֵאתוֹ לִקְרַאת עֲמָשָׂא, וּפִיהָ לְמַטָּה כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּפֹּל, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְהוּא יָצָא וַתִּפֹּל, וּכְשֶׁנָּפְלָה וּנְטָלָהּ, כְּסָבוּר עֲמָשָׂא שֶׁלֹּא נְטָלָהּ אֶלָּא לְהַגְבִּיהָהּ מִן הָאָרֶץ, וְלֹא נִשְׁמַר מֵהַחֶרֶב אֲשֶׁר בְּיַד יוֹאָב.
rashi.eng: *And he put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins.* He had girded his sword, attached to his loins, not in the customary manner of those girding swords, and he went out to meet Amasa. He turned the opening downward so that it should easily fall out of the sheath to the ground as it says (Samuel II 20:8) “and he went out towards Amasa and it fell out.” As soon as it fell, Joab [nonchalantly] retrieved it, and held it ready in his hand. Amasa presumed he retrieved it solely to pick it up from the ground, and was not alert to guard himself against an attack from the sword which was in Joab’s hand.

rashi.heb:
*וּבְנַעֲלוֹ אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלָיו.* 
אֶת אַבְנֵר הָרַג בְּעָרְמָה, שֶׁשְּׁאָלוֹ גִּדֶּמֶת הֵיאָךְ חוֹלֶצֶת, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּטֵּהוּ יוֹאָב אֶל תּוֹךְ הַשַּׁעַר לְדַבֵּר אִתּוֹ 'בַשֶּׁלִי', לְשׁוֹן 'שַׁל' נְעָלֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *and in his shoes that (were) on his feet.*

notes.114: (tn, Heb): “and do not bring down his grey hair in peace [to] Sheol.”

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא תוֹרֵד שֵׂיבָתוֹ בְּשָׁלֹם שְׁאֹל.* 
אַל תַּנִּיחֵהוּ לָמוּת מִיתַת עַצְמוֹ וְלִפֹּל בְּגֵיהִנֹּם.
rashi.eng: *And do not let his hoary head go down to the grave in peace.* Do not let him die a natural death [since this will minimize his worldly punishment] and cause him to fall into purgatory for torturous purification.

notes.115: (tn, Heb): “do loyalty with”; or “act faithfully toward.”
notes.116: (tn, Heb): “and let them be among the ones who eat [at] your table.”

notes.119: (tn, Heb): “and he cursed me with a horrible curse on the day I went to Mahanaim.”

rashi.heb:
*קְלָלָה נִמְרֶצֶת.* 
מְפֹרֶשֶׁת, כְּמוֹ: מַה יַּמְרִיצְךָ; (שם ו כה): וּמַה נִּמְרְצוּ, כְּמוֹ מַה נִּמְלְצוּ.
rashi.eng: *Who cursed me with a grievous curse.* [Others maintain] נִמְרֶצֶת means clear and unquestionable as (we find) in (Job 16:3): “what will bring clarity to you (ימריצך),” and (Job 6:25): “how clear (נמרצו) are right words,” the same as נִמְלְצוּ a derivation of the word מְלִיצָה, an interpretation or clarification.

notes.122: (tc): The Lucianic recension of the Old Greek and the Vulgate have here “you” rather than “now.” The two words are homonyms in Hebrew.
notes.123: (tn, Heb): “what you should do to him.”
notes.124: (tn, Heb): “bring his grey hair down in blood [to] Sheol.”

rashi.heb:
*כִּי אִישׁ חָכָם אָתָּה.* 
תֵּן לִבְּךָ לִמְצֹא לוֹ עֲוֹן מָוֶת בִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר אַחֵר, וְזֶהוּ: וְיָדַעְתָּ אֵת אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה לּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *For you are a wise man.* Turn your attention to find for him an iniquity justifying a death penalty in another matter.

notes.125: (tn, Heb): “and David lay down with his fathers.”
notes.126: (sn): The phrase the city of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.

notes.127: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*וַתִּכֹּן מַלְכֻתוֹ מְאֹד.* 
אַף עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנִים.
rashi.eng: *And his kingdom was firmly established.* He was also master and ruler of all heavenly creatures and beings.

notes.132: (tn, Heb): “set their face to me to be king.”
notes.133: (tn, Heb): “and the kingdom turned about and became my brother’s, for from the Lord it became his.”

notes.134: (tn, Heb): “Do not turn back my face.”

notes.136: (tn, Heb): “Say to Solomon the king, for he will not turn back your face, that he might give to me Abishag the Shunammite for a wife.”

notes.139: (tn, Heb): “he set up a throne for the mother of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*לְדַבֶּר לוֹ.* 
לְדַבֵּר בִּשְׁבִילוֹ, בִּשְׁבִיל אֲדוֹנִיָּהוּ.
rashi.eng: *to speak to him.* to speak on his behalf; on behalf of Adoniahu.

rashi.heb:
*לְאֵם הַמֶּלֶךְ.* 
אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (בבא בתרא צא ב): לְאִמָּהּ שֶׁל מַלְכוּת, הִיא רוּת.
rashi.eng: *for the king’s mother.* Our Sages said, however, “the king’s mother” is a reference to Ruth.

notes.140: (tn): Or “I’d like to make just one request of you.”
notes.141: (tn, Heb): “Do not turn back my face.”
notes.142: (tn, Heb): “and the king said to her.”

rashi.heb:
*וְשַׁאֲלִי לוֹ אֶת הַמְּלוּכָה.* 
מִשֶּׁיִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּשַׁרְבִיטוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ, הוּא תְּחִלַּת הַשְּׂרָרָה.
rashi.eng: *… ask for him the kingdom also.* From the moment a commoner uses the scepter of the king, that is the beginning of authority.

notes.144: (tn, Heb): “So may God do to me, and so may he add.”
notes.145: (tn, Heb): “if with his life Adonijah has not spoken this word.”

rashi.heb:
*עָשָׂה לִי בַּיִת.* 
בֵּית הַמְּלוּכָה, כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּר בְּיַד נָתָן.
rashi.eng: *… Who has established me.* “… and Who has made me a house” a house of royalty as he had spoken through Nathan the prophet.

notes.147: (tn): The Hebrew text adds, “by the hand of.”
notes.148: (tn, Heb): “and he struck him and he died.”

notes.150: (tn, Heb): “you are a man of death.”
notes.151: (tn, Heb): “and because you suffered through all which my father suffered.”

rashi.heb:
*עֲנָתֹת לֵךְ.* 
מִשָּׁם הָיָה.
rashi.eng: *Go to Anathoth to your own fields….* He was from there.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי אִישׁ מָוֶת אָתָּה.* 
שֶׁמָּרַדְתָּ בְּמַלְכוּת אָבִי בִּהְיוֹתְךָ עִם אֲדוֹנִיָּהוּ, לְהַמְלִיכוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *For you are deservant of death.* Because you rebelled against the kingdom of my father when you were with Adoniahu to appoint him king without the knowledge of my father.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי נָשָׂאתָ אֶת אֲרוֹן.* 
בִּבְרֹחַ אָבִי מִפְּנֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם.
rashi.eng: *Because you did bear the Ark of the Lord God before David my father.* as my father was escaping from before Absalom.

rashi.heb:
*וְכִי הִתְעַנִּיתָ.* 
עִמּוֹ בְּאוֹתָהּ הַצָּרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי אָמְרוּ הָעָם רָעֵב וְעָיֵף וְצָמֵא בַּמִּדְבָּר.
rashi.eng: *And because you were afflicted.* with him in those very same afflictions, as it says (Samuel II 17:29) “for they said the people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.”

notes.152: (tn, Heb): “Solomon drove out Abiathar from being a priest to the Lord.”
notes.153: (tn, Heb): “fulfilling the word of the Lord which he spoke against the house of Eli in Shiloh.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶת אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר עַל בֵּית עֵלִי.* 
וַהֲקִימֹתִי לִי כֹּהֵן נֶאֱמָן וְגוֹ', וְהִבַּטְתָּ צַר מָעוֹן וְגוֹ', וּמִשֶּׁחָרְבָה שִׁילֹה, לֹא הָיָה בַּיִת חָשׁוּב לַעֲבוֹדָה לְהַקָּבָּ"ה, וְעַתָּה כְּשֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה, מִלֵּא הַקָּבָּ"ה אֶת דְּבָרוֹ לְגָרֵשׁ אֶת בְּנֵי עֵלִי.
rashi.eng: *Which He spoke concerning the house of Eli.* [Scripture predicts the end of the house of Eli:] “And I will raise Me up a faithful priest” (Samuel I 2:35) or “And you shall see a rival in My habitation” (Samuel I 2:32). From the time of the destruction of Shilo, there was no house worthy of the service to the Holy One Blessed be He and now that the Temple will be built, the Holy One Blessed be He fulfilled His word to banish the children of Eli.

notes.154: (tn, Heb): “turned after” (also later in this verse).
notes.155: (tn, Heb): “Joab.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.156: (sn): Grabbed hold of the horns of the altar. The “horns” of the altar were the horn-shaped projections on the four corners of the altar (see Exod 27:2). By going to the holy place and grabbing hold of the horns of the altar, Joab was seeking asylum from Solomon.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַשְּׁמֻעָה בָּאָה עַד יוֹאָב.* 
שְׁמוּעַת מִצְוַת דָּוִד שֶׁצִּוָּה לְהָרְגוֹ, וְיָדַע שֶׁשְּׁלֹמֹה שׂוֹנְאוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And the tidings came to Joab.* the report of David’s charge, that he had commanded to kill him, and he [also] knew that Solomon disliked him.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי יוֹאָב נָטָה אַחֲרֵי אֲדֹנִיָּה וְאַחֲרֵי אַבְשָׁלוֹם לֹא נָטָה.* 
סוֹף דָּבָר, אֲבָל בִּקֵשׁ לִנְטוֹת, אֶלָּא נִתְיָרֵא שֶׁעֲדַיִן לַחְלוּחִית שֶׁל דָּוִד קַיֶּמֶת.
rashi.eng: *For Joab turned after Adoniahu, and after Absalom he did not turn.* The end of the matter was [that Joab did not follow him], but he did seek to turn after him, but for the fact that he was fearful, because the vigor of David’s might was still present.

notes.157: (tn, Heb): “and it was related to King Solomon.”
notes.158: (tn, Heb): “so Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying.”

notes.159: (tn, Heb): “saying, “In this way Joab spoke and in this way he answered me.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא.* 
שְׁתַּיִם לֹא אֲקַבֵּל עָלַי, קְלָלוֹת שֶׁקִּלְלַנִי דָּוִד אָבִיךָ בְּמִיתַת אַבְנֵר: יָחוּלוּ עַל רֹאשׁ יוֹאָב, יְקַבְּלֵם שְׁלֹמֹה עָלָיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֵצֵא.
rashi.eng: *And he said “No…”.* Two punishments I will not accept upon myself. The curses that your father David cursed me at the death of Abner, “They shall fall upon the head of Joab,” let Solomon accept them upon himself, and afterward I will come out.

notes.161: (tn, Heb): “take away the undeserved bloodshed which Joab spilled from upon me and from upon the house of my father.”

rashi.heb:
*עֲשֵׂה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר.* 
אֲנִי מְקַבְּלָם עָלַי, לְכָךְ נִדְבְּקוּ כָּל אֵלֶּה בְּזֶרַע דָּוִד, עֻזִּיָּה הָיָה מְצֹרָע, אָסָא מַחֲזִיק בַּפֶּלֶךְ, יְהוֹיָקִים נָפַל בַּחֶרֶב, וַחֲסַר לֶחֶם צִדְקִיָּהוּ.
rashi.eng: *Do as he said.* I will accept the curses upon myself. Therefore, all these [curses] became attached to the offspring of David. Uzziah was a leper (Chronicles II 26:19), Assa leaned on a staff (Kings I 15:23), Jehoiakim fell by the sword (Jeremiah 22:19), and one who lacked bread was Zedekiah (Kings II 25:30).

notes.162: (tn, Heb): “The Lord will cause his blood to return upon his head.”
notes.163: (tn, Heb): “because he struck down two men more innocent and better than he and he killed them with the sword, and my father David did not know.”

notes.166: (tn, Heb): “struck him and killed him.” The referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*בְּבֵיתוֹ בַּמִּדְבָּר.* 
שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ הֶפְקֵר כַּמִּדְבָּר, לַעֲנִיִּים.
rashi.eng: *And he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.* His home was ownerless and unrestricted as a wilderness for all the destitute and needy to use at their convenience.

notes.168: (tc): The Old Greek translation includes after v. 35 some fourteen verses that are absent from the MT.

notes.170: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.171: (tn, Heb): “and you may not go out from there here or there.”

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא תֵצֵא מִשָּׁם.* 
כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא מָצוּי לוֹ, וְלִמְצֹא לוֹ חֵטְא מָוֶת.
rashi.eng: *And do not go forth.* in order that he be accessible to him and that he might find him guilty of a crime deserving of death.

notes.172: (tn, Heb): “your blood will be upon your head.”

notes.173: (tn, Heb): “Good is the word, as my master the king has spoken.”

notes.177: (tn, Heb): “Is it not [true]…?” In the Hebrew text the statement is interrogative; the rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course it is.”
notes.179: (tn, Heb): “good is the word; I have heard.”

rashi.heb:
*וָאָעִד בְּךָ.* 
לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה.
rashi.eng: *And forewarned you.* Heb. ואעד, an expression referring to the legal warning given to the offender before committing the offense.

notes.180: (tn, Heb): “Why have you not kept the oath [to] the Lord and the commandment I commanded you?”

rashi.heb:
*אֵת שְׁבֻעַת ה'.* 
אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁבַּעְתִּיךָ בַּה'.
rashi.eng: *And why have you nor kept the oath of the Lord.* which I made you swear in the name of the Lord?

notes.181: (tn, Heb): “You know all the evil, for your heart knows, which you did to David my father.”
notes.182: (tn, Heb): “The Lord will cause your evil to return upon your head.”

notes.185: (tn): “The king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada and he went out and struck him down and he died.”
notes.186: (tn): “And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמַּמְלָכָה נָכוֹנָה וְגוֹ'.* 
כְּלוֹמַר, לֹא נֶעֱנַשׁ עַל כָּל אֵלֶּה.
rashi.eng: *And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.* that is to say, he was not punished for any of these deeds.

notes.187: (sn): The phrase City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
notes.188: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּתְחַתֵּן שְׁלֹמֹה.* 
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהָיָה שִׁמְעִי רַבּוֹ קַיָּם, לֹא נִתְחַתֵּן בּוֹ, מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: לְעוֹלָם יָדוּר אָדָם בִּמְקוֹם רַבּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And Solomon became allied by marriage.* as long as Shimei was alive he did not become allied to him in marriage. As a result, our Sages declare, a person should always live in the vicinity of his teacher where his influence and guidance are ever present.

rashi.heb:
*עַד כַּלֹּתוֹ לִבְנוֹת וְגוֹ'.* 
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָה לָהּ בַּיִת.
rashi.eng: *Until he completed building.* and afterward built a house for her.

notes.189: (sn): Offering sacrifices at the high places. The “high places” were places of worship that were naturally or artificially elevated.
notes.190: (tn, Heb): “for the name of the Lord.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor (thus the translation here, “to honor the Lord”). The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

rashi.heb:
*מְזַבְּחִים בַּבָּמוֹת.* 
לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, כָּל הָרוֹצֶה בּוֹנֶה מִזְבֵּחַ בְּרֹאשׁ גַּגּוֹ אוֹ בַּחֲצֵרוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Only the people sacrificed in the high places.* In the name of Heaven, each who so desired would build an altar at the top of his roof or in his yard [and offer his sacrifices there].

notes.191: (tn, Heb): “Solomon loved the Lord by walking in.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֶּאֱהַב שְׁלֹמֹה לָלֶכֶת בְּחֻקּוֹת דָּוִד אָבִיו.* 
אַרְבַּע שָׁנִים, עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִיל לִבְנוֹת הַבַּיִת, אֲבָל מִשֶּׁהִתְחִיל לִבְנוֹת, וַיִּתְחַתֵּן שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת פַּרְעֹה, נִמְצֵאתָ אוֹמֵר: כִּי עַל אַפִּי וְעַל חֲמָתִי הָיְתָה לִּי הָעִיר הַזֹּאת, לְמִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ אוֹתָהּ וְעַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה, כָּךְ שָׁנִינוּ בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם, לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁאֵין הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת כְּתוּבוֹת כַּסֵּדֶר.
rashi.eng: *And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father.* The first four years, as long as he did not begin to build the Temple. But from the time he began to build and he became allied in marriage to the daughter of Pharaoh this was no longer true. Consequently, the prophet declares “for this city has been to me as a provocation of my anger and of my fury from the day that they built it and until this day” (Jeremiah 32:31). Thus have we learned in Seder Olam (Chap. 15). We learn from this the passages are not written in chronological order.

rashi.heb:
*בַּבָּמוֹת הוּא מְזַבֵּחַ.* 
בִּגְנוּתוֹ דִּבֵּר הַכָּתוּב, שֶׁשָּׁהָה אֶת בִּנְיַן הַבַּיִת אַרְבַּע שָׁנִים.
rashi.eng: *Only he sacrificed… in the high places.* The text has discussed his dishonor. Since he delayed the construction of the Temple four years.

notes.193: (tn, Heb): “for it was the great high place.”
notes.194: (tn): The verb form is an imperfect, which is probably used here in a customary sense to indicate continued or repeated action in past time. See GKC 314 �107.b.

rashi.heb:
*הִיא הַבָּמָה הַגְּדוֹלָה.* 
הוּא מִזְבַּח הַנְּחשֶׁת שֶׁעָשָׂה משֶׁה בַּמִּדְבָּר, וְהֻקְבְּעָה בְּשִׁילֹה, חָרְבָה שִׁילֹה בִּימֵי עֵלִי וּבָא לְנוֹב, חָרְבָה נוֹב בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל, וּבָאוּ לְגִבְעוֹן.
rashi.eng: *That was the great high place.* That was the copper altar which Moses made in the desert and was instituted in Shilo. Shilo was destroyed in the days of Eli, and they came to Nob. Nob was destroyed in the days of Saul, and they came to Gibeon.

rashi.heb:
*יַעֲלֶה שְׁלֹמֹה.* 
כְּמוֹ מַעֲלֶה שְׁלֹמֹה.
rashi.eng: *did Solomon offer.*

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הַהוּא.* 
בְּיוֹם אֶחָד.
rashi.eng: *Upon that altar.* in one day.

notes.199: (tn, Heb): “in faithfulness and in innocence and in uprightness of heart with you.”
notes.200: (tn, Heb): “and you have kept to him this great loyalty and you gave to him a son [who] sits on his throne as this day.”

rashi.heb:
*וַתִּשְׁמָר לוֹ.* 
לְשׁוֹן מְאַמֵּת אֶת דְּבָרָיו, כְּמוֹ: וְשָׁמַר ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְךָ וְגוֹ', וְאַף כָּאן וַתִּשְׁמָר לוֹ אֶת הַחֶסֶד, הֶאֱמַנְתָּ דְבָרֶיךָ לְקַיֵּם לוֹ אֶת הַחֶסֶד, אֲשֶׁר הִבְטַחְתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי נָתָן הַנָּבִיא.
rashi.eng: *And You have kept for him.* an expression of authentication of his words as, “And the Lord your God shall keep for you the covenant” [means] You have authenticated your words to fulfill to him the kindness which You promised him through Nathan the prophet.

notes.201: (tn, Heb): “and I do not know going out or coming in.”

rashi.heb:
*נַעַר קָטֹן.* 
בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה הָיָה, וְזֶה לְךָ הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן, וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יְדִידְיָה, בּוֹ בַּפֶּרֶק עִנָּה אַמְנוֹן אֶת תָּמָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי כֵן וּלְאַבְשָׁלוֹם אָחוֹת, מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים וַיִּהְיוּ גֹזְזִים לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם וְהָרַג אֶת אַמְנוֹן, וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם בָּרַח וַיֵּלֶךְ גְּשׁוּרָה, וַיְהִי שָׁם שָׁלשׁ שָׁנִים, הֲרֵי חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים, וְשָׁב אַבְשָׁלוֹם לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, וַיֵּשֶׁב בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם שְׁנָתַיִם, הֲרֵי שֶׁבַע לִשְׁלֹמֹה, וּמָרַד בְּאָבִיו וְנֶהֱרַג, אַחַר זֹאת: וַיְהִי רָעָב בִּימֵי דָוִד שָׁלשׁ שָׁנִים, הֲרֵי עֶשֶׂר, בְּאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מָנָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וַיָּשׁוּטוּ בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁעָה חֳדָשִׁים, בִּשְׁנַת מוֹתוֹ תִּקֵּן מִשְׁמָרוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בִּשְׁנַת הָאַרְבָּעִים לְמַלְכוּת דָּוִיד נִדְרָשׁוּ, הֲרֵי שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה לַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה.
rashi.eng: *A little child.* He was twelve years old. And this is your figuring. And he called his name Jedidjah [Solomon] (Samuel II 12:25). At the same time Amnon violated Tamar, as it says “And it was after this, and Absalom had a sister, etc.” At the end of two years “And Absalom had sheepshearers, etc.,” and he killed Amnon. And Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years, so we have five years. And Absalom returned to Jerusalem, “and dwelt in Jerusalem two years” (Samuel II 14:28) so we have seven years in Solomon’s life. And he [Absalom] rebelled against his father and was killed. After this (Samuel II 21:1) “And there was famine in the days of David three years,” so we have ten. In the eleventh year he counted the Israelites and they scattered in all the land nine months (Samuel II 24:8). In the year of his death he instituted divisions [among the priests and Levites] as it says “In the fortieth year of David’s reign they were sought for” [Chronicles I 26:31, see Rashi there] so we have twelve years in the life of King Solomon.

notes.202: (tn): There is no verb expressed in the Hebrew text; “stands” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.203: (tn, Heb): “your people whom you have chosen.”

notes.204: (tn, Heb): “a hearing heart.” (The Hebrew term translated “heart” often refers to the mental faculties.)
notes.206: (tn, Heb): “to understand between good and evil.”
notes.207: (tn, Heb): “for”; the word “otherwise” is used to reflect the logical sense of the statement.
notes.208: (tn, Heb): “who is able?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “no one.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶת עַמְּךָ הַכָּבֵד.* 
מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהֵם רַבִּים, יֵשׁ לָהֶם עֲסָקִים רַבִּים, וּבָאִים לְדִין, וְאֵין לִי מָתוּן לְעַיֵּן בְּדִינָם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: כִּי מִי יוּכַל לִשְׁפֹּט אֶת עַמְּךָ הַכָּבֵד הַזֶּה, מִשְׁפָּטָם כָּבֵד מְאֹד, אִם יָבֹא דִין שְׁנֵי גוֹיִם לְפָנַי, וְאֶטֹּל מִזֶּה וְאֶתֵּן לָזֶה שֶׁלֹּא כַדִּין, אֵינִי נֶעֱנַשׁ, אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲרֵינִי נֶעֱנַשׁ עָלָיו עֹנֶשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְקָבַע אֶת קֹבְעֵיהֶם נָפֶשׁ.
rashi.eng: *For who is able to judge this Your great people.* Since they are many there are many transactions, and they come to be judged and I have no time to deliberate over their arguments. Another interpretation of “for who is able to judge this your great people” their decisions are very difficult to make. If a lawsuit comes before me and I take from one and give to the other unjustly, I shall be punished for it with capital punishment, as it says “And He takes the lives of those that steal from them” (Proverbs 22:23).

notes.211: (tn): The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here and in v.15 is אֲדֹנָי (’adonay).
notes.212: (tn, Heb): “And the thing was good in the eyes of the Lord, for Solomon asked for this thing.”

notes.213: (tn, Heb): “because you asked for this thing, and did not ask for yourself many days and did not ask for yourself riches and did not ask for the life of your enemies, but you asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment.”

notes.214: (tn): This statement is introduced in the Hebrew text by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) which draws attention to and emphasizes what follows.
notes.215: (tn, Heb): “I am doing according to your words.” The perfect tense is sometimes used of actions occurring at the same time a statement is made.
notes.216: (tn): This statement is introduced by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) which draws attention to and emphasizes what follows. The translation assumes that the perfect tense here indicates that the action occurs as the statement is made (i.e., “right now I give you”).
notes.217: (tn, Heb): “heart.” (The Hebrew term translated “heart” often refers to the mental faculties.)
notes.218: (tn, Heb): “so that there has not been one like you prior to you, and after you one will not arise like you.”

notes.219: (tn): The translation assumes that the perfect tense here indicates that the action occurs as the statement is made.
notes.220: (tn, Heb): “so that there is not one among the kings like you all your days.” The LXX lacks the words “all your days.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאִם תֵּלֵךְ בִּדְרָכַי וְגוֹ' וְהַאֲרַכְתִּי אֶת יָמֶיךָ.* 
הָעשֶׁר וְהַכָּבוֹד שֶׁלֹּא הִתְנֵיתִי בְּתוֹרָתִי לָתֵת לַמֶּלֶךְ, אֶתֵּן לְךָ, בֵּין זַכַּאי בֵּין חַיָּב, אֲבָל אֹרֶךְ הַיָּמִים וּמַלְכוּת הַדּוֹרוֹת, כְּבָר הִתְנֵיתִי בְּתוֹרָתִי: לְבִלְתִּי סוּר מִן הַמִּצְוָה לְמַעַן יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים עַל מַמְלַכְתּוֹ וְגוֹ', וְעַל אוֹתוֹ תְּנַאי לֹא אֶשְׁנֶה, וְאִם תֵּלֵךְ בִּדְרָכַי וְהַאֲרַכְתִּי וְגוֹ', וְכֵן בְּמַלְכוּת דּוֹרוֹתָיו אַחֲרָיו, אָמַר לוֹ: וְאַתָּה אִם תֵּלֵךְ לְפָנַי וְגוֹ' לֹא יִכָּרֵת לְךָ אִישׁ וְגוֹ', כָּךְ שְׁנוּיָה בְּסִפְרֵי. וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר גַּם עשֶׁר גַּם כָּבוֹד וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *And if you walk in My ways… I will lengthen your days.* The riches and the honor for which I imposed no conditions in my Torah to give to the king, I shall grant you whether deserving or not. However, longevity and a hereditary monarchy I already imposed conditions in my Torah “that he shall not turn aside from the commandment that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, etc.” (Deut. 17:20) and that stipulation I shall not alter. “And if you will walk in My ways… then I will lengthen your days.” And likewise concerning the continuation of the monarchy to his descendants after him God said to him “And if you shall go before me… there shall not cease to be from you a man, etc.” (9:4, 5). Thus is it learned in Sifrei (Deut. 17:20) Rabbi Chanina the son of Gamliel says, “Behold he has said also riches also honor, etc.”

notes.226: (tn): Or “tokens of peace”; NIV, TEV “fellowship offerings.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקַץ שְׁלֹמֹה וְהִנֵּה חֲלוֹם.* 
וְהִנֵּה הֵבִין שֶׁחֲלוֹמוֹ אֱמֶת, שׁוֹמֵעַ עוֹף מְצַפְצֵף וּמֵבִין לְשׁוֹנוֹ, כֶּלֶב נוֹבֵחַ וּמֵבִין לְשׁוֹנוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And Solomon awoke, and behold it was a dream.* and behold he understood that his dream was true. He would hear a bird chirp and understand its language, a dog would bark and he would understand its language.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּה.* 
מִשִּׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ, שֶׁהֵבִין שֶׁחֲלוֹמוֹ אֱמֶת.
rashi.eng: *And he came to Jerusalem… and made a feast for all his servants.* out of the gladness of his heart since he understood that his dream was true.

notes.227: (sn): There was no one else in the house except the two of us. In other words, there were no other witnesses to the births who could identify which child belonged to which mother.

notes.231: (tn, Heb): “look, it was not my son to whom I had given birth.”

rashi.heb:
*וָאֶתְבּוֹנֵן אֵלָיו.* 
נָתַתִּי לֵב לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *But when I looked closely at him.* I gave my complete attention to scrutinize him.

notes.232: (tn, Heb): “they spoke before the king.” Another option is to translate, “they argued before the king.”

notes.233: (tn, Heb): “the woman whose son was alive.”
notes.234: (tn, Heb): “for her compassions grew warm for her son.”
notes.235: (tn): The infinitive absolute before the negated jussive emphasizes the main verb.

rashi.heb:
*הִיא אִמּוֹ.* 
בַּת קוֹל הוֹפִיעָה וְאָמְרָה: הִיא אִמּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *She is its mother.* a divine voice which appeared and said ‘She is its mother.’

notes.236: (tn, Heb): “feared,” perhaps in the sense, “stood in awe of.”
notes.238: (tn, Heb): “the wisdom of God within him.”

rashi.heb:
*מֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
מִשֶּׁרָאוּ בְּחָכְמָתוֹ, שָׂמְחוּ כֻּלָּם בְּמַלְכוּתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Was king over all Israel.* For when they saw his wisdom they all rejoiced in his kingdom.

notes.239: (tn, Heb): “were scribes”; NASB, NIV, NRSV “secretaries”; TEV, NLT “court secretaries.”

rashi.heb:
*סֹפְרִים.* 
לִכְתֹּב דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים.
rashi.eng: *Scribes.* to write the chronicles of the king.

rashi.heb:
*הַמַּזְכִּיר.* 
אֵיזֶה מִשְׁפָּט בָּא לְפָנָיו רִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁיִּפְסְקֶנּוּ רִאשׁוֹן, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי.
rashi.eng: *the recorder.* [His duty was to remind the king] which judgment came before him first, that he might decide it first. So I heard.

notes.242: (tn, Heb): “close associate of”; KJV, ASV, NASB “the king’s friend” (a title for an adviser, not just an acquaintance).

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַנִּצָּבִים.* 
שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר נְצִיבִים הָיוּ, לְכַלְכֵּל אֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ וְאֶת בֵּיתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Was over the officers.* He had twelve officers to supply the food of the king and his household.

notes.245: (sn): The work crews. This Hebrew word (מַס, mas) refers to a group of laborers conscripted for royal or public service.

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַמַּס.* 
שֶׁהֶעֱלָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּעַל הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה מַס.
rashi.eng: *Was over the levy.* which Solomon had raised on the Israelites, as it is said, “And king Solomon raised a levy” (below 5:27).

rashi.heb:
*וְכִלְכְּלוּ אֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ.* 
כָּל סְעוּדָתוֹ, וּמַאֲכַל הַסּוּסִים, וְכָל צָרְכֵי הוֹצָאָה.
rashi.eng: *Who provided victuals for the king.* all his meals, and the food of the numerous horses and all the needs of his expenditures.

rashi.heb:
*נָפַת דֹּאר.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) פַּלְכֵי דֹאר.
rashi.eng: *The region of Dor.* Heb. נפתדאר, the region of Dor.

notes.246: (map): For location see Map1-D4; Map2-C1; Map4-C2; Map5-F2; Map7-B1.

rashi.heb:
*חֶבֶל אַרְגֹּב.* 
מְמֻנֶּה הָיָה עֲלֵיהֶם לִגְבּוֹת מַס הַמֶּלֶךְ, כִּי מִשְׁפַּט הַמֶּלֶךְ יֵשׁ לִגְבּוֹת יְצִיאוֹתָיו מִן הָעָם, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמִשְׁפַּט הַמְּלוּכָה בְּסֵפֶר שְׁמוּאֵל.
rashi.eng: *The region of Argob.* He was appointed over them to collect the levy of the king, because the rules of the monarchy dictate that his expenditures should be collected from the people, as it is said in the rules of the monarchy in the book of Samuel I (8:11).

rashi.heb:
*וּנְצִיב אֶחָד אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ.* 
רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל פְּלִיגֵי, חַד אָמַר: אֶחָד מְמֻנֶּה עַל כֻּלָּם, הוּא עֲזַרְיָה בֶּן נָתָן הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה, וְחַד אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד חֹדֶשׁ הָעִבּוּר.
rashi.eng: *And one officer that was in the land.* There is a difference of opinion between Rav and Shmuel. One says, [He was the] one who was appointed over all of them. This was Azariahu the son of Nathan, who was mentioned previously in verse 5, and one says, [To provide the victuals of the king] for the thirteenth month of a Jewish leap year.

notes.247: (sn): Beginning with , the verse numbers through in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with ET = HT, ET = HT, etc., through ET = HT. Beginning with the numbering of verses in the English Bible and the Hebrew text is again the same.
notes.248: (tn, Heb): “the River” (also in v. 24). This is the standard designation for the Euphrates River in biblical Hebrew.
notes.249: (tn, Heb): “[They] were bringing tribute and were serving Solomon all the days of his life.”

notes.250: (tn, Heb): “the food of Solomon for each day was.”
notes.251: (tn): As a unit of dry measure a cor was roughly equivalent to six bushels.

notes.252: (tn): The words “in the stall” are added for clarification; note the immediately following reference to cattle from the pasture.

notes.253: (tn, Heb): “because.” The words “his royal court was so large” are added to facilitate the logical connection with the preceding verse.
notes.254: (sn): Tiphsah. This was located on the Euphrates River.
notes.255: (tn, Heb): “for he was ruling over all [the region] beyond the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kingdoms beyond the River, and he had peace on every side all around.”

notes.256: (tn, Heb): “Judah and Israel lived securely, each one under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beer Sheba, all the days of Solomon.”

notes.257: (tn): The Hebrew text has “40,000,” but this is probably an inflated number (nevertheless it is followed by KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV, TEV, CEV). Some Greek mss of the OT and the parallel in 2 Chr 9:25 read “4,000” (cf. NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT).

notes.258: (tn, Heb): “everyone who drew near to the table of King Solomon.”

notes.259: (tn, Heb): “barley and straw for the horses and the steeds they brought to the place which was there, each according to his measure.”

notes.260: (tn, Heb): “heart,” i.e., mind. (The Hebrew term translated “heart” often refers to the mental faculties.)

notes.261: (tn, Heb): “the wisdom of Solomon was greater than the wisdom of all the sons of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.”

notes.262: (tn, Heb): “his name was in all the surrounding nations.”

notes.267: (sn): The verse numbers in the English Bible differ from those in the Hebrew text (BHS) here; in the English Bible corresponds to in the Hebrew text. See the note at 4:21.
notes.268: (map): For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

notes.270: (tn, Heb): “a house for the name of the Lord.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.
notes.271: (tn, Heb): “because of the battles which surrounded him until the Lord placed them under the soles of his feet.”

rashi.heb:
*בְּרִאִים.* 
פְּטוּמִים עַל הָאֵבוּס.
rashi.eng: *Fat.* Fattened in the stall.

rashi.heb:
*רְעִי.* 
מִן הָאָחוּ.
rashi.eng: *The pastures.* On the grass.

rashi.heb:
*וּבַרְבֻּרִים אֲבוּסִים.* 
יֵשׁ מֵרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אוֹמְרִים: תַּרְנְגוֹלִים פְּטוּמִין (וּכְעֵין זֶה כָּתַב רש"י בב"מ פו ב).
rashi.eng: *And fatted fowl.* There are amongst our Sages those who say these were roosters which were fattened [forcefully].

notes.273: (tn, Heb): “a house for the name of the Lord.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.
notes.274: (tn, Heb): “a house for my name.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

rashi.heb:
*אַרְבָּעִים אֶלֶף אֻרְו‍ֹת סוּסִים.* 
וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים הוּא אוֹמֵר: אַרְבַּעַת אֲלָפִים, פֵּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אַרְבָּעִים אֶלֶף אֻרְווֹת הָיוּ, וּבְכָל אַחַת אַרְבַּע אֶלֶף אִצְטַבְּלָאוֹת. אוֹ אַרְבַּעַת אֲלָפִים אֻרְווֹת, וּבְכָל אַחַת אַרְבָּעִים אֶלֶף אִצְטַבְּלָאוֹת.
rashi.eng: *forty thousand stalls of horses.* In Chron. II 9:25 it says four thousand [stalls of horses whereas here forty thousand are mentioned]. Our Sages explained there were forty thousand stalls and in each there were four thousand partitions, or there were four thousand stalls and in each there were forty thousand partitions.

notes.275: (tn): Or “Blessed be the Lord today, who….”

rashi.heb:
*לֹא יְעַדְּרוּ דָּבָר.* 
אֲפִלּוּ שֶׁל יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
rashi.eng: *They lacked nothing.* Even summer fruits and vegetables, as cucumbers in the winter.

notes.277: (tn, Heb): “I will satisfy all your desire with respect to cedar wood and with respect to the wood of evergreens.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהַשְּׂעֹרִים וְהַתֶּבֶן.* 
הָיוּ נוֹתְנִים אֵלּוּ הַנְּצִיבִים, אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה שָׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *And the barley and the straw.* These officers [were obligated] not only to provide the necessary food but also to deliver it to the place where the king would be.

notes.278: (tn, Heb): “I will place them [on? as?] rafts in the sea to the place where you designate to me.” This may mean he would send them by raft, or that he would tie them in raft-like bundles, and have ships tow them down to an Israelite port.
notes.279: (tn, Heb): “smash them,” i.e., untie the bundles.
notes.280: (tn, Heb): “as for you, you will satisfy my desire by giving food for my house.”

notes.281: (tn, Heb): “and Hiram gave to Solomon cedar wood and the wood of evergreens, all his desire.”

rashi.heb:
*מֵחָכְמַת כָּל בְּנֵי קֶדֶם.* 
מַה הִיא חָכְמַת בְּנֵי קֶדֶם, יוֹדְעִים בְּמַזָּלוֹת וְכוּ' כִּדְאִיתָא בִּפְסִיקְתָּא דְּפָרָה אֲדֻמָּה, וְכָל הַפָּרָשָׁה הַזֹּאת נִדְרֶשֶׁת שָׁם לְפִי מַשְׁמָעָהּ.
rashi.eng: *Was greater than the wisdom of all the children of the east.* What was the wisdom of the children of the east? They were learned in astronomy, as it is stated in the Pesikta of Para Adumah, and all of this chapter is expounded there according to its ordinary sense.

notes.282: (sn): As a unit of dry measure a cor was roughly equivalent to six bushels.
notes.284: (tc): The Hebrew text has “twenty cors,” but the ancient Greek version and the parallel text in 2 Chr 2:10 read “twenty thousand baths.” A bath was a liquid measure equivalent to almost six gallons.
notes.286: (tn, Heb): “and Solomon supplied Hiram with twenty thousand cors of wheat…pure olive oil. So Solomon would give to Hiram year by year.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֶּחְכַּם מִכָּל הָאָדָם.* 
כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And he was wiser than all men.* As its ordinary sense.

rashi.heb:
*אֵיתָן וְהֵימָן וְכַלְכֹּל וְדַרְדַּע.* 
אַחִין הָיוּ, בְּנֵי זֶרַח בֶּן יְהוּדָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וּבְנֵי זֶרַח זִמְרִי וְאֵיתָן (הָיוּ לְוִיִּם מְשׁוֹרְרִים).
rashi.eng: *Ethan, Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda.* They were all brothers, the sons of Zerach the son of Yehuda as it says (Chron. I 2:6), “And the children of Zerach were Zimri and Ethan.”

rashi.heb:
*בְּנֵי מָחוֹל.* 
הָיוּ יוֹדְעִים לְיַסֵּד מִזְמוֹרִים הָאֲמוּרִים בִּמְחוֹלוֹת שִׁיר, שֶׁהָיוּ הַלְוִיִּם אוֹמְרִים עַל דּוּכָנָם מִזְמוֹרִים שֶׁיִּסְּדוּ בְסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים: מַשְׂכִּיל לְאֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי; וּמַשְׂכִּיל לְהֵימָן הָאֶזְרָחִי. מִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה בִּפְסִיקְתָּא: מִכָּל הָאָדָם — זֶה אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן; אֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי — זֶה אַבְרָהָם; הֵימָן — זֶה משֶׁה; וְכַלְכֹּל — זֶה יוֹסֵף; וְדַרְדַּע — זֶה דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר; מָחוֹל — שֶׁנִּמְחַל לָהֶם עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֵגֶל.
rashi.eng: *The sons of Mahol.* They knew how to compose hymns which are said in dancing. They were songs which the Levites said on their platform in the בֵּית הַמִקְדָשׁ, hymns which they composed in the book of Psalms. The Medrash Agada in the Pesikta has another interpretation: הָאָדָם מִכָּל this is a reference to אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן אֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי this is אַבְרָהָם. הֵימָן this is משה, וְכַלְכֹּל this is יוֹסֵף. וְדַרְדַע this is the generation of the wilderness [known as the דור דעה]. מָחוֹל that they were forgiven for the act of the golden calf.

notes.287: (tn, Heb): “a covenant,” referring to a formal peace treaty or alliance.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים מָשָׁל.* 
שְׁלשֶׁת לִמּוּדֵי מְשָׁלוֹת, שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים כָּתוּב 'מִשְׁלֵי שְׁלֹמֹה' בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי.
rashi.eng: *Three thousand proverbs.* Three parabolical studies. It is written three times “The proverbs of Solomon” in the book of Proverbs.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי שִׁירוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה.* 
שְׁלשָׁה אֵלֶּה, וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים, וְקֹהֶלֶת.
rashi.eng: *And his songs were five.* These three, The Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes.

rashi.heb:
*וָאָלֶף.* 
בְּכָל אֶחָד כְּדַי הוּא לִלְמֹד. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר בְּכָל פָּסוּק שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים מָשָׁל, וְעַל כָּל מָשָׁל, אֶלֶף וַחֲמִשָּׁה טְעָמִים.
rashi.eng: *And a thousand.* in each it was worthy of studying. And in the Medrash Aggada [we find Solomon’s great wisdom enabled him] to say three thousand allegories in each sentence of the Torah, and in each of the allegories one thousand and five reasons.

notes.289: (sn): Work crews. This Hebrew word (מַס, mas) refers to a group of laborers conscripted for royal or public service.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְדַבֵּר עַל הָעֵצִים.* 
מָה רְפוּאַת כָּל אֶחָד, וְעֵץ פְּלוֹנִי יָפֶה לְבִנְיָן פְּלוֹנִי, וְלִטַּע בְּקַרְקַע פְּלוֹנִית וְכֵן עַל הַבְּהֵמָה, מָה רְפוּאָתָהּ, וְעִקַּר גִּדּוּלֶיהָ וּמַאֲכָלָהּ. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: מָה רָאָה מְצֹרָע לִטָּהֵר בְּגָבוֹהַּ שֶׁבַּגְּבוֹהִים, וּבְנָמוּךְ שֶׁבַּנְּמוּכִים. וְעַל הַבְּהֵמָה וְעַל הָעוֹף, מָה רָאָה זֶה לִהְיוֹת כָּשֵׁר בִּשְׁחִיטָה בְּסִימָן אֶחָד, וְזֶה בִּשְׁנֵי סִימָנִין, וְדָגִים וַחֲגָבִים בְּלֹא כְלוּם.
rashi.eng: *And he spoke of trees.* which cure is derived from each tree, and that particular wood would be best for that type of building and to plant [a certain tree] in that type of earth. And also of the beasts, what is its cure and the vital elements [necessary] for its upbringing and development and its food. The Midrash Aggada [has another explanation]: Why did God see fit that a ‘metzora’ become clean with the tallest of the tall trees, as the cedar, and the shortest of the short trees? And also of the beasts and the fowl. Why did God see fit that this one, should become permissible by severing one, either the esophagus or the trachea, and this one, the beast, by severing both the esophagus and the trachea, and fish and grasshoppers with neither.

notes.293: (tc): Some Greek mss of the OT read “3,600”; cf. 2 Chr 2:2, 18 and NLT.
notes.294: (tn, Heb): “besides thirty-three hundred from the officials of Solomon’s governors who were over the work, the ones ruling over the people, the ones doing the work.”

rashi.heb:
*לֹא יָכֹל לִבְנוֹת בַּיִת וְגוֹ'.* 
לֹא הָיָה רַשַּׁאי מִפְּנֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה, וְהַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר: וְהֵנִיחַ לָכֶם מִכָּל אֹיְבֵיכֶם מִסָּבִיב, וְאַחַר כָּךְ: וְהָיָה הַמָּקוֹם וְגוֹ' לְשִׁכְנוֹ תִדְרְשׁוּ וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *He could not build a house.* He was not permitted because of the wars, as the Torah states clearly (Deut. 12:10): “And He will give you rest from all your enemies round about” and afterwards, “Then it shall come to pass that the place [which the Lord your God shall choose etc.] even unto His habitation shall you seek etc.”

notes.297: (tn, Heb): “the Gebalites.” The reading is problematic and some emend to a verb form meaning, “set the borders.”
notes.298: (tc): The LXX includes the words “for three years.”

rashi.heb:
*כַּצִּדֹנִים.* 
שְׁכֵנִים לַיַּעַר לְצַד אֶחָד הָיוּ, וּבְמֶמְשַׁלְתּוֹ שֶׁל חִירָם.
rashi.eng: *Like the Zidonians.* The Zidonians were neighboring with the forest of Lebanon on one side and part of the kingdom of Hiram.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשִׂימֵם דֹּבְרוֹת.* 
'רַפְסוֹדוֹת' קוֹרֵא לָהֶם בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים, וּבִלְשׁוֹן אַשְׁכְּנַז פליצי"ן, וּבְלַעַ"ז רי"ץ, קוֹשְׁרִין הָעֵצִים זֶה עִם זֶה, וּמְצִיפִין אוֹתָן עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם, וּמוֹלִיכִין אוֹתָן כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין הַסְּפִינוֹת.
rashi.eng: *I will make them into rafts.* The prophet Ezra calls them רַפְסוֹדוֹת, in Chronicles [II 2:15]. And in German they are called floss, floats, and in old French res, similar to rafts. They would tie the fallen trees together and float them on the water and conduct them as ships are conducted.

rashi.heb:
*עַד הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁלַח אֵלַי.* 
אֲשֶׁר תּוֹדִיעֵנִי לַהֲבִיאָם שָׁם.
rashi.eng: *To the place that you shall send me.* That you shall send a messenger to inform me to bring them. there

rashi.heb:
*וְנִפַּצְתִּים שָׁם.* 
כְּשֶׁמַּתִּיר אוֹגְדָן וּמוֹצִיאָן אֶל הַיַּבָּשָׁה כָּל עֵץ וְעֵץ לְעַצְמוֹ, הִיא קְרוּיָה נִפּוּץ (כָּל דָּבָר שָׁלֵם שֶׁמְּחַלְּקִים אוֹתוֹ לִפְרָקִים, קָרוּי נִפּוּץ), דיפצי"ר בְּלַעַ"ז.
rashi.eng: *And will separate them there.* As their binding is untied and they are taken from the water to the beach, each and every log separately, that is called נִיפּוּץ. Any whole object when it is taken apart, that is called נִיפּוּץ, depced in old French.

rashi.heb:
*מַכֹּלֶת לְבֵיתוֹ.* 
לְשׁוֹן מַאֲכָל.
rashi.eng: *Food for his household.* Heb. מכלת, an expression from the word מַאֲכָל, food.

rashi.heb:
*שֶׁמֶן כָּתִית.* 
שֶׁמֶן נָקִי, שֶׁאֵין זֵיתִים נִטְחָנִים בָּרֵיחַיִם, אֶלָּא כּוֹתֵשׁ בְּמַכְתֶּשֶׁת, וְאֵין מַעֲלֶה שְׁמָרִים כָּל כָּךְ כְּמוֹ הַטָּחוּן.
rashi.eng: *beaten oil.* This oil was pure because the olives were not ground in a mill but rather crushed with a mortar, and this process does not stir up as much dregs as those which are ground.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי הַמַּס.* 
עוֹלֶה לְשָׂכָר שֶׁל שְׁלשִׁים אֶלֶף אִישׁ.
rashi.eng: *And the levy was thirty thousand men.* which amounted to the wages of thirty thousand men.

rashi.heb:
*חֲלִיפוֹת.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּסַיֵּם וְאוֹמֵר: חֹדֶשׁ יִהְיוּ בַלְּבָנוֹן, כְּשֶׁהָיוּ עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים אִישׁ בְּתִשְׁרֵי בַּלְּבָנוֹן, וְהָעֶשְׂרִים אֶלֶף אִישׁ בְּבֵיתוֹ, בְּמַרְחֶשְׁוָן מִתְחַלְּפִים עֲשֶׂרֶת הָאֲלָפִים הַשְּׁנִיִּים וְיוֹצְאִים לִלְבָנוֹן, וְאֵלּוּ חוֹזְרִים לְבֵיתָם, וּבְכִסְלֵו יוֹצְאִים עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים הַשְּׁלִישִׁים וְיוֹצְאִים לִלְבָנוֹן, וְאֵלּוּ חוֹזְרִים לְבֵיתָם, וּבְטֵבֵת יוֹצְאִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים וְחוֹזְרִים לִלְבָנוֹן, וְכֵן חוֹזְרִים חָלִילָה, נִמְצְאוּ כָּל עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים שֶׁבָּהֶם, חֹדֶשׁ בַּלְּבָנוֹן, וּשְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים בְּבֵיתָם.
rashi.eng: *Ten thousand a month alternately.* When the thousand men were in Lebanon in Tishrei and the twenty thousand men were at home, in Marcheshvan the second ten thousand would alternate and go out to Lebanon and these would return to their homes. And in the month of Kislev the third group of ten thousand go out, and they would go out to Lebanon, and these second ones would return to their homes. And in the month of Teveth the first ones go out and return to Lebanon, and thus they return again and again. So it is found that each group of ten thousand amongst them would be one month in Lebanon and two months at home.

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַמַּס.* 
לִגְבּוֹתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And Adoniram was over the levy.* to collect the levy.

rashi.heb:
*שִׁבְעִים אֶלֶף נֹשֵׂא סַבָּל.* 
לְהָבִיא הָאֲבָנִים מִן הָהָר לָעִיר, וּשְׁמוֹנִים אֶלֶף הַחוֹצְבִים אוֹתָם בָּהָר, הֲרֵי מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף, וְכֻלָּם גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים הָיוּ, שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּרוּ מֵחֲמַת גְּדֻלַּת שְׁלֹמֹה וְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ, וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: וַיִּסְפֹּר שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת כָּל הַגֵּרִים וַיִּמְצָאֵם מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף וַיַּעַשׂ מֵהֶם שִׁבְעִים אֶלֶף וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *Seventy thousand that bore burdens.* to bring the stones from the mountains to the city, and the eighty thousand men were the ones who hewed them in the mountains. There is altogether one hundred fifty thousand men. And they were all proselytes who were drawn and attracted to the Jewish people, that converted because of Solomon’s greatness and hospitality. And it is likewise written in Chronicles II (2: 16) “And Solomon numbered all the strangers that were in the land of Israel… and they were found a hundred and fifty thousand. And he set seventy thousand…”

rashi.heb:
*מִשָּׂרֵי הַנִּצָּבִים.* 
נוֹגְשִׂים וּנְצִיבִים עַל עוֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה.
rashi.eng: *The chief officers.* These were the oppressors and overseers over those who did the work.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּשְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת.* 
וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים הוּא אוֹמֵר: וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת, אוֹמֵר אֲנִי, שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּשְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת הָיוּ מְמֻנִּים עַל מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מְמֻנֶּה עַל אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה וְיוֹתֵר, וְהַשְּׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת שֶׁנּוֹסָפִים בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים, הָיוּ מְמֻנִּים עַל כֻּלָּם, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מְמֻנֶּה עַל חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וְיוֹתֵר. וְתֵדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ עוֹד שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים בְּדָבָר זֶה, וּמַכְחִישִׁין זֶה אֶת זֶה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ בְּסֵפֶר זֶה: אֵלֶּה שָׂרֵי הַנִּצָּבִים אֲשֶׁר לִשְׁלֹמֹה חֲמִשִּׁים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת, וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים הוּא אוֹמֵר: מָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים, הֲרֵי אַרְבַּע מִקְרָאוֹת מַכְחִישִׁין זֶה אֶת זֶה. אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָנוּ לְפָרֵשׁ, שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָאוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים מְמֻנִּים עַל כֻּלָּן, וְלִשְׁלֹמֹה הָיוּ אֵלּוּ הַגֵּרִים לִהְיוֹת לְנוֹשֵׂא סַבָּל וְלַחֲצֹב אֲבָנִים בָּהָר, וְיִהְיוּ לוֹ שְׁאָר עוֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה לְעָרֵי הַמִּסְכְּנוֹת, שֶׁהֵם אֶזְרָחִיִּים, שֶׁאֵלּוּ הַכְּתוּבִים אֲמוּרִים שָׁם. וּבְסֵפֶר מְלָכִים מָנָה אֶת הַנְּצִיבִים הַגֵּרִים שְׁנֵי מִנְיָנִים, שָׂרֵי הָאַרְבָּעִים וְהַחֲמִשָּׁה לְבַדָּם, וְהַשְּׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת הַחֲשׁוּבִים צֵרֵף עִם מָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁהָיוּ מְמֻנִּים עַל עוֹשֵׂי עָרֵי הַמִּסְכְּנוֹת, וּמָנָה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים שָׂרִים, וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים מָנָה כָּל נְצִיבֵי הַגֵּרִים לְעַצְמָם, הַגְּדוֹלִים עִם הַקְּטַנִּים שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת, וְכֻלָּן גֵּרִים, וּנְצִיבֵי עָרֵי הַמִּסְכְּנוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים, מָנָה לְעַצְמָן.
rashi.eng: *Three thousand and three hundred.* And in Chronicles II (2:1) it says three thousand and six hundred. It is, therefore, my opinion that the three thousand three hundred men were in charge of one hundred fifty thousand men, so that each one was in charge of forty five and some odd men, and the three hundred men who were added in Chronicles were in charge of all of them, so that each of these three hundred men was in charge of five hundred and some odd men. And you shall know the evidence in support of my opinion that there are two other passages on this subject, and they contradict one another. For it says on this topic in this book of Kings I (9:23) “These were the chief officers that were over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty,” and in the book of Chronicles II (8:10) it says “two hundred and fifty.” There are, therefore, altogether, four verses contradicting one another. But we may explain it thus. Those that are mentioned in the latter verses in I Kings 9:23 and in Chronicles II (8:10), were in charge of all of them. And it is a fact that Solomon had employed these proselytes to be bearers of burdens and to hew stones in the mountains. And, in addition, he had the remaining workers for the store cities which he also built, who were native born Jews. Because these passages are stated there in Chronicles II which discusses the store-cities. And to sum it up then, in the book of Kings he counted the proselyte officers in two separate totals. First, he counted the three thousand three hundred men, the officers who were in charge of forty-five men each, separately. And in (9:23) he combined the three hundred superior officers, who were in charge of these three thousand three hundred men, with the two hundred and fifty men who were in charge of the builders of the store-cities, and totaled together five hundred and fifty officers. And, on the other hand, in Chronicles II he counted all the proselyte officers, the major and minor ones, together, three thousand six hundred men, and they were all proselytes. And the officers in charge of the workers in the store-cities, who were Jews, totaling two hundred and fifty men, he counted separately.

rashi.heb:
*הָרֹדִים בָּעָם הָעֹשִׂים בַּמְּלָאכָה.* 
הַנּוֹגְשִׂים אֶת הָעָם עוֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה.
rashi.eng: *Who bore rule over the people that wrought in the work.* Who bore rule over the people that did the work.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּסִּעוּ.* 
מִן הָהָר, לְשׁוֹן עֲקִירָה.
rashi.eng: *And they quarried.* the stones from the mountains. This is an expression of uprooting.

rashi.heb:
*אֲבָנִים יְקָרוֹת.* 
כְּבֵדוֹת.
rashi.eng: *Great stones, heavy stones.* Heb. יקרות, heavy.

rashi.heb:
*אַבְנֵי גָזִית.* 
נִפְסָלוֹת וּמְסֻתָּתוֹת. וְאִם תֹּאמַר וַהֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: וּמַקָּבוֹת וְהַגַּרְזֶן לֹא נִשְׁמַע בַּבַּיִת בְּהִבָּנוֹתוֹ, פֵּרוּשׁ שֶׁכְּלִי בַּרְזֶל לֹא נִשְׁמַע בַּבַּיִת בְּהִבָּנוֹתוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה מְסַתֵּת מִבַּחוּץ, וּמַכְנִיס וּבוֹנֶה מִבִּפְנִים (סוטה מח ב).
rashi.eng: *Hewn stone.* They were carved and chiseled [precisely to the required measurement]. And if you ask it has already been stated (6:7) “There was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.” How then were the stones cut to a specific size? The explanation is, that although no tool of iron was heard in the house, while it was in building, but he would chisel the stones while still on the outside, and then bring them in and build from the inside. Thus is this explained in the Tractate Sota (48b).

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּפְסְלוּ.* 
בֶּהָרִים.
rashi.eng: *And they did hew them.* in the mountains.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַגִּבְלִים.* 
אֻמָּה שֶׁשְּׁמָהּ גְּבָל, וּבְקִיאִים לְסַתֵּת אֲבָנִים וְלִבְנוֹת, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּצוֹר: זִקְנֵי גְבַל וַחֲכָמֶיהָ הָיוּ בָךְ מַחֲזִיקֵי בִּדְקֵךְ.
rashi.eng: *And the Gebalites.* a nation whose name was Gebal. And they were skilled in the art of chiseling stones and building. As it is stated in reference to the wise men of Tyre (Ezek. 27:9) “The elders of Cebal and the wise men thereof, were in you your calkers.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּכִינוּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן הַזְמָנָה.
rashi.eng: *And they prepared.* An expression of designation.

notes.299: (sn): During the month Ziv. This would be April-May, 966 b.c. by modern reckoning.

rashi.heb:
*בְּחֹדֶשׁ זִו.* 
הוּא אִיָּר, דְּאִית בֵּהּ זִיוָא לְאִילָנָא, וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: זִיו נִיצָנַיָּא.
rashi.eng: *In the month of Ziv.* This is Iyar. The word Ziv means bloom. [It is called Ziv] because [in that month] there is the bloom of the trees. And Targum Jonathan translated this similarly ‘the bloom of the buds.’

rashi.heb:
*הוּא הַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי.* 
לְמִנְיַן הֶחֳדָשִׁים, שֶׁהֲרֵי נִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֶחֳדָשִׁים.
rashi.eng: *Which is the second month.* [Iyar is considered the second month] when numbering the months, since Nissan is the beginning of the year in [the numbering of] the months.

rashi.heb:
*לִמְלֹךְ שְׁלֹמֹה.* 
מוּסַב עַל הַשָּׁנָה הָרְבִיעִית, רְבִיעִית לְמַלְכוּת שְׁלֹמֹה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: וַיָּחֶל לִבְנוֹת בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְמַלְכוּתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Of Solomon’s reign.* “the fourth year.” [It was] the fourth [year] of Solomon’s reign. And so does he also state in Chronicles II (3:2) “And he began to build in the second month in the fourth year of his reign.”

notes.300: (tn, Heb): “sixty cubits.” A cubit was a unit of measure roughly equivalent to 18 inches or 45 cm. Measurements in vv. 2-10 have been converted to feet in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*שִׁשִּׁים אַמָּה.* 
הַהֵיכָל וְהַדְּבִיר יַחַד.
rashi.eng: *Sixty cubits.* [This included] the Temple [proper] and the Holy of Holies together.

rashi.heb:
*וְהָאוּלָם עַל פְּנֵי.* 
לִפְנֵי הַהֵיכָל בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And the porch before.* before the Temple, in it’s entranceway.

rashi.heb:
*אָרְכּוֹ עַל פְּנֵי רֹחַב הַבָּיִת.* 
אֹרֶךְ הָאוּלָם לְרָחְבּוֹ שֶׁל הַהֵיכָל מִן הַצָּפוֹן לַדָּרוֹם. כָּל מִדָּה הַיְתֵרָה קְרוּיָה אֹרֶךְ, וְהַפְּחוּתָה קְרוּיָה רֹחַב, לְפִי שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל מִדַּת מִן הַמִּזְרָח לַמַּעֲרָב יְתֵרָה, קְרוּיָה אֹרֶךְ, וּבָאוּלָם שֶׁמִּדַּת מִצָּפוֹן לַדָּרוֹם יְתֵרָה בּוֹ, קְרוּיָה אֹרֶךְ מִן הַצָּפוֹן לַדָּרוֹם, וּמִן הַמִּזְרָח לַמַּעֲרָב קְרוּיָה בּוֹ רֹחַב.
rashi.eng: *The length thereof before the breadth of the house.* The length of the porch was along the width of the Temple [and extended] from the north to the south. All larger [measurements] are called the length, and the lesser [measurements] are called the width. Since in the Temple proper the measurement from the east to the west was greater, that was called the length, and in the porch that the measurement from the north to the south was the larger, therein was called the length from the north to the south, and from the east to the west therein was called the width.

rashi.heb:
*עַל פְּנֵי הַבָּיִת.* 
לִפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, לְצַד מִזְרָח לְצַד חוּץ.
rashi.eng: *Before the house.* [The porch was] in front of the house [of the Temple], on the eastern side [and was] on the outside.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁקֻפִים אֲטֻמִים.* 
רַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ: שְׁקוּפִים לְשׁוֹן רְאִיָּה וּפְתִיחָה וְהַשְׁקָפָה, פְּתוּחִים מִבַּחוּץ וַאֲטוּמִים מִבִּפְנִים, קְצָרִים מִבִּפְנִים, שֶׁלֹּא כְּדֶרֶךְ שְׁאָר חַלּוֹנוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְמָאוֹר, לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְאוֹרָה.
rashi.eng: *Broad without and narrow within.* Our Sages explained שְּׁקוּפִים as an expression of looking and an opening and an observation. These windows were constructed so that they were open on the outside and closed (אֲטוּמִים) on the inside. [The opening was wider on the outside] and narrow on the inside. This was not in the usual manner of all other windows which are made [expressly] for illumination.

notes.305: (tn, Heb): “and he built on the wall of the temple an extension all around, the walls of the temple all around, for the main hall and for the holy place, and he made side rooms all around.”

rashi.heb:
*יָצִיעַ.* 
אפנטי"ץ בְּלַעַ"ז (יָצִיעַ), וּשְׁלשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת יֵשׁ לָהּ, יָצִיעַ, תָּא, צֶלַע כַּךְ מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּבָּבָא בַּתְרָא.
rashi.eng: *A chamber.* Appentis in French, a projecting gallery. This chamber had three names, יָצִיעַ a wing or extension of the building תָּא, a compartment, צֶלָע a side chamber. Thus is this explained in Baba Bathra 61a.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת קִירוֹת הַבַּיִת סָבִיב.* 
כְּלוֹמַר כְּנֶגֶד הַהֵיכָל וּבֵית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים הוּא הַדְּבִיר, עָשָׂה צְלָעוֹת מִבַּחוּץ, לְדָרוֹם וּלְמַעֲרָב וּלְצָפוֹן, וְסוֹף הַמִּקְרָא הוּא פֵּרוּשׁ לְרֹאשׁוֹ, וַיִּבֶן עַל קִיר הַבַּיִת, סָמוּךְ לְקִיר הַבַּיִת, יָצִיעַ סָבִיב, כֵּיצַד עָשָׂה? אֶת קִירוֹת הַבַּיִת לַהֵיכָל וְלַדְּבִיר, עָשָׂה צְלָעוֹת.
rashi.eng: *Against the walls of the house round about.* That is to say against the Temple and the house of the Holy of Holies, which is [synonymous with] the דְבִיר, he made chambers on the outside at the south, and at the west and the north. And the end of the sentence is an explanation of the beginning. And he built “on” the wall of the house, meaning “near” the wall of the house, a chamber round about. How did he make it? Against the walls of the house, that is, the Temple and the Holy of Holies, he made chambers.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַשׂ.* 
כְּמוֹ עָשָׂה, וְכֵן: וַיְהִי לִי לִישׁוּעָה, כְּמוֹ הָיָה לִי לִישׁוּעָה.
rashi.eng: *He made.* Heb. ויעש, like עשה, “he made.” And likewise, “He was (ויהי) my salvation” (Exodus 15:2), like, “He was (היה) my salvation.”

notes.309: (tn): Or “offsets” (ASV, NAB, NASB, NRSV); NIV “offset ledges.”
notes.310: (tn, Heb): “so that [the beams] would not have a hold in the walls of the temple.”

rashi.heb:
*הַיָּצִיעַ הַתַּחְתֹּנָה.* 
בְּכָל רוּחַ וְרוּחַ הָיוּ הַתָּאִים שְׁלשָׁה זֶה עַל זֶה, וּמִדַּת אָרְכּוֹ לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה כָּאן, וּבְמַסֶּכֶת מִדּוֹת שָׁנִינוּ: שְׁלשִׁים וּשְׁמוֹנָה תָּאִים הָיוּ, חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּצָּפוֹן, חֲמִשָּׁה עַל גַּבֵּי חֲמִשָּׁה, וַחֲמִשָּׁה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, וְכֵן בַּדָּרוֹם, וּשְׁמוֹנָה בַּמַּעֲרָב, שְׁלשָׁה עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁלשָׁה, וּשְׁנַיִם עַל גַּבֵּיהֶם, הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה חָמֵשׁ, וְהָאֶמְצָעוֹת שֵׁשׁ, וְהָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁבַע, לָמָּה? כִּי מִגְרָעוֹת נָתַן לַבַּיִת סָבִיב חוּצָה, קוֹמַת הַתָּא חָמֵשׁ אַמּוֹת, וּכְשֶׁעוֹלֶה כֹּתֶל הַהֵיכָל חָמֵשׁ אַמּוֹת, גּוֹרֵעַ אֶת עָבְיוֹ, וְכִנֵּס בּוֹ אַמָּה לְפָנִים, וְהִנִּיחַ עַל אוֹתָהּ כְּנִיסָה רָאשֵׁי קוֹרוֹת גַּג עֲלִיַּת הַתָּא, שֶׁהִיא קַרְקָעִית לְאֶמְצָעִית, וּכְשֶׁעוֹלֶה עֶשֶׂר, כִּנֵס אַמָּה, לְהַנִּיחַ רָאשֵׁי קוֹרוֹת עֲלִיַּת הָאֶמְצָעִית, שֶׁהִיא קַרְקַע הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, נִמְצֵאת אֶמְצָעִית רְחָבָה מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַמָּה, וְהָעֶלְיוֹנָה רְחָבָה מִן הַתִּיכוֹנָה אַמָּה.
rashi.eng: *The nethermost chamber.* On each side [of the Temple] the chambers were [built in] three [tiers], one on the other. And the measurement of its length is not stated here, [only its width]. And in the Tractate Midoth (4:3) we learned [as follows]: There were thirty-eight chambers [in all], fifteen in the north, five on top of five, and five [more] on top of them, and the same [number] in the south. And eight [more were] in the west, three on top of three and two [more] on top of them. The nethermost [chamber] was five [cubits wide] and the middle ones were six [cubits], and the top ones seven. Why [was this difference]? For he made rebatements in [the wall] of the house round about on the outside. The height of the chamber was five cubits, and as the height of the wall of the Temple [proper] reached five cubits he reduced its thickness and recessed it one cubit inward [on the outside], and on that recess he placed the ends of the beams of the roof at the top of the chamber which served as the floor of the middle one. And as the wall reached ten [cubits] he again recessed it one cubit [in order] to place the ends of the beams of the roof of the middle chamber which served as the floor of the upper chamber. We [thus] find the middle one is broader than the lower one by one cubit, and the upper one is broader than the middle one by one cubit.

rashi.heb:
*לְבִלְתִּי אֲחֹז בְּקִירוֹת הַבָּיִת.* 
שֶׁלֹּא לְדַבֵּק רָאשֵׁי הַקּוֹרוֹת דֶּרֶךְ נְקָבִים בְּקִירוֹת הַבַּיִת, שֶׁקִּלְקוּל הַחוֹמָה הוּא, וְאֵינוֹ דֶּרֶךְ נוֹי.
rashi.eng: *That the beams should not have hold in the walls of the house.* In order not to join the ends of the beams to the walls through perforations in the walls of the house, since this causes the deterioration of the wall and is [also] not beautiful, architecturally.

notes.311: (tn, Heb): “finished stone of the quarry,” i.e., stones chiseled and shaped at the time they were taken out of the quarry.

rashi.heb:
*בְּהִבָּנֹתוֹ אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה מַסָּע.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִסִּיעוּהָ מִן הָהָר עַל יְדֵי הַשָּׁמִיר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה מִשָּׁם, נְתָנוּהָ בְּחוֹמַת הַבִּנְיָן, וְלֹא סִתְּתוּהָ בִּכְלֵי בַרְזֶל, וְאַבְנֵי גָזִית הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה, מַחֲלֹקֶת הִיא בְּסוֹטָה (מח ב).
rashi.eng: *When it was in building, of stone finished at the quarry.* as it was removed from the mountain, through the worm שָּׁמִיר [which cuts through stones]. Exactly as it came from there, they set it into the wall of the structure, and they did not chisel it further with any metal tools. And the hewn stones which are mentioned above [in 5:31, indicating that the stones were cut to some degree], is a controversy discussed in the Tractate Sota (48b).

rashi.heb:
*וּמַקָּבוֹת.* 
דלוט"א בִּלְשׁוֹן רוּסְיָא (פַּטִּישׁ).
rashi.eng: *And hammers.* Delutta, a chisel, in the Russian language.

notes.312: (tc): The Hebrew text has “middle,” but the remainder of the verse suggests this is an error.
notes.313: (tn, Heb): “by stairs they went up.” The word translated “stairs” occurs only here. Other options are “trapdoors” or “ladders.”
notes.314: (tc): The translation reads with a few medieval Hebrew mss, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate הַשְּׁלִשִׁית (hash�lishit, “the third”) rather than MT הַשְּׁלִשִׁים (hash�lishim, “the thirty”).

rashi.heb:
*פֶּתַח הַצֵּלָע הַתִּיכֹנָה אֶל כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת הַיְמָנִית.* 
יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם תִּיכוֹנָה זוֹ כְּמוֹ תַּחְתּוֹנָה, לֹא תִּיכוֹנָה בֵּין עֶלְיוֹנָה לַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, שֶׁבְּחָמֵשׁ תָּאִים שֶׁבַּדָּרוֹם הָיָה לָהּ פֶּתַח אֶל הַחוּץ בַּשּׁוּרָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, וְזֶה (הַתַּרְגּוּם) ּובְלוּלִים יַעֲלוּ עַל הַתִּיכוֹנָה הַתִּיכֹנָה תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: מְצִיעָתָא, כִּי הַתָּאִים הַלָּלוּ לֹא הָיוּ פְּתוּחִים אֶל הַחוּץ. שְׁלשָׁה פְּתָחִים הָיוּ לְכָל אֶחָד, כָּךְ הִיא שְׁנוּיָה בְּמַסֶּכֶת מִדּוֹת (שָׁם), אֶחָד לַתָּא מִן הַיָּמִין, וְאֶחָד לַתָּא מִן הַשְּׂמֹאל, וְאֶחָד לַתָּא שֶׁעַל גַּבָּיו. וְלִמֵּד כָּאן, שֶׁאֶחָד מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים שֶׁבְּכֹתֶל דְּרוֹמִי, הָיָה לוֹ פֶּתַח אֶל הַחוּץ, וְדֶרֶךְ אוֹתוֹ פֶּתַח נִכְנָסִים לְכֻלָּם, 'וְצֵלָע הַתִּיכוֹנָה' דִּקְרָא, לֹא תִּיכוֹנָה בֵּין עֶלְיוֹנָה לַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, אֶלָּא תִּיכוֹנָה שֶׁבְּחָמֵשׁ תָּאִים שֶׁבַּדָּרוֹם הָיָה לָהּ פֶּתַח אֶל הַחוּץ בַּשּׁוּרָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, וְזֶהוּ תַּרְגּוּם 'וּבְלוּלִּים יַעֲלוּ עַל הַתִּיכוֹנָה', שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה הֵימֶנָּה, מַשְׁמָע דְהַצֶּלַע הַתִּיכוֹנָה לְמַטָּה.
rashi.eng: *The door of the lowest chamber was in the right side of the house.* Jonathan rendered this word תִּיכוֹנָה as “the lowest,” not תִּיכוֹנָה [which is] between the upper and lower ones [as is usually translated]. Because the five chambers on the southern side had one opening to the outside which was in the lowest story. And this [second usage of the word תִּיכוֹנָה in this same verse] “and with winding stairs they went up into the middle (תִּיכוֹנָה) chamber,” Jonathan rendered תִּיכוֹנָה; “the middle” because these chambers were not opened to the outside. There were three openings to each [of the chambers].
