And it had four undersetters in its four corners, and this is what the verse said, (7:34) “and there were four undersetters at etc. of each base, the undersetters were of the base itself,” because the lower part of the laver was slanting at the bottom so that it should fit into the כֵּן and in order that it should not fall into it more than the desired amount, therefore these undersetters were made, to carry and support it. This ends the quotation of ‘The Temple Structure.’

notes.422: (tn, Heb): “forty baths” (a bath was a liquid measure roughly equivalent to six gallons).
notes.423: (tn, Heb): “four cubits, each basin.” It is unclear which dimension is being measured.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַשׂ עֲשָׂרָה כִיֹּרוֹת.* 
כְּתִיב בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָמִים: אֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֹלָה יָדִיחוּ בָם.
rashi.eng: *And he made ten lavers.* It is written in Chron. II (4:6) “such things as belonged to the burnt offering they washed in them.”

rashi.heb:
*עַל כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת.* 
כְּנֶגֶד כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת הַיְמָנִית.
rashi.eng: *On the side of the house.* Against the right side of the house.

rashi.heb:
*מִכֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת הַיְמָנִית.* 
מָשׁוּךְ מִצַּד דָּרוֹם לְצַד צָפוֹן, וְזֶה קֵדְמָה מוּל נֶגֶב, מִקְצוֹעַ מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית, כְּנֶגֶד הָאֲוִיר שֶׁבֵּין כֹּתֶל צְפוֹנִי שֶׁל בַּיִת לְצַד כֹּתֶל הָעֲזָרָה, וְצַד צְפוֹנִי קָרוּי מִמּוּל נֶגֶב, מָשׁוּךְ וּמְרֻחָק מִן הַדָּרוֹם, וְאֵין 'מוּל' וּ'מִמּוּל' שָׁוִין בְּפִתָּרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *On the right side of the house.* It [was in the southeast corner,] extended [along the eastern wall,] from the south side toward the north side. And the following is: קֵדְמָה מוּל נֶגֶב, the northeast corner against the space which is between the northern wall of the house and the wall of the court. And the northern wall [alone,] is called מִמוּל נֶגֶב, extended and removed far away from the south, and מוּל and מִמוּל are not translated the same.

notes.424: (tn, Heb): “Hiram.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.425: (tn, Heb): “Hiram finished doing all the work which he did for King Solomon [on] the house of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַשׂ חִירוֹם וְגוֹ'.* 
וְאָמַר רַבִּי, הַכִּירוֹת הֵן הֵן סִירוֹת, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר: כְּכִיּוֹר אֵשׁ בְּעֵצִים; וְכֵן: וְהִכָּה בַכִּיּוֹר.
rashi.eng: *And Hiram made etc..* And Rebbi said, the כִּיוֹרוֹת and the סִירוֹת (7:15) are one and the same, [meaning pots or pans,] as we read in the Scriptures, “like a pan of fire among wood” (Zecharia 12:6) and likewise “and he struck it into the pan” (Samuel I 2:14).

rashi.heb:
*הַכִּיֹּרוֹת.* 
שֶׁל נְחשֶׁת, לְדַשֵּׁן אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
rashi.eng: *The lavers.* They were of copper, [and were used] to remove the ashes therein from the altar.

rashi.heb:
*הַיָּעִים.* 
מַגְרֵפוֹת שֶׁל נְחשֶׁת, שֶׁקּוֹרִין ווידו"ל (יָעֶה, מַגְרֵפָה) בְּאַשְׁכְּנַז, לַחֲתוֹת בָּהֶן דֶּשֶׁן בְּתוֹךְ הַסִּירוֹת.
rashi.eng: *The shovels.* copper shovels which they call, vedil and shauffel in Germany. They were used to rake the ashes with them into the pots.

notes.426: (tn): The words “he made” are added for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁנֵי טוּרִים רִמּוֹנִים.* 
מֵאָה רִמּוֹנִים בְּטוּר, חֲרוּזִים בְּשַׁרְשְׁרוֹת.
rashi.eng: *Two rows of pomegranates.* [There were] one hundred pomegranates in each row hanging by chains.

notes.428: (tn, Heb): “which Hiram made for King Solomon [for] the house of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*יְצָקָם.* 
הִתִּיכָם וְהִצִּיקָם כְּתַבְנִיתָם.
rashi.eng: *Did the king cast them.* He melted them and poured them according to their form.

rashi.heb:
*בְּמַעֲבֵה הָאֲדָמָה.* 
תַּרְגּוּם: בְּעוֹבֵי גַּרְגִּשְׁתָּא.
rashi.eng: *In the thick clay.* [As the Targum renders:] בְּעוֹבֵי גִרְגַשְׁתָּא in the thickness of the clay.

notes.430: (tn, Heb): “Solomon left all the items, due to their very great abundance; the weight of the bronze was not sought.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּנַּח שְׁלֹמֹה.* 
מִלִּשְׁקֹל אֶת מִשְׁקַל הַכֵּלִים הָאֵלֶּה מֵרֹב מְאֹד וְחָדַל לִסְפֹּר מִשְׁקָלָם.
rashi.eng: *And Solomon left.* He refrained from weighing the weight of these vessels because there were very many, and [therefore] ceased to count their weight.

notes.431: (tn, Heb): “the bread of the face [or presence].” Many recent English versions employ “the bread of the Presence,” although this does not convey much to the modern reader. This bread was viewed as a perpetual offering to God and was regarded as holy. See Lev 24:5-9.

rashi.heb:
*חָמֵשׁ מִיָּמִין וְחָמֵשׁ מִשְּׂמֹאל.* 
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר חָמֵשׁ מִימִין הַפֶּתַח וְחָמֵשׁ מִשְּׂמֹאל הַפֶּתַח, אִם כֵּן מָצִינוּ מְנוֹרָה בַּצָּפוֹן, וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: עַל יֶרֶךְ הַמִּשְׁכָּן תֵּימָנָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁל משֶׁה בָּאֶמְצַע, חָמֵשׁ מִימִינָהּ, וְחָמֵשׁ מִשְּׂמֹאלָהּ.
rashi.eng: *Five on the right side and five on the left.* It is impossible to say [these] five were on the right side of the entrance and [the other] five were on the left of the entrance, for if so, we will find a candlestick on the north side and the Torah states, [specifically, the candlestick should be] on the south side of the tabernacle. Therefore, Moses’ [candlestick] was in the middle, five on its right [side] and five on its left.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַפֶּרַח.* 
שֶׁל מְנוֹרָה.
rashi.eng: *And the flowers.* Of the candlestick.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַנֵּרֹת.* 
בָּזִיכִין שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין בָּהֶן הַשֶּׁמֶן וְהַפְּתִילָה.
rashi.eng: *And the lamps.* [These are] the cups into which the oil and wicks are put.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמֶּלְקָחַיִם.* 
שֶׁמְּרִימִים בָּהֶן אֶת הַפְּתִילָה מִתּוֹךְ הַשֶּׁמֶן.
rashi.eng: *And the tongs.* With which the wick is lifted out of the oil.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַסִּפּוֹת.* 
כְּלִי שֶׁל מִינֵי זֶמֶר הוּא, וְכֵן מְזַמְּרוֹת.
rashi.eng: *And the bowls.* some type of musical instruments, and similarly, מְזַמְרוֹת [means musical instruments].

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמִּזְרָקוֹת.* 
לְקַבֵּל דָּם.
rashi.eng: *And the basins.* To receive the blood.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַכַּפּוֹת.* 
לְבָזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה.
rashi.eng: *And the spoons.* [To serve] as the vessels for frankincense.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמַּחְתּוֹת.* 
לַחֲתוֹת בָּהֶן תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְגֶחָלִים לְהוֹלִיךְ מִמִּזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן לַמִּזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי לְהַקְטִיר קְטֹרֶת.
rashi.eng: *And the censers.* [These were more in the form of a shovel or rake] to remove the ashes [from the altar], and [to rake] the coals and carry them from the outer altar, the מִזְבֵּח ַהַנְחוֹשֶׁת [in the court of the priests,] to the inner altar, the מִזְבֵּח ַהַזָהָב [in the temple, in order] to burn incense.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַפֹּתוֹת.* 
מַפְתְּחוֹת, שָׁמַעְתִּי. שֶׁמְּפַתְּחִין בָּהֶם אֶת הַמַּנְעוּל.
rashi.eng: *And the hinges.* [These were] keys, I heard [that these were used] to open with them the locks [of the temple].

rashi.heb:
*לְדַלְתוֹת הַבַּיִת.* 
שֶׁהוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים.
rashi.eng: *For the doors of the inner house.* Which is the most Holy of Holies [only the hinges were of gold, whereas the doors were of wood overlaid with gold].

rashi.heb:
*לְדַלְתֵי הַבַּיִת.* 
שֶׁהוּא לַהֵיכָל, כָּל פִּתְחוֹתֵיהֶן הָיוּ זָהָב.
rashi.eng: *For the doors of the house.* which is for the temple, all of their entrances were of gold.

notes.432: (tn, Heb): “Solomon.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת קָדְשֵׁי דָּוִד אָבִיו.* 
מַה שֶּׁנִּשְׁאַר מִכֶּסֶף וְזָהָב שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ אָבִיו. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה שְׁלֹמֹה לָתֵת מֵאוֹתוֹ הֶקְדֵּשׁ לְבִנְיַן הַבַּיִת. וְשָׁמַעְתִּי מֵחַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִין: לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לֵחָרֵב, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים אוֹמְרִים, קָשָׁה יִרְאָתָם, שֶׁלָּקְחוּ נִקְמָתָם מִן הַבַּיִת, שֶׁנִּבְנָה מִן גְּזֵלוֹת וַחֲבָלוֹת שֶׁגָּזַל מֵהֶם דָּוִד. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כָּךְ אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה, רָעָב הָיָה בִּימֵי אָבִיו שָׁלשׁ שָׁנִים, שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה, וְהָיָה לוֹ לְבַזְבֵּז הַהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת הַלָּלוּ, לְהַחֲיוֹת בָּהֶן עֲנִיֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
rashi.eng: *The things which David his father had dedicated.* That which remained of the silver and gold dedicated by his father [he put into the treasuries of the house of the Lord]. But the Midrash explains that Solomon did not wish to use any of those dedicated materials for the construction of the house. And I heard from scholars of Israel who said [the reason was] because David knew [through prophetic inspiration] that eventually it would be destroyed. [David himself, therefore, begged that his materials should not be used,] so that the idol worshipping nations should not be able to say their idols are mightier for they took their revenge upon the house which was built of the [vast] plunder and destruction which David plundered from them. And others say [that the reason for his refusal was because] Solomon said thus; there was a famine in the days of his father for three consecutive years, and he should have squandered these dedicated materials to sustain therewith the poor people of Israel.

notes.433: (tc): The Old Greek translation includes the following words at the beginning of ch. 8: “It so happened that when Solomon finished building the Lord’s temple and his own house, after twenty years.”
notes.434: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.435: (tn, Heb): “Then Solomon convened the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, the chiefs of the fathers belonging to the sons of Israel to King Solomon [in] Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David (it is Zion).”

rashi.heb:
*נְשִׂיאֵי הָאָבוֹת לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
שֶׁל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
rashi.eng: *The princes of the fathers’ houses of the children of Israel.* [Literally, to the children of Israel, but translated] of the children of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*מֵעִיר דָּוִד.* 
שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ שָׁם דָּוִד כְּשֶׁהֱבִיאוֹ מִבֵּית עוֹבֵד אֱדוֹם.
rashi.eng: *Out of the city of David.* David had placed it there when he brought it [back] from the house of Obed-edom (Samuel II 6:12).

notes.436: (sn): The festival. This was the Feast of Tabernacles, see Lev 23:34.
notes.437: (sn): The month Ethanim. This would be September-October in modern reckoning.

rashi.heb:
*בְּיֶרַח הָאֵתָנִים.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: בְּיַרְחָא דְּעַתִּיקַיָּא דְּקָרַן לֵהּ יַרְחָא קַדְמָאָה בְּחַגָּא וּכְעָן הוּא יַרְחָא שְׁבִיעָאָה, מִשֶּׁנִּתְּנָה תוֹרָה וּכְתִיב בְּנִיסָן שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים, נִקְרָא תִּשְׁרֵי שְׁבִיעִי.
rashi.eng: *In the Month Ethanim.* Jonathan rendered [these words] בְּיֶרַח הָאֵיתָנִים בֶּחָג as follows: ‘In the month which the ancients called the first month, on the festival, and at present it is the seventh month,’ i.e., since the Torah was given, and it is written in reference to the month of נִיסָן that it is the first of the months, so תִּשְׁרֵי will then be called the seventh [month].

notes.438: (tn, Heb): “the tent of assembly.” The tent of meeting. See Exod 33:7-11.
notes.439: (tn, Heb): “and they carried the ark of the Lord…. The priests and the Levites carried them.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד.* 
שֶׁעָשָׂה משֶׁה, וּגְנָזוֹ שְׁלֹמֹה מִשֶּׁנִּבְנָה בַּיִת רִאשׁוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ בְּתוֹסֶפְתָּא דְּסוֹטָה (יג א).
rashi.eng: *And the tabernacle of meeting.* Which Moses made [in the desert, and was in Gibeon until now], And Solomon stored this away as soon as the first temple was built, [in the upper story which was above the temple and the Sanctuary,] as we have learned in the Tosefta of the tractate Sota (13:1).

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר בָּאֹהֶל.* 
אֲשֶׁר נָטָה דָּוִד לָאָרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *Which were in the tabernacle.* which David pitched for the ark.

notes.440: (tn, Heb): “And King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel, those who had been gathered to him, [were] before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle which could not be counted or numbered because of the abundance.”

notes.441: (tn): The word “assigned” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*כַּנְפֵי הַכְּרוּבִים.* 
אוֹתָן שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה הָעוֹמְדִים עַל רַגְלֵיהֶם בַּקַּרְקַע, וְאֵין אֵלּוּ כְּרוּבִים שֶׁל כַּפֹּרֶת שֶׁעַל הָאָרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *Under the wings of the cherubim.* Those which Solomon made, which are standing on their feet on the ground [and facing the temple.] And these are not the cherubim of the cover which was on the ark.

notes.442: (sn): And its poles. These poles were used to carry the ark. See Exod 25:13-15.

rashi.heb:
*אֶל מְקוֹם הָאָרוֹן.* 
מִקִּיר אֶל קִיר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה בָּעִנְיָן.
rashi.eng: *Over the place of the ark.* [Their wings were spread] from wall to wall as he said above on this subject (6:27).

notes.443: (tn, Heb): “they could not be seen outside.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֵּרָאוּ רָאשֵׁי הַבַּדִּים.* 
בַּפָּרֹכֶת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַפֶּתַח בָּאַמָּה טְרַקְסִין, יָכוֹל יִהְיוּ מְקָרְעִין בָּהּ וְיוֹצְאִין, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְלֹא יֵרָאוּ הַחוּצָה, הָא כֵּיצַד, דּוֹחֲקִין וּבוֹלְטִין כְּעֵין שְׁנֵי דַּדֵּי אִשָּׁה, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בֵּין שָׁדַי יָלִין.
rashi.eng: *The ends of the staves were seen.* In the curtain which was against the entrance [of the sanctuary in the אמה טרקסין. You might think they tore through the curtain and protruded [on the other side]. The text, therefore, states “and they were not seen without.” How is this possible? They were pushing and bulging similar to two breasts of a woman, as it says, “he lies between my breasts” (Song of Songs 1:13).

notes.444: (sn): Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai.

rashi.heb:
*בְּצֵאת הַכֹּהֲנִים מִן הַקֹּדֶשׁ.* 
הַכֹּהֲנִים שֶׁנָּשְׂאוּ הָאָרוֹן בַּדְּבִיר, כְּשֶׁיָּצְאוּ שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בַּהֵיכָל.
rashi.eng: *When the priests came out of the holy place.* When the priests who carried the ark into the Sanctuary were leaving, the Divine presence immediately came to rest there.

notes.446: (tn, Heb): “were not able to stand to serve.”

rashi.heb:
*אָז אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה.* 
כְּשֶׁרָאָה הֶעָנָן, אָמַר: עַתָּה רוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה בַּבַּיִת שֶׁבָּנִיתִי, שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּךְ הִבְטִיחַ לָבֹא וְלִשְׁכֹּן בּוֹ מִתּוֹךְ עָנָן וַעֲרָפֶל, וְהֵיכָן אָמַר: כִּי בֶּעָנָן אֵרָאֶה עַל הַכַּפֹּרֶת, כָּךְ שְׁנוּיָה בַּסִּפְרִי.
rashi.eng: *Then.* When he saw the cloud, he said, Now I see that the Divine presence is in the house which I built, for thus did He promise to come and dwell in it from the midst of a cloud and thick darkness. And where did he say this promise? “For in the cloud will I appear upon the ark-cover” (Lev. 16:12). Thus is this taught in the Sifrei.

notes.448: (tn): The words “O Lord” do not appear in the original text, but they are supplied for clarification; Solomon addresses the Lord in prayer at this point.

rashi.heb:
*לְשִׁבְתְּךָ עוֹלָמִים.* 
שֶׁמִּשֶּׁנִּבְחֲרָה, לֹא הֻתָּרוּ הַבָּמוֹת, וְלֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
rashi.eng: *For You to dwell in forever.* And from the time that this [place] was chosen, it would no longer be permissible [to offer sacrifices] on any strange altars, [except those in the temple,] and the Divine presence no longer dwelled in any other place.

notes.450: (tn, Heb): “and he blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.”

notes.451: (tn): The Hebrew text reads, “by his hand.”
notes.452: (tn): The Hebrew text reads, “by his mouth.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר בְּפִיו.* 
שֶׁיִּתֵּן לוֹ בֵּן שֶׁיִּבְנֶה בַּיִת.
rashi.eng: *Who spoke with His mouth.* [He also told him] that he would grant him a son who would build the temple.

rashi.heb:
*וּבְיָדוֹ מִלֵּא.* 
קִיֵּם אֶת דְּבָרוֹ בְּיָדוֹ הַטּוֹבָה.
rashi.eng: *And has fulfilled it with His hand.* He has fulfilled His word with His good power, lit. with His good hand.

notes.454: (tn, Heb): “to build a house for my name to be there.” To build a temple in which to live ( “to build a house for my name to be there”). In the OT, the word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

rashi.heb:
*מִן הַיּוֹם וְגוֹ'.* 
אֶת זֶה דִּבֵּר אֶל דָּוִד אָבִי.
rashi.eng: *… Since the day, etc..* This is what He spoke to my father David.

notes.455: (tn, Heb): “and it was with the heart of David my father.”
notes.456: (tn, Heb): “to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.” The word “name” in the OT sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

notes.457: (tn, Heb): “Because it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.”

notes.458: (tn, Heb): “your son, the one who came out of your body, he will build the temple for my name.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעֲמֹד שְׁלֹמֹה לִפְנֵי מִזְבַּח ה'.* 
כְּתִיב: כִּי עָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה כִּיּוֹר נְחשֶׁת וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ בְּתוֹךְ הָעֲזָרָה וְגוֹ', וַיַּעֲמֹד עָלָיו וַיִּבְרַךְ עַל בִּרְכָּיו.
rashi.eng: *And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord.* [He was not always standing upright but kneeling, nor was he on the ground but on the laver, as] it is written in (Chronicles II 6:13): “for Solomon had made a copper laver, [of five cubits long, and five cubits broad,] and three cubits high, and had set it in the midst of the court, and upon it he stood, and kneeled down upon his knees [in the presence of all the congregation of Israel].”

notes.464: (tn, Heb): “one who keeps the covenant and the loyal love.” The expression is a hendiadys.
notes.465: (tn, Heb): “who walk before you with all their heart.”

rashi.heb:
*שֹׁמֵר הַבְּרִית.* 
מַמְתִּין וְגוֹנֵז לִשְׁמֹר הַבְּרִית וְהַחֶסֶד, לְקַיֵּם הַבְטָחָתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Who keeps covenant.* He waits and stores away [the reward], to keep the covenant, and [which was based on] mercy, to fulfill His promise.

notes.466: (tn, Heb): “[you] who kept to your servant David my father that which you spoke to him.”
notes.467: (tn, Heb): “you spoke by your mouth and by your hand you fulfilled, as this day.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַרְתָּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן אֲמָנַת הַבְטָחָה.
rashi.eng: *Who has kept.* שָּׁמַרְתִּי is an expression meaning fulfilling a promise [a reference to the promise that Solomon would build the temple].

notes.468: (tn, Heb): “there will not be cut off from you a man from before me sitting on the throne of Israel.”
notes.469: (tn, Heb): “guard their way by walking before me as you have walked before me.”

notes.472: (tn, Heb): “Indeed, can God really live on the earth?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course not,” the force of which the translation above seeks to reflect.

rashi.heb:
*הַאֻמְנָם.* 
לְשׁוֹן תֵּימָהּ.
rashi.eng: *… will… indeed…?.* Heb. האמנם, This is an expression of wonder.

rashi.heb:
*לֹא יְכַלְכְּלוּךָ.* 
לֹא יְכִילוּךָ.
rashi.eng: *cannot contain You.* Heb. יְכַלְכְּלוּךָ [the root is יכול, to contain].

notes.475: (tn, Heb): “the loud cry and the prayer.”

notes.477: (tn, Heb): “so your eyes might be open toward this house night and day, toward the place about which you said, ‘My name will be there.’”
notes.478: (tn, Heb): “by listening to the prayer which your servant is praying concerning this place.”

notes.479: (tn, Heb): “listen to the request of your servant and your people Israel which they are praying concerning this place.”
notes.480: (tn, Heb): “and you, hear inside your dwelling place, inside heaven.” The precise nuance of the preposition אֶל (’el), used here with the verb “hear,” is unclear. One expects the preposition “from,” which appears in the parallel text in 2 Chr 6:21. The nuance “inside; among” is attested for אֶל (see Gen 23:19; 1 Sam 10:22; Jer 4:3), but in each case a verb of motion is employed with the preposition, unlike 1 Kgs 8:30. The translation above (“from inside”) is based on the demands of the immediate context rather than attested usage elsewhere.

notes.482: (tn, Heb): “and forgive the man who sins against his neighbor when one takes up against him a curse to curse him and the curse comes before your altar in this house.” In the Hebrew text the words “and forgive” conclude v. 30, but the accusative sign at the beginning of v. 31 suggests the verb actually goes with what follows in v. 31. The parallel text in 2 Chr 6:22 begins with “and if,” rather than the accusative sign. In this case “forgive” must be taken with what precedes, and v. 31 must be taken as the protasis (“if” clause) of a conditional sentence, with v. 32 being the apodosis (“then” clause) that completes the sentence. Be willing to forgive the accused if the accusation is false. At first it appears that Solomon is asking God to forgive the guilty party. But in v. 32 Solomon asks the Lord to discern who is guilty and innocent, so v. 31 must refer to a situation where an accusation has been made, but not yet proven. The very periphrastic translation reflects this interpretation.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר יֶחֶטָא אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ.* 
בּוֹעֵל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
rashi.eng: *If a man sins against his neighbor.* One who is intimate with a married woman.

rashi.heb:
*וְנָשָׁא בוֹ אָלָה.* 
כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתָהּ, כָּךְ הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *and an oath be exacted of him.* curse [rather than oath]. Just as the water inspects her, so does the water inspect him.

rashi.heb:
*וְנָשָׁא בוֹ.* 
לְשׁוֹן נוֹשֶׁה.
rashi.eng: *shall be exacted of him.* Heb. ונשא בו, an expression of נוֹשֶׁה, a creditor.

rashi.heb:
*וּבָא אָלָה לִפְנֵי מִזְבַּחֲךָ.* 
וְהֶעֱמִיד הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי ה'.
rashi.eng: *and he come and swear before your altar.* As it says, “And the priest shall stand the woman before the Lord” (Num. 5:10).

notes.483: (tn, Heb): “and you, hear [from] heaven and act and judge your servants by declaring the guilty to be guilty, to give his way on his head, and to declare the innocent to be innocent, to give to him according to his innocence.”

rashi.heb:
*לָתֵת דַּרְכּוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ.* 
וְצָבְתָה בִטְנָהּ וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *To bring his way upon his head.* “And her belly shall swell, etc.” (ibid. 27).

rashi.heb:
*וּלְהַצְדִּיק צַדִּיק.* 
וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע, כָּךְ נִדְרַשׁ בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא דְּסוֹטָה.
rashi.eng: *And justifying the righteous.* [By rewarding those who deserve it, as it says,] “Then she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed” (ibid. 28). Thus is this explained in the Tosefta of the Tractate Sota (Chap. 1:3).

notes.484: (tn, Heb): “when.” In the Hebrew text vv. 33-34 actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
notes.485: (tn): Or “are struck down before an enemy.”
notes.487: (tn, Heb): “and they pray and ask for help.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהוֹדוּ אֶת שְׁמֶךָ.* 
שֶׁחַיָּב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה.
rashi.eng: *And praise Your name.* For our Sages said that a person is obliged to bless God for the bad as well as the good.

notes.488: (tn, Heb): “when.” In the Hebrew text vv. 35-36a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided into two sentences for stylistic reasons.
notes.489: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (your people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.491: (tn): The Hebrew text has “because you answer them,” as if the verb is from עָנָה (’anah, “to answer”). However, this reference to a divine answer is premature, since the next verse asks for God to intervene in mercy. It is better to revocalize the consonantal text as תְעַנֵּם (t�’annem, “you afflict them”), a Piel verb form from the homonym עָנָה (“to afflict”).

rashi.heb:
*כִּי תַעֲנֵם.* 
לְמַעַן תַּעֲנֵם, 'כִּי' מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְשׁוֹן 'אֲשֶׁר'.
rashi.eng: *so that You may answer them.* The word כי here is used in the context of אשר, “so that.”

notes.492: (tn): The translation understands כִּי (ki) in an emphatic or asseverative sense.
notes.493: (tn, Heb): “the good way in which they should walk.”

notes.495: (tn): Actually two Hebrew terms appear here, both of which are usually taken as referring to locusts. Perhaps different stages of growth or different varieties are in view.

rashi.heb:
*יֵרָקוֹן.* 
שֶׁהַתְּבוּאָה אֵינָהּ עוֹלָה בַּקָּנֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת שִׁבֹּלֶת.
rashi.eng: *yellowing.* Heb. ירקון, when the wheat does not grow up on the stalk to make an ear [on top].

notes.497: (tn, Heb): “every prayer, every request for help which will be to all the people, to all your people Israel.”
notes.498: (tn, Heb): “which they know, each the pain of his heart.”

notes.499: (tn): The words “their sin” are added for clarification.
notes.500: (tn, Heb): “and act and give to each one according to all his ways because you know his heart.” In the Hebrew text vv. 37-39a actually contain one lengthy conditional sentence, which the translation has divided up for stylistic reasons.
notes.501: (tn, Heb): “Indeed you know, you alone, the heart of all the sons of mankind.”

notes.504: (tn, Heb): “your name.” In the OT the word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor. The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

notes.505: (tn, Heb): “your great name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in the previous verse.
notes.506: (tn, Heb): “and your strong hand and your outstretched arm.”

notes.507: (tn, Heb): “and do all which the foreigner calls to [i.e., “requests of”] you.”
notes.508: (tn, Heb): “your name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in v. 41.
notes.510: (tn, Heb): “that your name is called over this house which I built.” The Hebrew idiom “to call the name over” indicates ownership. See 2 Sam 12:28.

rashi.heb:
*כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא אֵלֶיךָ הַנָּכְרִי.* 
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא אוֹמֵר: וְנָתַתָּ לָאִישׁ כְּכָל דְּרָכָיו, לְפִי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַכִּיר בְּהַקָּבָּ"ה, וְיוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַיְכֹלֶת בְּיָדוֹ, וְאִם אֵין תְּפִלָּתוֹ נִשְׁמַעַת, תּוֹלֶה אֶת הַדָּבָר בְּעַצְמוֹ וּבְחֶטְאוֹ, אֲבָל עוֹבֵד גִּלּוּלִים קוֹרֵא תִּגָּר, וְאוֹמֵר: בַּיִת שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ הוֹלֵךְ לְסוֹף הָעוֹלָם, נִתְיַגַּעְתִּי לְכַמָּה דְּרָכִים וּבָאתִי וְהִתְפַּלַּלְתִּי בּוֹ, וְלֹא מָצָאתִי בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מַמָּשׁ בַּעֲבוֹדַת גִּלּוּלִים, לְפִיכָךְ כְּכָל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא אֵלֶיךָ הַנָּכְרִי, אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִם אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁהוּא מַשְׁחִית בְּמָמוֹנוֹ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, אַל תִּתֵּן לוֹ.
rashi.eng: *According to all that the stranger called to you for.* And by the [request of] the Jew he says (v. 39), “and give to every man according to his ways” [indicating that he may occasionally be refused,] that is because the Jew recognizes and accepts God, the Holy One, may He be blessed, and he knows that He has the ability in His power to respond [favorably to his request, if God so wished;] and if his prayers will not be heard [and fulfilled], he will blame the matter on himself and his sins. But [if] the non-Jew would [experience the same frustrations he would] say, a house whose name and fame reaches to the ends of the world, and I have exhausted myself [traveling] on many roads, and I [finally] came [to this house] and prayed in it and I find no substance [nor significance] in it, just as there is no substance in idol worshipping. Therefore, [I beg You, said Solomon,] “according to all that the stranger called to you for,” but [as for] the Jew, if you see that he uses his wealth to destroy his friend, [then] do not give him [any].

notes.511: (tn, Heb): “When your people go out for battle against their enemies in the way which you send them.”
notes.512: (tn): Or perhaps “to you, O Lord.” See 2 Chr 6:34.
notes.513: (tn, Heb): “your name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in v. 41.

rashi.heb:
*דֶּרֶךְ הָעִיר.* 
פּוֹנִים לְצַד יְרוּשָׁלַיִם.
rashi.eng: *Toward the city.* [while in the land of the enemy, they shall pray] facing towards Jerusalem.

notes.514: (tn, Heb): “their prayer and their request for help.”

rashi.heb:
*וְעָשִׂיתָ מִשְׁפָּטָם.* 
נִקְמָתָם בְּאוֹיְבֵיהֶם.
rashi.eng: *And maintain their cause.* their vengeance against their enemy.

notes.516: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (your people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.518: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (your people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.519: (tn, Heb): Or “stop and reflect”; “bring back to their heart.”

notes.522: (tn, Heb): “in the land of their enemies.”
notes.523: (tn, Heb): “your name.” See the note on the word “reputation” in v. 41.

notes.524: (tn, Heb): “their prayer and their request for help.”

notes.526: (tn, Heb): “and forgive your people who have sinned against you, [forgive] all their rebellious acts by which they rebelled against you, and grant them mercy before their captors so they will show them mercy.”

notes.529: (tn): The Hebrew term כּוּר (kur, “furnace,” cf. Akkadian ku„ru) is a metaphor for the intense heat of purification. A כּוּר was not a source of heat but a crucible (“iron-smelting furnace”) in which precious metals were melted down and their impurities burned away (see I. Cornelius, NIDOTTE 2:618-19). Thus Egypt served not as a place of punishment for the Israelites, but as a place of refinement to bring Israel to a place of submission to divine sovereignty. From the middle of the iron-smelting furnace. The metaphor of a furnace suggests fire and heat and is an apt image to remind the people of the suffering they endured while slaves in Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל.* 
הַחֶרֶס שֶׁמְּזַקְּקִין בּוֹ זָהָב, קָרוּי כּוּר.
rashi.eng: *The melting furnace of iron.* An earthenware utensil used to purify gold of its impurities.

notes.531: (tn, Heb): “to listen to them in all their calling out to you.”

notes.535: (tn, Heb): “he has given a resting place to his people Israel.”
notes.536: (tn, Heb): “not one word from his entire good word he spoke by Moses his servant has fallen.”

rashi.heb:
*כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּר.* 
וְהֵיכָן דִּבֵּר: וְהֵנִיחַ לָכֶם מִכָּל אוֹיְבֵיכֶם.
rashi.eng: *According to all that he spoke.* And where did he speak this? [As it is written], “And He shall give you rest from all your enemies [round about]” (Deuteronomy 12:10).

notes.537: (tn, Heb): “to bend our hearts toward him.” The infinitive is subordinate to the initial prayer, “may the Lord our God be with us.” The Hebrew term לֵבָב (levav, “heart”) here refers to the people’s volition and will.
notes.538: (tn, Heb): “to walk in all his ways.”

notes.540: (tn, Heb): “May these words of mine, which I have requested before the Lord, be near the Lord our God day and night.”

rashi.heb:
*לַעֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפַּט עַבְדּוֹ וּמִשְׁפַּט עַמּוֹ.* 
לִתְבֹּעַ עֶלְבּוֹנָם מִיַּד הָאוֹיֵב.
rashi.eng: *that He sustain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel.* to avenge their humiliation from their adversaries.

notes.543: (tn, Heb): “the Lord, he is the God, there is no other.”

notes.544: (tn, Heb): “may your hearts be complete with the Lord our God.”

notes.548: (tn): Or “tokens of peace”; NIV, TEV “fellowship offerings.”

notes.549: (tn, Heb): “to hold the burnt sacrifices, grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶת תּוֹךְ הֶחָצֵר.* 
דְּבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. קִדֵּשׁ אֶת רִצְפַּת הָעֲזָרָה בִּקְדֻשַּׁת מִזְבֵּחַ, לְהַקְטִיר עַל הָרִצְפָּה.
rashi.eng: *The same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard.* These words are to be taken literally. This is Rabbi Yehudah’s view. [Solomon] hallowed the pavement of the court with the sanctity of the altar, in order to offer sacrifices on the pavement.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי מִזְבַּח הַנְּחשֶׁת.* 
מִזְבַּח הָאֲבָנִים שֶׁעָשָׂה תַּחַת מִזְבַּח הַנְּחשֶׁת.
rashi.eng: *For the copper altar.* [i.e., the stone altar] that Solomon constructed in lieu of the copper altar [of Moses].

rashi.heb:
*קָטֹן מֵהָכִיל אֶת הָעוֹלָה וְאֶת הַמִּנְחָה.* 
שֶׁהִרְבּוּ לְהָבִיא. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסִי: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: אֶלֶף עוֹלוֹת יַעֲלֶה שְׁלֹמֹה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁעָשָׂה משֶׁה, וּכְשֶׁאַתָּה מַגִּיעַ לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן אַמּוֹת וּלְמִנְיַן עוֹלוֹת, זֶה שֶׁל אֲבָנִים גָּדוֹל מִשֶּׁל משֶׁה, שֶׁמִּזְבַּח משֶׁה מְקוֹם מַעֲרַכְתּוֹ אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה, וְזֶהוּ הָיָה מְקוֹם מַעֲרַכְתּוֹ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע עַל עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע, הֲרֵי שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁבְעִים וְשֵׁשׁ כְּשֶׁל משֶׁה, אִם כֵּן מַהוּ: קִדַּשׁ הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת תּוֹךְ הֶחָצֵר, שֶׁקָּבַע בּוֹ מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁל אֲבָנִים מְחֻבָּר בָּרִצְפָּה.
rashi.eng: *was too small to contain the burnt offerings and the meal offerings.* for they brought very many. Rabbi Jose said to him, Is it not already written (Kings 1:3), “One thousand burnt offerings Solomon offered on that altar which Moses had made,” and when one computes the number of cubits and the number of burnt offerings, [he will find that] this one of stones was larger than Moses’, for on Moses’ altar the place of the ‘maarachah,’ the place usually used for the sacrifice, was but one cubit by one cubit, whereas on this one the place of its ‘maarachah’ was twenty-four cubits by twenty-four cubits. Hence Solomon’s was 576 times as large as that of Moses. If so, what is the meaning of “the king consecrated the middle of the court?” It means that he set the stone altar into it, fastened to the floor.

rashi.heb:
*קָטֹן מֵהָכִיל.* 
בְּשֶׁל משֶׁה הוּא אוֹמֵר, כְּאָדָם שֶׁאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ: נַנָּס פְּלוֹנִי וּפָסוּל לַעֲבוֹדָה.
rashi.eng: *was too small to contain.* [According to Rabbi Jose] he is referring to that of Moses, like one who says to his friend, ‘So-and-so is a dwarf,’ meaning that he is disqualified to perform the sacrificial service.

notes.550: (tn): Or “the Wadi of Egypt” (NAB, NIV, NRSV); CEV “the Egyptian Gorge.”
notes.551: (tn, Heb): “Solomon held at that time the festival, and all Israel was with him, a great assembly from Lebo Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before the Lord our God for seven days and seven days, fourteen days.”

rashi.heb:
*מִלְּבוֹא חֲמָת.* 
שֶׁהִיא בִּצְפוֹנָהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
rashi.eng: *from the entrance to Hamath.* which is in the north of Eretz Israel.

rashi.heb:
*עַד נַחַל מִצְרַיִם.* 
שֶׁהִיא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בִּדְרוֹמָהּ, בְּאֵלֶּה מַסְעֵי.
rashi.eng: *to the Brook of Egypt.* which is opposite it in the south, as is delineated in the section entitled אֵלֶה מַסְעֵי (Num. 34:5-8).

rashi.heb:
*שִׁבְעַת יָמִים.* 
שֶׁל חִנּוּךְ.
rashi.eng: *seven days.* of the inauguration

rashi.heb:
*וְשִׁבְעַת יָמִים.* 
חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת, נִמְצָא שֶׁאָכְלוּ וְשָׁתוּ בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
rashi.eng: *and seven days.* of Succoth. It is found that they ate and drank on Yom Kippur.

notes.552: (tn, Heb): “on the eighth day” (that is, the day after the second seven-day sequence).

rashi.heb:
*לְדָוִד עַבְדּוֹ.* 
לְהוֹדִיעַ שֶׁמָּחַל לוֹ עֲוֹנוֹתָיו, כִּדְאִיתָא בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה לְהַכְנִיס הָאָרוֹן לְבֵית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים, דָּבְקוּ שְׁעָרִים זֶה בָּזֶה.
rashi.eng: *for David His servant.* to make known that He had forgiven him his sins, as we find in Moed Katan (9a): When Solomon wished [to bring] the Ark into the Holy of Holies, the gates clung to one another.

rashi.heb:
*וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ.* 
שֶׁמָּחַל לָהֶם עַל עֲוֹן יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְיָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה: כֻלְּכֶם מְזֻמָּנִים לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
rashi.eng: *and for Israel His people.* that He forgave them the sin of Yom Kippur, and a Bath-Kol [heavenly voice] emanated and declared: All of you are prepared for the life of the World to Come.

notes.555: (tn, Heb): “and all the desire of Solomon which he wanted to do.”

notes.556: (sn): In the same way he had appeared to him at Gibeon. See 1 Kgs 3:5.

notes.558: (tn, Heb): “by placing my name there perpetually” (or perhaps, “forever”).
notes.559: (tn, Heb): “and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהָיוּ עֵינַי וְלִבִּי.* 
תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: וּתְהִי שְׁכִנְתִּי שַׁרְיָא בֵיהּ אִם רְעוּתִי מִתְעַבְּדָא.
rashi.eng: *and My eyes and My heart shall be there at all times.* Jonathan rendered: And My Shechinah shall dwell there if My will is done.

rashi.heb:
*יְהֵא עֵינַי שָׁם.* 
אִם לִבִּי וְחֶפְצִי שָׁם.
rashi.eng: *And My eyes and My heart shall be there.* if My heart and My will are there.

notes.560: (tn, Heb): “As for you, if you walk before me, as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, by doing all which I commanded you, [and] you keep my rules and my regulations.” Verse 4 is actually a lengthy protasis (“if” section) of a conditional sentence, the apodosis (“then” section) of which appears in v. 5.

notes.561: (tn, Heb): “I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever.”
notes.562: (tn, Heb): “there will not be cut off from you a man from upon the throne of Israel.”

notes.564: (tn, Heb): “and walk and serve other gods and bow down to them.”

notes.565: (tn, Heb): “I will cut off Israel from upon the surface of the land.”
notes.566: (tn, Heb): “and the temple which I consecrated for my name I will send away from before my face.” Instead of “I will send away,” the parallel text in 2 Chr 7:20 has “I will throw away.” The two verbs sound very similar in Hebrew, so the discrepancy is likely due to an oral transmissional error.
notes.567: (tn, Heb): “will become a proverb and a taunt,” that is, a proverbial example of destruction and an object of reproach.

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר הִקְדַּשְׁתִּי לִשְׁמִי.* 
תְּנַאי הוּא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם, וְאִם לֹא תִּשְׁמְעוּ, מַה נֶּאֱמַר שָׁם: וַהֲשִׁמּוֹתִי אֶת מִקְדְּשֵׁיכֶם.
rashi.eng: *and this house which I have made sacrosanct for My Name.* There is a condition between Me and You, “If you heed not…” What is stated there? “I shall make desolate your sanctuaries” (Lev. 26:31).

rashi.heb:
*וְלִשְׁנִינָה.* 
כְּתַרְגּוּם: וּלְשׁוֹעֵי, יְסַפְּרוּ אֶת הָרָעוֹת הַבָּאוֹת עָלָיו וְיִתְלַעֲגוּ בּוֹ, כְּמוֹ: וַיְסַפֵּר, וְאִשְׁתָּעֵי. וּלְשׁוֹן 'שְׁנִינָה' אַף הוּא לְשׁוֹן 'דִּבּוּר', דִּכְתִיב: וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *and a byword.* As the Targum renders: וּלְשׁוּעִי and for a topic of conversation. They will tell [about the] evils [that] have befallen them and will scoff at them. Just as וַיְסַפֵּר “and he told” (Gen. 37:9) the Targum renders וְאִשְׁתָּעֵי. The expression שְׁנִינָה too is an expression of speech, as in וְשִׁנַּנְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ “And you shall repeat them to your children” (Deut. 5:7).

notes.568: (tn, Heb): “and this house will be high [or elevated].” The statement makes little sense in this context, which predicts the desolation that judgment will bring. Some treat the clause as concessive, “Even though this temple is lofty [now].” Others, following the lead of several ancient versions, emend the text to, “this temple will become a heap of ruins.”
notes.569: (tn, Heb): “hiss,” or perhaps “whistle.” This refers to a derisive sound one would make when taunting an object of ridicule.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה יִהְיֶה עֶלְיוֹן.* 
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא חֲטָאתֶם, וּמִשֶּׁתֶּחֶטְאוּ, כָּל עוֹבֵר עָלָיו יִשּׁוֹם וְיִשְׁרֹק. וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עֶלְיוֹן כָּל עוֹבֵר עָלָיו וְגוֹ'. וְכֹה פִּתְרוֹנוֹ: וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר הָיָה עֶלְיוֹן וְנוֹרָא אַף לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה: וְגַם אֶל הַנָּכְרִי אֲשֶׁר לֹא מֵעַמְּךָ וְגוֹ', וְעַכְשָׁיו בְּחֻרְבָּנוֹ, כָּל הָעוֹבֵר עָלָיו, אַף עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים, יִשּׁוֹם וְיִשְׁרֹק, וְיֹאמַר כִּי חֶטְאוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹרֵם.
rashi.eng: *And this house will be exalted.* as long as you have not sinned. And from the time you will sin, every passerby will be astounded and will hiss. And so it is written in Chron II 7:21: “And this house that was exalted by everyone who passed by it…” And this is its interpretation: And this house that was exalted and revered even by the gentiles, as is stated above: “And also to the gentile who is not of Your people…” (Chron. II 6:32), now in its destruction, everyone who passes by it, even the gentiles, will be astounded and will hiss, and will say that the Jews’ sins were the cause.

rashi.heb:
*יִשֹּׁם.* 
יִתְמַהּ, כְּמוֹ: וְשָׁמְמוּ עָלֶיהָ אוֹיְבֵיכֶם; עַל יוֹמוֹ נָשַׁמּוּ אַחֲרוֹנִים.
rashi.eng: *will be astounded.* יִשֹּׁם in Heb. will wonder, like “… and your enemies will wonder (ושממו) about it.” (Lev. 25:32. Also, “Concerning his day the later ones will wonder (נשמו)” (Job 18:20).

rashi.heb:
*וְשָׁרָק.* 
שופילי"ר בְּלַעַ"ז (לִשְׁרוֹק), וְכֵן דֶּרֶךְ כָּל הָרוֹאֶה חֻרְבָּן פִּתְאֹם, לִשְׁרֹק.
rashi.eng: *and will hiss.* siffler in French. Such is the habit of anyone who suddenly sees desolation, to hiss.

notes.572: (tn, Heb): “and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them.”

notes.573: (tn, Heb): “the two houses, the house of the Lord and the house of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה.* 
שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים לְבֵית ה', וְאֶת בֵּיתוֹ שְׁלשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה.
rashi.eng: *Twenty years.* i.e., seven years for the Temple, and thirteen years for his own palace, as mentioned above 6:38, 7:1.

notes.574: (map): For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

rashi.heb:
*נִשָּׂא אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה.* 
עִנְיַן עֹמֶס, כִּלְכֵּל אֶת מַשָּׂאוֹ בְּדָבָר זֶה.
rashi.eng: *had supplied Solomon.* An expression of bearing, i.e., he bore his burden in this matter.

notes.575: (tn, Heb): “they were not agreeable in his eyes.”

notes.577: (tn, Heb): “my brother.” Kings allied through a parity treaty would sometimes address each other as “my brother.” See 1 Kgs 20:32-33.
notes.578: (tn, Heb): “he called them the land of Cabul to this day.” The significance of the name is unclear, though it appears to be disparaging. The name may be derived from a root, attested in Akkadian and Arabic, meaning “bound” or “restricted.” Some propose a wordplay, pointing out that the name “Cabul” sounds like a Hebrew phrase meaning, “like not,” or “as good as nothing.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶרֶץ כָּבוּל.* 
אֶרֶץ כְּבָלִים, אֶרֶץ טִיט, שֶׁהָרֶגֶל מִשְׁתַּקֵעַ וְנִכְבֶּלֶת בָּהּ.
rashi.eng: *the land of Cabul.* A land of chains; i.e., a muddy land into which the foot sinks and is entrapped.

notes.579: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 9,000 pounds of gold (cf. NCV, NLT); CEV “five tons”; TEV “4,000 kilogrammes.”

notes.580: (sn): The work crews. This Hebrew word מַס (mas) refers to a group of laborers conscripted for royal or public service.
notes.582: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.583: (tn): The words “the cities of” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.584: (map): For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.
notes.585: (map): For location see Map1-D4; Map2-C1; Map4-C2; Map5-F2; Map7-B1.

rashi.heb:
*וְזֶה דְבַר הַמַּס.* 
מַה שֶּׁמְּפָרֵשׁ בְּסוֹף הָעִנְיָן: כָּל הָעָם הַנּוֹתָר וְגוֹ', וַיַּעֲלֵם שְׁלֹמֹה לְמַס עוֹבֵד, אוֹתוֹ הַמַּס הָיָה לִבְנוֹת בּוֹ אֶת כָּל אֵלֶּה.
rashi.eng: *And this is the matter of the tax levy.* delineated at the end of this topic (below v. 20- 21).“All the remaining people… of them did Solomon raise a levy of forced labor.” This tax levy was to build therewith all these [structures].

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת הַמִּלּוֹא.* 
מָקוֹם הָיָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּעִיר דָּוִד, וְנִקְרָא מִלּוֹא, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמֻּקָּף חוֹמָה נְמוּכָה, וּמִלְּאוּ לְתוֹכָהּ עָפָר.
rashi.eng: *and the Millo.* Heb. מלוא, a place that was in Jerusalem, in the city of David, that was called Millo, since it was enclosed by a low wall and was filled (מלא) with dirt.

rashi.heb:
*שִׁלֻּחִים.* 
נְדוּנְיָא.
rashi.eng: *a gift.* a dowry.

notes.586: (tn): The Hebrew text has “in the wilderness, in the land.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת תַּדְמוֹר בַּמִּדְבָּר בָּאָרֶץ.* 
אֵצֶל הַיִּשּׁוּב.
rashi.eng: *And Tadmor in the desert in the land.* near civilization.

notes.587: (tn, Heb): “to Solomon.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.588: (tn, Heb): “the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horses.”
notes.589: (tn, Heb): “and the desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his kingdom.”

rashi.heb:
*עָרֵי הַמִּסְכְּנוֹת.* 
(תרגום:) קִרְוֵי בֵּית אוֹצָרַיָּא.
rashi.eng: *the store-cities.* cities of storehouses.

notes.590: (tn, Heb): “all the people who were left from the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not from the sons of Israel.”

notes.591: (tn, Heb): “their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were unable to wipe out, and Solomon raised them up for a crew of labor to this day.”

notes.592: (sn): These work crews. The work crews referred to here must be different than the temporary crews described in 5:13-16.
notes.593: (tn, Heb): “officers of his chariots and his horses.”

notes.594: (tn, Heb): “these [were] the officials of the governors who were over the work belonging to Solomon, five hundred fifty, the ones ruling over the people, the ones doing the work.”

rashi.heb:
*שָׂרֵי הַנִּצָּבִים.* 
מְמֻנִּים עַל הַמְמֻנִּים.
rashi.eng: *These were the commanders of the officers.* That is to say, those who were appointed subordinate to the officers who were in overall command.

rashi.heb:
*חֲמִשִּׁים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת.* 
שְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת מֵהֶם הָיוּ גֵּרִים הַמְמֻנִּים עַל שִׁבְעִים אֶלֶף נוֹשֵׂא סַבָּל וּשְׁמוֹנִים אֶלֶף חוֹצֵב בָּהָר, וּשְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּשְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת הָרוֹדִים בָּעָם, שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה: לְבַד מִשָּׂרֵי הַנִּצָּבִים לִשְׁלֹמֹה וְגוֹ' שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּשְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת. וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים הוּא אוֹמֵר: שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת, אֵלּוּ שְׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת שֶׁחָסֵר שָׁם, מָנָה כָּאן, שֶׁהָיוּ מְמֻנִּים עַל כֻּלָּן, וּמָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנּוֹתָרִים, הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, מְמֻנִּים עַל שְׁאָר עוֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה. וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים מְנָאָן לְעַצְמָן: וְאֵלֶּה שָׂרֵי הַנִּצָּבִים לִשְׁלֹמֹה חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם הָרֹדִים בָּעָם, עוֹשֵׂי הַמְּלָאכָה.
rashi.eng: *five hundred fifty.* Three hundred of them were proselytes appointed over the 70,000 who bore burdens and the 80,000 hewers in the mountains, and the 3,300 who bore rule over the people, as stated above: “Besides Solomon’s chief officers… three thousand and three hundred” (5:30). And in II Chron. (2:1) it is stated: “six hundred.” These three hundred that are missing here (5:30), he counted there, for they were appointed over all of them. The two hundred and fifty remaining were Israelites appointed over the other laborers. In II Chron. (8:10) he counted them separately: “And these were Solomon’s chief officers two hundred fifty who bore rule over the people who did the work.”

notes.595: (sn): The phrase city of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
notes.596: (tn, Heb): “As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter went up from the city of David to her house which he built for her, then he built the terrace.”

rashi.heb:
*אַךְ בַּת פַּרְעֹה.* 
שֶׁהָיְתָה מִתְּחִלָּה בְּעִיר דָּוִד, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרֹאשׁ הַסֵּפֶר: וַיְבִיאָהּ אֶל עִיר דָּוִד.
rashi.eng: *But Pharaoh’s daughter.* who was originally in the city of David, as it is stated in the beginning of this book (3:1): “and he brought her to the city of David.”

rashi.heb:
*עָלְתָה מֵעִיר דָּוִד וְגוֹ'.* 
וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים מְפָרֵשׁ: כִּי אָמַר לֹא תֵשֵׁב אִשָּׁה לִי בְּעִיר דָּוִד כִּי קֹדֶשׁ הֵמָּה אֲשֶׁר בָּאָה אֲלֵיהֶם אֲרוֹן ה'.
rashi.eng: *came up from the city of David.* … In Chronicles (II 8:11) Scripture explains: “… for he said, A woman shall not live with me in the city of David (the exact wording is: ”… in the house of David, king of Israel.“) for they [the entire city and all the houses] are holy, for the Ark of the Lord was brought in to them.”

rashi.heb:
*אָז בָּנָה.* 
שְׁלֹמֹה.
rashi.eng: *then he built up.* i.e., Solomon.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא.* 
לִבְנוֹת לְתוֹכוֹ בָּתִּים, לַעֲבָדֶיהָ וּלְשִׁפְחוֹתֶיהָ, וְזֶה שֶׁהוֹכִיחוֹ יָרָבְעָם: אָבִיךָ הִנִּיחוֹ פָּרוּץ לְעוֹלֵי רְגָלִים, וְאַתָּה בָּנִיתָ אוֹתוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת אַנְגַּרְיָא לְבַת פַּרְעֹה, וְזֶהוּ 'אַךְ' הָאָמוּר כָּאן, אַךְ בְּזוֹ הֶעֱוָה שְׁלֹמֹה, שֶׁבָּנָה לָהּ אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי. וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, אַךְ בַּת פַּרְעֹה וְגוֹ', כְּלוֹמַר הֶעָרִים הָאֲמוּרוֹת לְמַעְלָה, הֻצְרַךְ לִבְנוֹת לְמִסְכְּנוֹת לָרֶכֶב וְלַפָּרָשִׁים וְלַגְּדֻלָּה, אַךְ אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא, לֹא הָיָה בּוֹנֶה לְשׁוּם גְּדֻלָּה, כִּי אָבִיו הִנִּיחוֹ לִפְרֹשׂ בּוֹ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים אֹהָלִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁבַּת פַּרְעֹה עָלְתָה אֶל בֵּיתָהּ, וְהַמִּלּוֹא סָמוּךְ לְאוֹתוֹ בַּיִת, אָז בָּנָה אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא.
rashi.eng: *the Millo.* (See above v. 15) to build within it houses for her manservants and maidservants. Concerning this Jeroboam admonished him, saying: Your father left it open for the pilgrims, and you enclosed it to make a labor force for Pharaoh’s daughter. This is [the inference of] “But” mentioned here. But in this did Solomon sin. So have I heard. I say, however, but Pharaoh’s daughter… i.e., the above mentioned cities were necessary to build for store-cities, for chariots, for riders, and for greatness. But, the Millo he did not build for any greatness, for his father had left it for the pilgrims to pitch their tents therein, but since Pharaoh’s daughter had gone up to her house, and the Millo was adjacent to that house, then he built up the Millo.

notes.597: (tn): Or “tokens of peace”; NIV, TEV “fellowship offerings.”
notes.598: (tn, Heb): “and he made complete the house.”

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.* 
שֶׁל בֵּית עוֹלָמִים.
rashi.eng: *upon the altar.* i.e., the altar of the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*וְהִקְטִיר אֹתוֹ.* 
וְאוֹתוֹ מִזְבַּח הַקְּטֹרֶת אֲשֶׁר לִפְנֵי ה' לִקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים.
rashi.eng: *and burning upon it, upon the altar that was before the Lord.* And that incense altar that was before the Lord for the burning of incense.

notes.599: (tn): Or “a fleet” (in which case “ships” would be implied).

rashi.heb:
*וָאֳנִי.* 
אֳנִיָּה.
rashi.eng: *King Solomon made a ship.* [The usual word is אֳנִיָה] a ship.

notes.600: (tn, Heb): “and Hiram sent with the fleet his servants, men of ships, [who] know the sea, [to be] with the servants of Solomon.”

notes.602: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 31,500 pounds of gold (cf. NCV); CEV, NLT “sixteen tons”; TEV “more than 14,000 kilogrammes.”

notes.603: (tn, Heb): “the report about Solomon.” The Hebrew text also has, “to the name of the Lord,” which fits very awkwardly in the sentence. If retained, perhaps it should be translated, “because of the reputation of the Lord.” The phrase, which is omitted in the parallel passage in 2 Chr 9:1, may be an addition based on the queen’s declaration of praise to the Lord in v. 9.

notes.606: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.607: (tn, Heb): “with very great strength.” The Hebrew term חַיִל (khayil, “strength”) may refer here to the size of her retinue (cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV) or to the great wealth she brought with her.

notes.609: (tn, Heb): “Solomon declared to her all her words; there was not a word hidden from the king which he did not declare to her.” If riddles are specifically in view (see v. 1), then one might translate, “Solomon explained to her all her riddles; there was no riddle too complex for the king.”

notes.613: (tn, Heb): “the seating of his servants and the standing of his attendants.”
notes.614: (tn, Heb): “there was no breath still in her.”

rashi.heb:
*וְעֹלָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲלֶה בֵּית ה'.* 
דֶּרֶךְ מָבוֹא שֶׁהֵכִין מִבֵּיתוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהָיָה עוֹלֶה בוֹ לְבֵית ה'.
rashi.eng: *and his ascent by which he would go up to the Temple of the Lord.* A passageway that he had prepared from his house to the Temple, by which he would go up to the house of the Lord.

notes.615: (tn, Heb): “about your words [or perhaps, “deeds”] and your wisdom.”

notes.616: (tn, Heb): “the half was not told to me.”

notes.618: (tn, Heb): “How happy are your men! How happy are these servants of yours, who stand before you continually, who hear your wisdom!”

notes.621: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 9,000 pounds of gold (cf. NCV, NLT); CEV “five tons”; TEV “4,000 kilogrammes.”
notes.622: (tn, Heb): “there has not come like those spices yet for quantity which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.”

rashi.heb:
*עֲצֵי אַלְמֻגִּים.* 
קוריי"ל בְּלַעַ"ז (אַלְמוֹגִים).
rashi.eng: *almog wood.* corail in French.

notes.623: (tn): This Hebrew architectural term occurs only here. The meaning is uncertain; some have suggested “banisters” or “parapets”; cf. TEV, NLT “railings.” The parallel passage in 2 Chr 9:11 has a different word, meaning “tracks,” or perhaps “steps.”
notes.624: (tn): Two types of stringed instruments are specifically mentioned, the כִּנּוֹר (kinnor, “zither” [?]), and נֶבֶל (nevel, “harp”).
notes.625: (tn, Heb): “there has not come thus, the fine timber, and there has not been seen to this day.”

rashi.heb:
*מִסְעָד לְבֵית ה'.* 
וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים כְּתִיב: מְסִלּוֹת לְבֵית ה', לְכָךְ אֲנִי אוֹמֵר, הַמִּסְעָד הַזֶּה לְשׁוֹן רִצְפָּה.
rashi.eng: *a path to the House of the Lord.* [lit. a support.] In II Chron. 9:11 it is written, מְסִלּוֹת, paths to the House of the Lord. I, therefore, say that this מִסְעָד, support, is an expression of a pavement.

rashi.heb:
*לַשָּׁרִים.* 
לִבְנֵי לֵוִי.
rashi.eng: *to accompany the vocalists.* for the Levites.

notes.626: (tn, Heb): “besides what he had given her according to the hand of King Solomon.”

rashi.heb:
*נָתַן לְמַלְכַּת שְׁבָא.* 
נְתִינָה זוֹ אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא לִמּוּד חָכְמָה.
rashi.eng: *And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba.* This giving refers only to the teaching of wisdom.

rashi.heb:
*כָּל חֶפְצָהּ.* 
(בָּא אֵלֶיהָ וְנוֹלַד מִמֶּנָּה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, וְהֶחֱרִיב הַבַּיִת שֶׁעָמַד אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת וְעֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים בְּחֵלֶק כָּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים, מֵהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל).
rashi.eng: *all her wish.* He cohabited with her and Nebuchadnezzar was born to her. He later destroyed the Temple that had stood 410 years in the territory of the twelve tribes. From the Arizal.

rashi.heb: *מִלְּבַד אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָהּ.*  מַתָּנוֹת וּמִגְדָּנוֹת הַמְּצוּיִין כָּאן וְאֵינָם מְצוּיִין בִּמְקוֹמָהּ.
rashi.eng: *aside from what he gave her.* Gifts and delicacies that are found here and are not in her place.

notes.628: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 50,000 pounds of gold (cf. NCV); CEV, NLT “twenty-five tons”; TEV “almost 23,000 kilogrammes.”
notes.629: (tn, Heb): “the weight of the gold which came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold.”

rashi.heb:
*שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וָשֵׁשׁ.* 
חִירָם נָתַן לוֹ מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים, וּמַלְכַּת שְׁבָא מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים, וָאֳנִי תַּרְשִׁישׁ הֵבִיאָה מֵאוֹפִיר אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת וְעֶשְׂרִים, הֲרֵי שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים, וְהַשִּׁשָּׁה לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מֵאַיִן. וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים כְּתִיב: שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ מֵאוֹפִיר אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים, וְאֵין מוֹנֶה שָׁם מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שֶׁל חִירָם, וְיֵשׁ לְתַקֵּן הַמִּקְרָא, שֶׁהַשְּׁלשִׁים הַיְתֵרִים הָיוּ מִן הַמֵּאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שֶׁל חִירָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי עַבְדֵי חִירָם הָיוּ שָׁם עִם עֲבָדָיו.
rashi.eng: *Six hundred sixty-six.* Hiram gave him 120 talents (v. 14). The Queen of Sheba, 120 (v. 10), the ships of Tarshish brought from Ophir 420, totaling 660. I do not know from where the other six came. In Chronicles (II 8:18) it stated that the ships brought from Ophir 450 talents, however it does not include the 120 talents of Hiram. We can resolve the contradictions [by saying] that the extra 30 were from the 120 of Hiram. because Hiram’s servants were in Ophir with his [Solomon’s] servants.

rashi.heb:
*לְבַד מֵאַנְשֵׁי הַתָּרִים.* 
שֶׁהָיוּ מְבִיאִים לוֹ הַסּוֹחֲרִים הַתָּרִים בָּאָרֶץ לִסְחוֹרָה.
rashi.eng: *Aside from [that which came through] merchants.* the merchants who traversed the land on business would bring to him.

rashi.heb:
*הָרֹכְלִים.* 
מוֹכְרֵי בְּשָׂמִים, וּמוֹלִיכִין אוֹתָם מֵעִיר לְעִיר.
rashi.eng: *And the spice peddlers.* Dealers of spice would carry them from city to city.

rashi.heb:
*וְכָל מַלְכֵי הָעֶרֶב.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וְכָל מַלְכֵי סוּמְכְוָתָא, לְשׁוֹן עֲרֻבָּה, הַמְּלָכִים שֶׁהָיוּ בַעֲרֻבָּתָן וְסוֹמְכִין עָלָיו, גאראנטיא"ה בְּלַעַ"ז (מִלְשׁוֹן עַרְבוּת).
rashi.eng: *and all the dependent kings.* Heb. וכל מלכי הערב. Jonathan Translates: מלכי סומכותא, and all the dependent kings, an expression of guarantee. Kings who granted support and were dependent on him; garantie in French.

notes.631: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply “six hundred,” with no unit of measure given.

rashi.heb:
*צִנָּה.* 
מַקֶּפֶת אֶת הָאָדָם מִשְּׁלשָׁה רוּחוֹתָיו, וְהוּא שֶׁאָמַר בְּסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים: כַּצִּנָּה רָצוֹן תַעְטְרֶנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *body shields.* Heb. צנה, a body shield that encircles the person from three sides. This is the meaning of the verse in Psalms (5:13), “You shall encompass him with will like a shield (כַּצִנָּה).”

rashi.heb:
*שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת זָהָב.* 
וְהוּא שֵׁשׁ מָנִים, שֶׁהַזָּהָב הוּא הַדִּינָר.
rashi.eng: *six hundred [dinar of].* Six manehs, for a piece of gold (זָהָב) is a dinar [and one hundred dinars total one maneh].

notes.632: (sn): Three minas. The mina was a unit of measure for weight.
notes.633: (sn): The Palace of the Lebanon Forest. This name was appropriate because of the large amount of cedar, undoubtedly brought from Lebanon, used in its construction. The cedar pillars in the palace must have given it the appearance of a forest.

rashi.heb:
*זָהָב שָׁחוּט.* 
הוּא רַךְ וְנוֹחַ לְהֵרָקַע.
rashi.eng: *malleable gold.* It is soft and easy to flatten out.

rashi.heb:
*זָהָב מוּפָז.* 
מַבְהִיק כְּמַרְגָּלִית.
rashi.eng: *glittering gold.* Heb. זהב מופז, which sparkles like diamonds.

notes.634: (tn, Heb): “[There were] armrests on each side of the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.”

rashi.heb:
*שֵׁשׁ מַעֲלוֹת.* 
מַדְרֵגוֹת לַעֲלוֹת בּוֹ, וְרֹאשׁ הַכִּסֵּא הָיָה עָגֹל, מְקוֹם מוֹשַׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *six steps.* steps by which to ascend onto it, and the top of the throne was circular, i.e., the place of the king’s seat.

rashi.heb:
*מֵאַחֲרָיו.* 
תִּקּוּן הַכִּסֵּא הָיָה רָחָב, וְהַמַּעֲלוֹת הָיוּ לְצַד פָּנָיו, וּלְצַד רְחָבָה לְצַד אַחֲרָיו הָיָה הַמּוֹשָׁב גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הַכִּסֵּא מָקוֹם עָגֹל.
rashi.eng: *from behind.* The steps were to the front and to the width. To the back was the seat, a round place, higher than the throne.

rashi.heb:
*וְיָדֹת מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה.* 
לִסְמֹךְ זְרוֹעוֹתָיו עֲלֵיהֶם, כְּמִין מַקְלוֹת זָהָב מִפֵּאָה לְפֵאָה, פְּשׁוּטִין לְיָמִין וְלִשְׂמֹאל.
rashi.eng: *and arms on both sides.* on which to support his arms, like two gold rails from corner to corner, extending on the right and on the left.

rashi.heb:
*וּשְׁנַיִם אֲרָיוֹת.* 
שֶׁל זָהָב, וְכָל צוּרַת הַכִּסֵּא מְפֹרֶשֶׁת בְּאַגָּדַת מְגִלַּת אֶסְתֵּר.
rashi.eng: *and two lions.* of gold. The entire plan of the throne is described in the Aggadah of the Book of Esther.

notes.635: (tn, Heb): “nothing like it had been made for all the kingdoms.”

notes.636: (tn, Heb): “there was no silver, it was not regarded as anything in the days of Solomon.”

rashi.heb:
*אֵין כֶּסֶף לֹא נֶחְשָׁב.* 
אֵין כֶּסֶף בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶם, כִּי לֹא נֶחְשָׁב.
rashi.eng: *none was of silver, [since] it was reckoned with as nothing.* Lit. there was no silver; it was not reckoned… i.e., there was no silver in any of them because it was not reckoned.

notes.637: (tn, Heb): “a fleet of Tarshish [ships].” This probably refers to large ships either made in or capable of traveling to the distant western port of Tarshish.
notes.640: (tn): The meaning of this word is unclear. Some suggest “baboons.”

rashi.heb:
*אֳנִי תַרְשִׁישׁ.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) סְפִינַת אַפְרִיקָא.
rashi.eng: *Ships of Tarshish.* Ships of Africa.

rashi.heb:
*שֶׁנְהַבִּים וְקֹפִים וְתֻכִּיִּים.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) שֵׁן דְּפִיל וְקוֹפִין וְטַוָּסִין.
rashi.eng: *ivory and monkeys and peacocks.* Elephant tusks, monkeys and peacocks.

notes.641: (tn, Heb): “King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth with respect to wealth and with respect to wisdom.”

notes.642: (tc): The Old Greek translation and Syriac Peshitta have “all the kings of the earth.” See 2 Chr 9:23.
notes.643: (tn, Heb): “and all the earth was seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom which God had placed in his heart.”

notes.644: (tn, Heb): “and they were bringing each one his gift, items of silver…and mules, the matter of a year in a year.”

rashi.heb:
*וְנֵשֶׁק.* 
כְּלֵי זַיִן.
rashi.eng: *weapons.*

notes.646: (tn, Heb): “he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.” For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*אֶלֶף וְאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת רֶכֶב.* 
וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים כָּתוּב: אֶלֶף (וּשְׁבַע) [וְאַרְבַּע] מֵאוֹת. וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי, אֶלֶף וְאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת בְּעָרֵי הָרֶכֶב הָיוּ, וְהַשְּׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת עִם הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְכָךְ פֵּרוּשׁוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: וַיַּנִּיחֵם בְּעָרֵי הָרֶכֶב, וְעִם הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיָה עוֹד רֶכֶב אֶחָד בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם. וְכָאן כָּךְ פֵּרוּשׁוֹ: וַיַּנְחֵם בְּעָרֵי הָרֶכֶב, וְעִם הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיוּ מִקְצָתָן בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם.
rashi.eng: *a thousand and four hundred chariots.* It is stated [that Solomon had] one thousand four hundred [chariots]. I say that one thousand four hundred were in the chariot cities and [the remaining] three hundred were with the king in Jerusalem. And this is the explanation [of the verse] in Chron.: “And he stationed them (i.e., the 1,400) in the chariot cities and with the king”; [i.e., with the king] there were other chariots in Jerusalem. While here this is the explanation: And he led them (i.e., the 1,400) in the chariot cities, and with the king; i.e., with the king were some of them in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּנְחֵם.* 
וַיְנַהֲלֵם.
rashi.eng: *he led them.*

notes.647: (tn): The words “as plentiful” are added for clarification.
notes.649: (tn, Heb): “as the sycamore fig trees which are in the Shephelah.”

rashi.heb:
*כַּאֲבָנִים.* 
וּלְמַעְלָה הוּא אוֹמֵר 'לִמְאוּמָה'. רַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ: כָּאן קֹדֶם שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה, כָּאן לְאַחַר שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.
rashi.eng: *as stones.* Our Rabbis explained that one refers to the time before Solomon wedded Pharaoh’s daughter, and one refers to the time after Solomon wedded Pharaoh’s daughter.

notes.650: (sn): From Egypt. Because Que is also mentioned, some prefer to see in vv. 28-29 a reference to Mutsur. Que and Mutsur were located in Cilicia/Cappadocia (in modern southern Turkey). See HALOT 625 s.v. מִצְרַיִם.

rashi.heb:
*וּמוֹצָא הַסּוּסִים אֲשֶׁר לִשְׁלֹמֹה.* 
הָיָה מִמִּצְרַיִם.
rashi.eng: *The source of Solomon’s horses.* [was] from Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*וּמִקְוֵה.* 
אֲסֵפַת סוֹחֲרֵי הַסּוּסִים בְּמִצְרַיִם, סוֹחֲרֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה הָיוּ קוֹנִין אוֹתָם בִּמְחִיר מִמִּצְרַיִם מִן הַמֶּלֶךְ, שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא אָדָם סוּס מִשָּׁם, אֶלָּא עַל יָדָם, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי. וּלְכָךְ נָקוּד עַל 'וּמִקְוֵה' טַעַם זָקֵ"ף גָּדוֹל, לִלְמֹד שֶׁהַתֵּבָה עוֹמֶדֶת בְּעַצְמָהּ, וְאֵינָהּ דְּבוּקָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
rashi.eng: *and an assemblage.*  The assemblage of horse merchants was in Egypt. Solomon’s merchants bid and bought the rights from the king of Egypt, that no person could export horses from there except through them. Therefore, there is a ‘Zakef Gadol’ on the word ‘Mikvei,’ to denote that the word ‘Mikvei’ [stands by itself, and] is not connected with the following words.

notes.651: (tn, Heb): “and a chariot went up and came out of Egypt for six hundred silver [pieces], and a horse for one hundred fifty, and in the same way to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram by their hand they brought out.”

rashi.heb:
*וְסוּס בַּחֲמִשִּׁים וּמֵאָה.* 
לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁהַמֶּרְכָּבָה בְּאַרְבַּע סוּסִים, וְכֵן בַּדָּמִים הַלָּלוּ לְכָל מַלְכֵי הַחִתִּים וּלְמַלְכֵי אֲרָם.
rashi.eng: *and a horse for one hundred fifty.* We deduce that a chariot consisted of four horses. And so for these prices to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.

rashi.heb:
*בְּיָדָם.* 
שֶׁל סוֹחֲרֵי שְׁלֹמֹה, יוֹצְאִים מִמִּצְרַיִם.
rashi.eng: *through them.* Through Solomon’s merchants did they export them from Egypt.

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.* 
אַף הִיא מִן הַנָּכְרִיּוֹת, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה עָלָיו מִכֻּלָּם, מְנָאָהּ לְעַצְמָהּ, וְכֵן: וַיִּפָּקְדוּ מֵעַבְדֵי דָוִד תִּשְׁעָה עָשָׂר אִישׁ וַעֲשָׂהאֵל.
rashi.eng: *and Pharaoh’s daughter.* She too was one of the foreign women, but since she was beloved by him more than all of them, she was counted separately. Similarly, (II Sam. 2: 30) “… and there were missing of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.”

notes.652: (tn, Heb): “you must not go into them, and they must not go into you.”
notes.653: (tn, Heb): “Surely they will bend your heart after their gods.” The words “if you do” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.654: (tn, Heb): “Solomon clung to them for love.” The pronominal suffix, translated “them,” is masculine here, even though it appears the foreign women are in view. Perhaps this is due to attraction to the masculine forms used of the nations earlier in the verse.

notes.656: (sn): Concubines were slave women in ancient Near Eastern societies who were the legal property of their master, but who could have legitimate sexual relations with their master. A concubine’s status was more elevated than a mere servant, but she was not free and did not have the legal rights of a free wife. The children of a concubine could, in some instances, become equal heirs with the children of the free wife. The usage in the present passage suggests that after the period of the Judges concubines may have become more of a royal prerogative (cf. also 2 Sam 21:10-14).

notes.659: (tn, Heb): “his heart was not complete with the Lord his God, like the heart of David his father.”

notes.661: (tn, Heb): “Milcom, the detestable thing of the Ammonites.”

notes.662: (tn, Heb): “in the eyes of the Lord.”
notes.663: (tn): The idiomatic statement reads in Hebrew, “he did not fill up after.”

notes.665: (sn): The hill east of Jerusalem refers to the Mount of Olives. For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.666: (sn): A high place. The “high places” were places of worship that were naturally or artificially elevated (see 1 Kgs 3:2).
notes.667: (tn, Heb): “Chemosh, the detestable thing of Moab.”
notes.668: (tc): The MT reads “Molech,” but Milcom must be intended (see vv. 5, 33).

rashi.heb:
*אָז יִבְנֶה שְׁלֹמֹה בָּמָה.* 
רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא מִחָה בְּנָשָׁיו, נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Then did Solomon build a high place.* Our Rabbis said, since he did not protest against his wives, it is referred to on his name.

rashi.heb:
*בָּהָר אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי יְרוּשָׁלָיִם.* 
הַר הַזֵּיתִים.
rashi.eng: *on the mountain that is before Jerusalem.* The Mount of Olives.

notes.669: (tn, Heb): “and the same thing he did for all his foreign wives, [who] were burning incense and sacrificing to their gods.”

notes.671: (sn): These two occasions are mentioned in 1 Kgs 3:5 and 9:2.

notes.672: (tn, Heb): “and had commanded him concerning this thing not to walk after other gods.”

notes.674: (tn, Heb): “Because this is with you, and you have not kept my covenant and my rules which I commanded you.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר הָיְתָה זֹּאת עִמָּךְ.* 
אֲשֶׁר יָדַעְתָּ שֶׁאַתָּה עוֹבֵר עַל מִצְוָתִי.
rashi.eng: *For as this has been with you.* i.e., you knew that you were transgressing My precept.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי בִּהְיוֹת דָּוִד אֶת אֱדוֹם.* 
אָז וַיִּבְרַח הֲדַד מִפְּנֵי דָוִד וְיוֹאָב.
rashi.eng: *And it was when David was in Edom.* Then Hadad fled before David and Joab.

rashi.heb:
*לְקַבֵּר אֶת הַחֲלָלִים.* 
שֶׁקָּבְרוּ לַהֲרוּגִים שֶׁל אֱדוֹם, הוּא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם בְּסֵפֶר שְׁמוּאֵל: וַיַּעַשׂ דָּוִד שֵׁם בְּשׁוּבוֹ מֵהַכּוֹתוֹ אֶת (אֱדוֹם) [אֲרָם], שֶׁהָיוּ הַכֹּל מְקַלְּסִין אוֹתוֹ, אִישׁ חָסִיד שֶׁקּוֹבֵר אֶת הֲרוּגָיו, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּמִלְחֲמוֹת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג: וְקָבְרוּ כָּל עַם הָאָרֶץ וְהָיָה לָהֶם לְשֵׁם. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם לְקַבֵּר אֶת הַחֲלָלִים: לְחַלָּצָא יַת קְטִילַיָּא, לָקַחַת אֶת חֲלִיצָתָם.
rashi.eng: *to bury the slain.* for they buried the slain of Edom. This is what is referred to in the Book of Samuel (II 8:13): “And David made for himself a name when he returned from smiting the Edomites,” for all were praising him as a kind man who buried his slain. And so Scripture says concerning the wars of Gog and Magog: (Ez 39:13) “And they will bury all the people of the land, and it will be for them for a name.” [However,] Jonathan [translated]: לְחַלָצָא יַתקְטִילַיָא, to strip the slain, to take their clothing.

notes.679: (tn, Heb): “until he had cut off every male in Edom.”

notes.680: (tn): The MT reads “Adad,” an alternate form of the name Hadad.
notes.681: (tn, Heb): “and Adad fled, he and Edomite men from the servants of his father, to go to Egypt, and Hadad was a small boy.”

notes.682: (tn, Heb): “and they arose from Midian and went to Paran and they took men with them from Paran and went to Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and he gave to him a house and food and he said to him, and a land he gave to him.” Something seems to be accidentally omitted after “and he said to him.”

rashi.heb:
*וְלֶחֶם אָמַר לוֹ.* 
אָמַר לִמְשָׁרְתָיו, כָּךְ וְכָךְ לֶחֶם תְּנוּ לוֹ לְיוֹם.
rashi.eng: *and assigned him sustenance.* He said to his attendants, so much bread shall you give him every day.

notes.683: (tn, Heb): “and Hadad found great favor in the eyes of Pharaoh.”
notes.684: (tn, Heb): “and he gave to him a wife, the sister of his wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.”

rashi.heb:
*הַגְּבִירָה.* 
הַמַּלְכָּה.
rashi.eng: *the queen.* Heb. הגבירה, lit. the mistress.

notes.686: (tc): The Hebrew text reads וַתִּגְמְלֵהוּ (vattigm�lehu, “weaned him”) but a slight alteration of the consonantal text yields וַתִּגְדְלֵהוּ (vattigd�lehu, “raised him”), which seems to make better sense.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי שָׁכַב דָּוִד.* 
דָּוִד שֶׁמֵּת מִיתַת עַצְמוֹ, נֶאֶמְרָה בוֹ שְׁכִיבָה, יוֹאָב שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג, נֶאֶמְרָה בוֹ מִיתָה. דָּבָר אַחֵר: דָּוִד שֶׁהִנִּיחַ בֵּן הָגוּן מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹמוֹ, נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ שְׁכִיבָה, יוֹאָב שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ בֵּן הָגוּן מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹמוֹ, לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה בוֹ שְׁכִיבָה, כִּי אִם מִיתָה.
rashi.eng: *That David slept with his fathers.* concerning David who died a natural death, an expression of sleeping is mentioned, whereas concerning Joab who was killed, [an expression of dying is mentioned (Eccles. R. 7:1; Mid. Shmuel)]. Another explanation is that concerning David who was survived by a meritorious son who took his place, an expression of sleeping is mentioned, whereas concerning Joab who was not survived by a meritorious son who took his place, no expression of [sleeping is mentioned, but an expression of dying].

notes.689: (tn, Heb): “Indeed what do you lack with me, that now you are seeking to go to your land?”
notes.691: (sn): So Hadad asked Pharaoh… This lengthy description of Hadad’s exile in Egypt explains why Hadad wanted to oppose Solomon and supports the author’s thesis that his hostility to Solomon found its ultimate source in divine providence. Though Hadad enjoyed a comfortable life in Egypt, when the Lord raised him up (apparently stirring up his desire for vengeance) he decided to leave the comforts of Egypt and return to Edom.

notes.692: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Solomon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּקֶם אֱלֹהִים לוֹ שָׂטָן.* 
לִשְׁלֹמֹה, וְזֶה הוּא שֶׁאָמַר נָתַן הַנָּבִיא לְדָוִד: אֲשֶׁר בְּהַעֲוֹתוֹ וְהֹכַחְתִּיו בְּשֵׁבֶט אֲנָשִׁים.
rashi.eng: *And God raised up against him an adversary,.* against Solomon. Now this is what Nathan the prophet said to David (Sam. II 7:14) so that when he goes astray, I will chasten him with the rod of men.

notes.693: (tn, Heb): “and he was the officer of a raiding band.”
notes.694: (tn): The Hebrew text reads “when David killed them.” This phrase is traditionally joined with what precedes. The ancient Greek version does not reflect the phrase and some suggest that it has been misplaced from the end of v. 23.

notes.695: (tn): The construction (Qal of קוּץ + בְּ [quts + bet] preposition) is rare, but not without parallel (see Lev 20:23).

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר הֲדָד.* 
עִם הָרָעָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הֲדָד, הָיְתָה גַּם זוֹ שֶׁל רָזוֹן.
rashi.eng: *with the evil that was caused by Hadad.* Together with the evil that was perpetrated by Hadad, was also this evil of Rezon.

notes.697: (tn, Heb): “Ephrathite,” which here refers to an Ephraimite (see HALOT 81 s.v. אֶפְרַיִם).

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּרֶם יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ.* 
הוֹכִיחוֹ בָּרַבִּים.
rashi.eng: *raised his hand against the king..* He rebuked him in public.

notes.698: (tn, Heb): “this is the matter concerning which he raised a hand against the king.”
notes.699: (sn): The city of his father David. The phrase refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.

rashi.heb:
*וְזֶה הַדָּבָר.* 
אֲשֶׁר הוֹכִיחוֹ עָלָיו.
rashi.eng: *And this was the matter.* concerning which he rebuked him.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁלֹמֹה בָּנָה אֶת הַמִּלּוֹא.* 
וּבְבִנְיָן זֶה סָגַר אֶת פֶּרֶץ הָעִיר דָּוִד, שֶׁהָיָה הַפֶּרֶץ אֲחוֹרֵי הַמִּלּוֹא, אָמַר לוֹ: אָבִיךָ פָּרַץ פְּרָצוֹת בַּחוֹמָה לִכָּנֵס בּוֹ עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים, וְאַתָּה גָּדַרְתָּ אוֹתָהּ, לַעֲשׂוֹת אַנְגַּרְיָא לְבַת פַּרְעֹה, לְהוֹשִׁיב שָׁם עֲבָדֶיהָ וּמְשָׁרְתֶיהָ.
rashi.eng: *Solomon built up the Millo.* and with this building he closed up the breach behind the Millo. He said to him, Your father made breaches in the wall for the pilgrims to enter, and you fenced it in, to create a labor force for Pharaoh’s daughter, to station there her manservants and maidservants.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּרְא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת הַנַּעַר.* 
קֹדֶם לָכֵן.
rashi.eng: *and Solomon saw.* prior to this.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי עוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה הוּא.* 
מָהִיר בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ וְזָרִיז.
rashi.eng: *that he was a diligent worker..* Lit. that he was doing work. Quick in his work and diligent.

rashi.heb:
*לְכָל סֵבֶל בֵּית יוֹסֵף.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) לְכָל מַסְקֵי מִסִּין דְּבֵית יוֹסֵף, מְנַשֶּׁה וְאֶפְרַיִם, לְפִי שֶׁמִּשֵּׁבֶט אֶפְרַיִם הָיָה.
rashi.eng: *Over all the burdens of the house of Joseph.* Over all the taxpayers of the house of Joseph [Targum Jonathan], Manasseh and Ephraim, since he was from the tribe of Ephraim.

notes.702: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply “he,” making it a bit unclear whether Jeroboam or Ahijah is the subject, but in the Hebrew word order Ahijah is the nearer antecedent, and this is followed by the present translation.

notes.703: (tn, Heb): “and Ahijah grabbed the new robe that was on him.”

notes.704: (tn): The words “I am taking the kingdom from him” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.705: (tc): This is the reading of the MT; the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate read “he has.”
notes.707: (tn, Heb): “by doing what is right in my eyes, my rules and my regulations, like David his father.”

notes.708: (tn, Heb): “and I will give it to you, ten tribes.”

notes.710: (tn, Heb): “so there might be a lamp for David my servant all the days before me in Jerusalem.” The metaphorical “lamp” symbolizes the Davidic dynasty. Because this imagery is unfamiliar to the modern reader, the translation “so my servant David’s dynasty may continue to serve me” has been used.
notes.711: (tn, Heb): “so there might be a lamp for David my servant all the days before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for myself to put my name there.”

rashi.heb:
*נִיר.* 
מֶמְשָׁלָה, וְ'נִיר' לְשׁוֹן 'עֹל'.
rashi.eng: *a kingdom.* Heb. ניר, a kingdom. ניר is an expression of a yoke.

notes.713: (tn, Heb): “If you obey.” In the Hebrew text v. 38 is actually one long conditional sentence, which has been broken into two parts in the translation for stylistic purposes.
notes.715: (tn, Heb): “do what is right in my eyes.”
notes.716: (tn, Heb): “I will build for you a permanent house, like I built for David.”

notes.717: (sn): Because of this. Reference is made to the idolatry mentioned earlier.

rashi.heb:
*אַךְ לֹא כָּל הַיָּמִים.* 
כִּי לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ תָּשׁוּב הַמְּלוּכָה אֵלָיו. וּבְסֵדֶר עוֹלָם מָצָאתִי: וַאעַנֶּה אֶת זֶרַע דָּוִד לְמַעַן זֹאת, כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ שָׁנָה שֶׁנִּתְחַתֵּן שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה, שֶׁנְּשָׂאָהּ בַּשָּׁנָה הָרְבִיעִית לְמָלְכוֹ, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵרָה עַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד לֵחָלֵק, וּרְאוּיָה הָיְתָה הַמְּלוּכָה לַחֲזֹר בִּימֵי אָסָא בִּשְׁנַת שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֶה לְמָלְכוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁקִּלְקֵל לִשְׁלֹחַ שֹׁחַד לְמֶלֶךְ אֲרָם, וְלֹא סָמַךְ עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְהוּא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: בִּשְׁנַת שְׁלשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ לְמַלְכוּת אָסָא, בָּנָה בַּעְשָׁא אֶת הָרָמָה, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָסָא קָבַר אֶת בַּעְשָׁא בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ לְמַלְכוּתוֹ, אֶלָּא שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה שֶׁלּוֹ, הוּא קוֹרֵא שְׁלשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ, שֶׁהֵן סוֹף שְׁלשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ לַחֲלֻקַת הַמַּלְכוּת, וְהִגִּיד הַכָּתוּב שֶׁבְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה קִלְקֵל אָסָא, אַךְ לֹא כָּל הַיָּמִים, אֶלָּא שְׁלשִׁים וָשֵׁשׁ שָׁנָה.
rashi.eng: *but not for all times..* For in the days of the Messiah the kingdom will be restored to him. In Seder Olam (ch. 15) I found: “I shall afflict David’s descendants because of this. Corresponding to the thirty-six years that Solomon was married to Pharaoh’s daughter, for he married her during the fourth year of his reign. Corresponding to this, the decree was promulgated on the kingdom of the house of David to be divided. The kingdom should have been restored, however, in Asa’s time, in the sixteenth year of his reign, but he sinned by sending a bribe to the king of Aram (below 15:18), and did not depend on the Most Holy, Blessed be He. This is the meaning of that which is stated in Chronicles (II 16:1). In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign Baasha built the high place.” This is impossible, since Asa buried Baasha in the twenty-seventh year of his reign (i.e., Baasha died in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reignI Kings 15:33). Rather, the sixteenth year of his reign, Scripture calls “the thirty-sixth,” for they are the end of thirty-six years from the division of the kingdom, and Scripture tells us that in that year Asa sinned. Thus we explain: “But not for all times,” [but thirty-six years].

notes.719: (tn, Heb): “but Jeroboam arose and ran away to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt.”

notes.720: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Solomon, and all which he did, and his wisdom, are they not written on the scroll of the events of Solomon?”

notes.721: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.723: (sn): The city of his father David. The phrase refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
