notes.724: (tc): Before this sentence the Old Greek translation includes the following words: “And it so happened that when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard – now he was in Egypt where he had fled from before Solomon and was residing in Egypt – he came straight to his city in the land of Sarira which is on mount Ephraim. And king Solomon slept with his fathers.”

notes.726: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.727: (tc): Verse 2 is not included in the Old Greek translation. See the note on 11:43.
notes.728: (tn, Heb): “and Jeroboam lived in Egypt.” The parallel text in 2 Chr 10:2 reads, “and Jeroboam returned from Egypt.” In a purely consonantal text the forms “and he lived” and “and he returned” are identical (וישׁב).

notes.729: (tn, Heb): “They sent and called for him.”

notes.731: (tn, Heb): “but you, now, lighten the burdensome work of your father and the heavy yoke which he placed on us, and we will serve you.” In the Hebrew text the prefixed verbal form with vav (וְנַעַבְדֶךָ, [v�na’avdekha] “and we will serve you”) following the imperative (הָקֵל [haqel], “lighten”) indicates purpose (or result). The conditional sentence used in the translation above is an attempt to bring out the logical relationship between these forms.

notes.734: (tn, Heb): “If today you are a servant to these people and you serve them and answer them and speak to them good words, they will be your servants all the days.”

notes.735: (tn, Heb): “He rejected the advice of the elders which they advised and he consulted the young men with whom he had grown up, who stood before him.” The referent (Rehoboam) of the initial pronoun (“he”) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.736: (tn): In the Hebrew text the verb “we will respond” is plural, although it can be understood as an editorial “we.” The ancient versions have the singular here.
notes.737: (tn, Heb): “Lighten the yoke which your father placed on us.”

notes.738: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Rehoboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.739: (tn, Heb): “Your father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter upon us.”
notes.740: (tn, Heb): “My little one is thicker than my father’s hips.” The referent of “my little one” is not clear. The traditional view is that it refers to the little finger. As the following statement makes clear, Rehoboam’s point is that he is more harsh and demanding than his father.

rashi.heb:
*קָטָנִּי עָבָה.* 
אֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה שֶׁלִּי.
rashi.eng: *My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.* Heb. קטני, my little finger.

notes.741: (tn, Heb): “and now my father placed upon you a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke.”
notes.742: (tn, Heb): “My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.” “Scorpions” might allude to some type of torture using poisonous insects, but more likely it refers to a type of whip that inflicts an especially biting, painful wound. Cf. CEV “whips with pieces of sharp metal.”

rashi.heb:
*עַקְרַבִּים.* 
אשגלנטי"ר בְּלַעַ"ז (עֵץ וֶרֶד–הַבָּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קוֹצִים), שֶׁעוֹקְצִין כְּעַקְרָב.
rashi.eng: *scorpions.* aiguillon in French, a goad or sting [called so] because they sting like scorpions.

notes.744: (tn, Heb): “and spoke to them according to.”
notes.745: (tn, Heb): “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke.”
notes.746: (tn, Heb): “My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.” See the note on the same phrase in v. 11.

notes.747: (tn, Heb): “because this turn of events was from the Lord.”
notes.748: (tn, Heb): “so that he might bring to pass his word which the Lord spoke.”

notes.749: (sn): We have no portion in David; no share in the son of Jesse. Their point seems to be that they have no familial relationship with David that brings them any benefits or places upon them any obligations. They are being treated like outsiders.
notes.750: (tn, Heb): “to your tents, Israel.” The word “return” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*רְאֵה בֵיתְךָ.* 
בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁבָּנִיתָ, לְךָ לְבַדְּךָ יִהְיֶה.
rashi.eng: *Now see your house.* The Temple that you built, will be for you alone.

notes.753: (tc): The MT has “Adoram” here, but the Old Greek translation and Syriac Peshitta have “Adoniram.” Cf. 1 Kgs 4:6.
notes.754: (sn): The work crews. See the note on this expression in 4:6.
notes.755: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*אֲדוֹרָם.* 
הוּא אֲדוֹנִירָם.
rashi.eng: *And King Rehoboam sent Adoram.* He was Adoniram [mentioned above in 5:28].

notes.756: (tn, Heb): “there was no one [following] after the house of David except the tribe of Judah, it alone.”

notes.757: (tn, Heb): “he summoned all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen men, accomplished in war.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִן.* 
הָעוֹמְדִים עַל הַגְּבוּל, שֶׁיְּהוּדָה וּבִנְיָמִין הָיָה גְּבוּלָם סָמוּךְ זֶה לָזֶה.
rashi.eng: *and the tribe of Benjamin.* Who were situated on the border, for the boundaries of Judah and Benjamin were adjacent.

notes.758: (tn, Heb): “and the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying.”

notes.759: (tn, Heb): “for this thing is from me.”
notes.760: (tn, Heb): “and they heard the word of the Lord and returned to go according to the word of the Lord.”

notes.761: (tc): The Old Greek translation has here a lengthy section consisting of twenty-three verses that are not found in the MT.

notes.763: (tn, Heb): “Now the kingdom could return to the house of David.” The imperfect verbal form translated “could return” is understood as having a potential force here. Perhaps this is not strong enough; another option is “will return.”

notes.764: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.765: (tn, Heb): “the heart of these people could return to their master.”

rashi.heb:
*אִם יַעֲלֶה הָעָם הַזֶּה וְגוֹ'.* 
אֵין יְשִׁיבָה בָּעֲזָרָה אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד בִּלְבַד, וְיִהְיֶה הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וַאֲנִי עוֹמֵד, וּבְמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית בִּזְמַן הַקְהֵל, יִקְרָא אֶת פָּרָשַׁת הַמֶּלֶךְ, שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ בִּמְדִינָתוֹ, וַאֲנִי כִּשְׁאָר הָעָם, נִמְצֵאתִי בָּזוּי.
rashi.eng: *When this people goes.* Sitting in the Temple court is not permitted except for the kings of the house of David only. Therefore, he [Rehoboam] will be seated and I will be standing. Moreover, in the year following the Sabbatical Year, at the time of the Assembly, he will read the portion relating to the king, for he is the king of his province, whereas I will be like the rest of the people, and will, therefore, find myself degraded.

notes.766: (tn): The words “with his advisers” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.767: (tn, Heb): “to them,” although this may be a corruption of “to the people.” Cf. the Old Greek translation.

notes.768: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

notes.769: (tn, Heb): “and this thing became a sin.”
notes.770: (tc): The MT reads “and the people went before the one to Dan.” It is likely that some words have been accidentally omitted and that the text originally said, “and the people went before the one at Bethel and before the one at Dan.”

rashi.heb:
*עַד דָּן.* 
בְּסוֹף גְּבוּל הָאָרֶץ.
rashi.eng: *even until Dan.* at the end of the boundary of the land.

notes.771: (tn): The Hebrew text has the singular, but the plural is preferable here (see 1 Kgs 13:32). The Old Greek translation and the Vulgate have the plural.

notes.772: (sn): The eighth month would correspond to October-November in modern reckoning.
notes.773: (sn): The festival he celebrated in Judah probably refers to the Feast of Tabernacles (i.e., Booths or Temporary Shelters), held in the seventh month (September-October). See also 1 Kgs 8:2.
notes.774: (tn, Heb): “and he offered up [sacrifices] on the altar; he did this in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves which he had made.”

notes.775: (tn, Heb): “which he had chosen by himself.”
notes.776: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jeroboam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.777: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

rashi.heb: *בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִי.* דָּרַשׁ לָהֶם הוּא חֹדֶשׁ הָאָסִיף, וּבוֹ רָאוּי הֶחָג לִהְיוֹת.
rashi.eng: *in the eighth month.* He expounded to them that this was the month of ingathering, and was, therefore, the proper time for the festival to be [celebrated].

rashi.heb: *בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ.* לְשׁוֹן כָּזָב, קונטרובי"ר בְּלַעַ"ז:
rashi.eng: *that he had fabricated from his heart.* Heb. אשר בדא מלבו, an expression of falsehood (controver in O.F., to invent).

notes.778: (tn, Heb): “Look.” The Hebrew particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) is a rhetorical device by which the author invites the reader to visualize the scene for dramatic effect.
notes.780: (tn, Heb): “came by the word of the Lord to Bethel.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים.* 
זֶה הָיָה עִדּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And behold a man of God.* This was Iddo.

notes.781: (tn, Heb): “by the word of the Lord.”
notes.782: (sn): ‘Look…you.’ For the fulfillment of this prophecy see 2 Kgs 23:15-20.

rashi.heb:
*מִזְבֵּחַ מִזְבֵּחַ.* 
שֶׁבְּבֵית אֵל וְשֶׁבְּדָן.
rashi.eng: *Altar, altar.* [Both the one] that is in Beth-El and [the one] that is in Dan.

rashi.heb:
*וְעַצְמוֹת אָדָם.* 
שֶׁל יָרָבְעָם זֶה, אֶלָּא שֶׁחָלַק לוֹ כָּבוֹד.
rashi.eng: *and human bones.* [This refers to the bones] of Jeroboam, but the prophet dealt him respect.

notes.785: (tn, Heb): “the fat.” Reference is made to burnt wood mixed with fat. See HALOT 234 s.v. דשׁן.

rashi.heb:
*וְנָתַן בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא.* 
הַנָּבִיא מוֹפֵת לִדְבָרָיו בַּיּוֹם שֶׁנִּתְנַבֵּא, זֶה לָכֶם הָאוֹת, הַמִּזְבֵּחַ נִקְרַע הַיּוֹם מֵאֵלָיו, וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדֶּשֶׁן לָאָרֶץ.
rashi.eng: *And he gave a sign on that day.* The prophet gave a sign on the day on which he prophesied. This is your sign: the altar will split by itself and the ashes will be spilled to the ground.

notes.788: (tn, Heb): “Jeroboam extended his hand from the altar.”
notes.790: (tn, Heb): “dried up” or “withered.” TEV and NLT interpret this as “became paralyzed.”

rashi.heb:
*וַתִּיבַשׁ יָדוֹ.* 
נָקַם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק יוֹתֵר מִכְּבוֹדוֹ, עוֹמֵד וּמַקְטִיר לַעֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים לֹא יָבְשָׁה יָדוֹ, וּבִשְׁבִיל לַעַז הַצַּדִּיק יָבְשָׁה יָדוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And his hand… became stiff.* The Holy One, Blessed be He, avenged the honor of a righteous man more than [He avenged] His own honor. [When] he was standing and offering sacrifices to pagan deities, his hand did not become stiff, yet because of the disdain for the righteous man his hand became stiff.

notes.791: (tn, Heb): “the fat.” Reference is made to burnt wood mixed with fat. See HALOT 234 s.v. דשׁן.
notes.792: (tn, Heb): “were poured out from the altar.”
notes.793: (tn, Heb): “according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.”

notes.794: (tn, Heb): “The king answered and said to.”
notes.795: (tn, Heb): “the man of God” (a second time later in this verse, and once in v. 7 and v. 8).
notes.797: (tn, Heb): “appeased the face of the Lord.”
notes.798: (tn, Heb): “and it was as in the beginning.”

rashi.heb:
*אֱלֹהֶיךָ.* 
וְלֹא אֱלֹהַי, עֲדַיִן עוֹמֵד בְּמִרְדּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *your God.* but not my God. He was still in a state of rebellion.

rashi.heb:
*וַתְּהִי כְּבָרִאשֹׁנָה.* 
עוֹמֵד וּמַקְטִיר לַעֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים.
rashi.eng: *and it was as before.* standing and burning sacrifices to idols.

rashi.heb:
*וּסֳעָדָה.* 
אֱכֹל.
rashi.eng: *and dine.* and eat.

notes.801: (tn, Heb): “for this he commanded me by the word of the Lord, saying.”

notes.803: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
notes.804: (tn, Heb): “and his son came and told him.” The MT has the singular here, but several other textual witnesses have the plural, which is more consistent with the second half of the verse and with vv. 12-13.
notes.806: (tn, Heb): “all the actions which the man of God performed that day in Bethel, the words which he spoke to the king, and they told them to their father.”

rashi.heb:
*וְנָבִיא אֶחָד.* 
נְבִיא הַשֶּׁקֶר.
rashi.eng: *And an elderly prophet.* a false prophet.

rashi.heb:
*יוֹשֵׁב בְּבֵית אֵל.* 
וְאֵינוֹ מִשָּׁם, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוֹמְרוֹן בָּא, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּפָרָשַׁת יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ: וַיְמַלְּטוּ עַצְמוֹתָיו אֶת עַצְמוֹת הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר בָּא מִשּׁוֹמְרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *sojourning in Beth-El.* He was not from there but from Samaria. So it is stated in the section dealing with Josiah (II Kings 23:18). And they saved his bones with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.

notes.807: (tn): The Hebrew text has “and his sons saw” (וַיִּרְאוּ [vayyir’u], Qal from רָאָה [ra’ah]). In this case the verbal construction (vav consecutive + prefixed verbal form) would have to be understood as pluperfect, “his sons had seen.” Such uses of this construction are rare at best. Consequently many, following the lead of the ancient versions, prefer to emend the verbal form to a Hiphil with pronominal suffix (וַיַּרְאֻהוּ [vayyar’uhu], “and they showed him”).

notes.811: (tn, Heb): “I am unable to return with you or to go with you.”

notes.813: (tn, Heb): “for a word to me by the word of the Lord.”

notes.816: (tn, Heb): “by the word of the Lord.”
notes.818: (tn): Or “deceiving him.” He was lying to him. The motives and actions of the old prophet are difficult to understand. The old man’s response to the prophet’s death (see vv. 26-32) suggests he did not trick him with malicious intent. The old prophet probably wanted the honor of entertaining such a celebrity, or perhaps simply desired some social interaction with a fellow prophet.

notes.819: (tn, Heb): “and he returned with him and ate food in his house and drank water.”

notes.820: (tn, Heb): “and the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶל הַנָּבִיא.* 
נְבִיא הַשֶּׁקֶר.
rashi.eng: *to the prophet.* the false prophet.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר הֱשִׁיבוֹ.* 
לָאִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים, מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: גְּדוֹלָה לְגִימָה שֶׁמַּשְׁרָה שְׁכִינָה עַל נְבִיאֵי הַבַּעַל.
rashi.eng: *who brought him back.* Who brought back the man of God. From here they deduced that offering refreshment is a great thing, for it causes the Shechinah to rest on the prophets of the Baal.

notes.821: (tn): The Hebrew text has “because” at the beginning of the sentence. In the Hebrew text vv. 21-22 are one long sentence comprised of a causal clause giving the reason for divine punishment (vv. 21-22a) and the main clause announcing the punishment (v. 22b). The translation divides this lengthy sentence for stylistic reasons.
notes.822: (tn, Heb): “the mouth [i.e., command] of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקְרָא.* 
הַנָּבִיא הַזָּקֵן, אֶל אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים.
rashi.eng: *And he called.* The old prophet called the man of God.

notes.823: (tn, Heb): “and you returned and ate food and drank water in the place about which he said to you, ‘do not eat food and do not drink water.’”
notes.824: (tn): “Therefore” is added for stylistic reasons. See the note at 1 Kgs 13:21 pertaining to the grammatical structure of vv. 21-22.
notes.825: (tn, Heb): “will not go to the tomb of your fathers.”

notes.826: (tn, Heb): “and after he had eaten food and after he had drunk.”
notes.827: (tn, Heb): “and he saddled for him the donkey, for the prophet whom he had brought back.”

rashi.heb:
*לַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר הֱשִׁיבוֹ.* 
שֵׁם זֶה לִרְכֹּב עָלָיו אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים.
rashi.eng: *for the prophet whom he had brought back.* [i.e., for the prophet] whom this one had brought there, for the man of God to ride upon.

notes.828: (tn, Heb): “and he went and a lion met him in the road and killed him.”
notes.829: (tn, Heb): “and his corpse fell on the road, and the donkey was standing beside it, and the lion was standing beside the corpse.”

notes.831: (tn, Heb): “the corpse.” The noun has been replaced by the pronoun (“it”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.832: (tn): The words “what they had seen” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

notes.833: (tn, Heb): “and the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard.”
notes.837: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke to him.”

notes.839: (tn, Heb): “the corpse.” The noun has been replaced by the pronoun (“it”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.840: (tn, Heb): “the prophet.” The word “old” has been supplied in the translation to distinguish this individual from the other prophet.

notes.842: (tn): “They” is the reading of the Hebrew text here; perhaps this is meant to include not only the old prophet but his sons (cf. v. 31).

rashi.heb:
*בְּקִבְרוֹ.* 
בְּבֵית קְבוּרָה שֶׁהָיָה לִנְבִיא הַשֶּׁקֶר הַזֶּה בָּעִיר.
rashi.eng: *in his grave.* [i.e.,] in the graveyard belonging to the false prophet in the city.

notes.844: (tn, Heb): “for the word which he cried out by the word of the Lord”
notes.845: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
notes.846: (tn, Heb): “Samaria.” The name of Israel’s capital city here stands for the northern kingdom as a whole. Actually Samaria was not built and named until several years after this (see 1 Kgs 16:24), so it is likely that the author of Kings, writing at a later time, is here adapting the old prophet’s original statement.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי הָיֹה יִהְיֶה וְגוֹ'.* 
אוּלַי יְמַלְּטוּ עַצְמוֹתָיו אֶת עַצְמוֹתַי.
rashi.eng: *For the thing… will come to be.* [i.e., the prophecy mentioned above in v. 2] and human bones they will burn upon you. Perhaps his bones will rescue my bones.

notes.847: (tn, Heb): “did not turn from his evil way.”
notes.848: (sn): The expression common people refers to people who were not Levites. See 1 Kgs 12:31.
notes.849: (tn, Heb): “and one who had the desire he was filling his hand so that he became [one of] the priests of the high places.”

rashi.heb:
*אַחַר הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה.* 
שֶׁרָאָה אֶת הַמּוֹפֵת הַזֶּה, וְשָׁמַע אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַנָּבִיא, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן לֹא שָׁב. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ: אַחַר שֶׁתְּפָסוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּבִגְדּוֹ, וְאָמַר לוֹ: חֲזֹר בְּךָ, וַאֲנִי וְאַתָּה וּבֶן יִשַׁי נְטַיֵּל בְּגַן עֵדֶן.
rashi.eng: *After this thing.* that he saw this wonder and heard the words of the prophet, he, nevertheless, did not return. And our Rabbis expounded: After the Holy One Blessed be He grasped him by his garment and said to him, Repent and I and you and the son of Jesse will stroll in Paradise.

notes.851: (tc): Some mss of the Old Greek lack vv. 1-20.

notes.853: (tn, Heb): “look, Ahijah the prophet is there, he told me [I would be] king over this nation.”

rashi.heb:
*וְנִקֻּדִים.* 
מִין קְלָיוֹת, מְיַבְּשִׁין בְּתַנּוּר וְעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן קֶמַח לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ מַאֲכָל, שֶׁקּוֹרִין לוֹ שְׁתִיתָא בִּלְשׁוֹן גְּמָרָא.
rashi.eng: *biscuits.* Heb. ונקדים. A type of parched grain, dried in an oven. They make flour from it to make it into a dish known in the language of the Gemara as ‘shethitha.’

notes.855: (tn, Heb): “and the wife of Jeroboam did so; she arose and went to Shiloh and entered the house of Ahijah.”
notes.856: (tn, Heb): “his eyes were set because of his old age.”

notes.857: (sn): Tell her so-and-so. Certainly the Lord gave Ahijah a specific message to give to Jeroboam’s wife (see vv. 6-16), but the author of Kings here condenses the Lord’s message with the words “so-and-so.” For dramatic effect he prefers to have us hear the message from Ahijah’s lips as he speaks to the king’s wife.

rashi.heb:
*וְהִיא מִתְנַכֵּרָה.* 
כְּאִלּוּ אֵינָהּ זֹאת.
rashi.eng: *she was disguised.* as though she were not this one.

notes.858: (tn, Heb): “I am sent to you [with] a hard [message].”

rashi.heb:
*שָׁלוּחַ אֵלַיִךְ.* 
מֵאֵת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּשְׁלִיחוּת קָשָׁה.
rashi.eng: *I am sent to you.* from the Holy One Blessed be He with a harsh message.

notes.859: (tn): The Hebrew text has “because” at the beginning of the sentence. In the Hebrew text vv. 7-11 are one long sentence comprised of a causal clause giving the reason for divine punishment (vv. 7-9) and the main clause announcing the punishment (vv. 10-11). The translation divides this lengthy sentence for stylistic reasons.

notes.860: (tn, Heb): “what was right in my eyes.”

notes.861: (tn, Heb): “you went and you made for yourself other gods, metal [ones], angering me, and you threw me behind your back.”

notes.862: (sn): Disaster. There is a wordplay in the Hebrew text. The word translated “disaster” (רָעָה, ra’ah) is from the same root as the expression “you have sinned” in v. 9 (וַתָּרַע [vattara’], from רָעַע, [ra’a’]). Jeroboam’s sins would receive an appropriate punishment.
notes.864: (tn, Heb): “and I will cut off from Jeroboam those who urinate against a wall (including both those who are) restrained and let free (or “abandoned”) in Israel.” The precise meaning of the idiomatic phrase עָצוּר וְעָזוּב (’atsur v�’azuv) is uncertain. For various options see HALOT 871 s.v. עצר 6 and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 107. The two terms are usually taken as polar opposites (“slaves and freemen” or “minors and adults”), but Cogan and Tadmor, on the basis of contextual considerations (note the usage with אֶפֶס [’efes], “nothing but”) in Deut 32:36 and 2 Kgs 14:26, argue convincingly that the terms are synonyms, meaning “restrained and abandoned,” and refer to incapable or incapacitated individuals.
notes.865: (tn): The traditional view understands the verb בָּעַר (ba’ar) to mean “burn.” Manure was sometimes used as fuel (see Ezek 4:12, 15). However, an alternate view takes בָּעַר as a homonym meaning “sweep away” (HALOT 146 s.v. II בער). In this case one might translate, “I will sweep away the dynasty of Jeroboam, just as one sweeps away manure it is gone” (cf. ASV, NASB, TEV). Either metaphor emphasizes the thorough and destructive nature of the coming judgment.

rashi.heb:
*מַשְׁתִּין בְּקִיר.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: יָדַע מַדָּע, מֵשִׁית בְּקִירוֹת לִבּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *male child.* Jonathan renders: One who knows knowledge; one who places [wisdom or counsel] into the walls of his heart.

rashi.heb:
*עָצוּר וְעָזוּב.* 
עָצוּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַחֲזִיק יָד, כְּמוֹ: זֶה יַעְצֹר בְּעַמִּי, וְעָזוּב, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַחֲזִיק בַּיָּד.
rashi.eng: *those who are restrained and those who are free.* Heb. עצור ועזוב. עצור is one who has someone restraining his hand, similar to “This one shall rule over (יעצור) My people” (Sam. 9:17). ועזוב means one who has no one restraining his hand.

rashi.heb:
*כַּאֲשֶׁר יְבַעֵר.* 
הַמְבַעֵר אֶת הַמַּאֲכָל בְּפִיו, לַעֲשׂוֹת גָּלָל, כָּךְ אֲבָעֵר אַחֲרָיו עַד תֻּמּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *as one expunges.* As the one who [consumes food to make] it eventually into dung, so will I expunge after him until he is completely consumed.

notes.866: (tn): The Hebrew text has “belonging to Jeroboam” here.

rashi.heb:
*דָּבָר טוֹב.* 
שֶׁבִּטֵּל מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ, שֶׁהוֹשִׁיבוֹ אָבִיו שׁוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה אִישׁ לָרֶגֶל, וּבִטֵּל מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וְעָלָה.
rashi.eng: *a good deed.* For he absented his watch, for his father had stationed him as a sentry so that no man would go up on the pilgrimage festivals. Instead, he absented his watch and he himself went up.

notes.869: (tn, Heb): “This is the day. What also now?” The precise meaning of the second half of the statement is uncertain.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר יַכְרִית אֶת בֵּית יָרָבְעָם זֶה הַיּוֹם וּמֶה גַּם עַתָּה.* 
הַנּוֹלָדִים לוֹ הַיּוֹם, וַאֲשֶׁר עֲתִידִין לְהִוָּלֵד לוֹ מֵעַתָּה, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן.
rashi.eng: *who will cut off the house of Jeroboam this day, and also those who will be born from now on..* [Those] who are already born to him this day, and those who are destined to be born to him from now on. So did Jonathan render.

notes.870: (tn): The elliptical Hebrew text reads literally “and the Lord will strike Israel as a reed sways in the water.”
notes.872: (tn, Heb): “the River.” In biblical Hebrew this is a typical reference to the Euphrates River. The name “Euphrates” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
notes.873: (tn, Heb): “because they made their Asherah poles that anger the Lord”; or “their images of Asherah”; ASV, NASB “their Asherim”; NCV “they set up idols to worship Asherah.” Asherah was a leading deity of the Canaanite pantheon, wife/sister of El and goddess of fertility. She was commonly worshiped at shrines in or near groves of evergreen trees, or, failing that, at places marked by wooden poles. These were to be burned or cut down (Deut 12:3; 16:21; Judg 6:25, 28, 30; 2 Kgs 18:4).

notes.876: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke.”

notes.877: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he ruled, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

notes.879: (tn, Heb): “Rehoboam.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.881: (tn, Heb): “the city where the Lord chose to place his name from all the tribes of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר ה'.* 
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן:
rashi.eng: *the city that the Lord had chosen.* Yet, even so…

notes.884: (tn, Heb): “and they made him jealous more than all which their fathers had done by their sins which they sinned.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוּדָה הָרָע.* 
וְלֹא נָתְנוּ זֶה עַל לִבָּם.
rashi.eng: *And Judah did what displeased the Lord.* and they did not pay attention to this.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְקַנְאוּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן קְנִיטָה.
rashi.eng: *and they angered Him.* Heb. ויקנאו [usually used in the sense of jealousy or zeal but here is] an expression of angering.

rashi.heb:
*גַּם הֵמָּה.* 
כִּשְׁאָר הַשְּׁבָטִים.
rashi.eng: *And they too.* [like the other] tribes.

notes.885: (tc): The Old Greek translation has “a conspiracy” rather than “male cultic prostitutes.”
notes.886: (tn, Heb): “they did according to all the abominable acts of the nations.”

rashi.heb:
*קָדֵשׁ.* 
נִאוּף.

*שִׁישַׁק.* 
מָצִינוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים) הוּא פַּרְעֹה נְכֹה, וְנִקְרָא שִׁישַׁק, עַל שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹקֵק וּמִתְאַוֶּה כָּל יָמָיו לְכִסֵּא הַשֵּׁן שֶׁהָיָה לִשְׁלֹמֹה חֲתָנוֹ, וְעַכְשָׁיו עָלָה וּלְקָחוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Shishak the king of Egypt.* We find in Midrash Shir Hashirim: This was Pharaoh Neco. He was called Shishak because all his life he longed for (שוקק) the ivory throne that belonged to Solomon, his son-in-law. Now, he went up and took it.

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת הַכֹּל לָקַח.* 
אֶת הַכִּסֵּא, הֶחָבִיב מִן הַכֹּל.
rashi.eng: *and he took everything.* the throne that was dearer to him than everything.

rashi.heb:
*יִשָּׂאוּם הָרָצִים.* 
לְפָנָיו לְכָבוֹד, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְשִׁיבוּם אֶל תָּא שֶׁהָרָצִים עוֹמְדִים שָׁם תָּמִיד.
rashi.eng: *the runners would carry them.* before him in honor. Afterwards, they would return them to the chamber where the runners were always stationed.

notes.888: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Rehoboam, and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”

notes.890: (tn): In the Hebrew text the name is spelled “Abijam” here and in 1 Kgs 15:1-8.

notes.891: (tc): The Old Greek also has the phrase “the son of Rehoboam.”

rashi.heb:
*וּבִשְׁנַת שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לַמֶּלֶךְ יָרָבְעָם.* 
שָׁנָה אַחַת אַחַר מוֹת רְחַבְעָם, וּבִשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים לְיָרָבְעָם מָלַךְ אָסָא, שָׁנָה הַשְּׁלִישִׁית שֶׁל נָדָב (אֲבִיָּם) נִמְנֵית לַמֶּלֶךְ אָסָא שָׁנָה, וְלוֹ נַמֵּי נִמְנֵית.
rashi.eng: *And in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam.* One year after Rehoboam’s death. Now in the twentieth year of Jeroboam, Asa reigned. The third year of Nadab [Abijam] is counted for King Asa as a year, and for him it is also counted.

notes.908: (tn, Heb): “mother,” but Hebrew often uses the terms “father” and “mother” for grandparents and more remote ancestors.

notes.910: (tn, Heb): “father,” but Hebrew often uses the terms “father” and “mother” for grandparents and more remote ancestors.

notes.911: (tn): The word used here, גִלּוּלִים [gillulim], is always used as a disdainful reference to idols. It is generally thought to have originally referred to “dung pellets” (cf. KBL 183 s.v. גִלּוּלִים). It is only one of several terms used in this way, such as “worthless things” (אֱלִילִים, ’elilim), “vanities” or “empty winds” (הֲבָלִים, havalim).

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעֲבֵר הַקְּדֵשִׁים.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וּפַלֵּי נָפְקַת בְּרָא.
rashi.eng: *and he abolished the adulterers.* Jonathan renders: And he abolished the prostitutes.

notes.913: (tn, Heb): “mother,” but Hebrew often uses the terms “father” and “mother” for grandparents and more remote ancestors.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְסִרֶה מִגְּבִירָה.* 
מִהְיוֹת גְּבִירָה.
rashi.eng: *from being queen.* Heb. מגבירה, [lit. from queen,] from being queen.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר עָשְׂתָה מִפְלֶצֶת.* 
אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ מַפְלִיא לֵיצָנוּתָא, כְּמִין זַכְרוּת עָשְׂתָה לָּהּ, וְהִיא הָיְתָה נִבְעֶלֶת לוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם.
rashi.eng: *for she had made a frightful image.* Our Rabbis stated: [מפלצת is a combination of] מפליא ליצנותא, it carried lasciviousness to an extreme. She made for it a phallic symbol, and she would copulate with it every day.

notes.914: (tn, Heb): “yet the heart of Asa was complete with the Lord all his days.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהַבָּמוֹת לֹא סָרוּ.* 
בָּמוֹת הַיָּחִיד, שֶׁהֻרְגְּלוּ לִקָּרֵב עֲלֵיהֶן לַשָּׁמַיִם מִשֶּׁחָרְבָה שִׁילֹה עַד שֶׁנִּבְנָה הַבַּיִת שֶׁהָיוּ הַבָּמוֹת מֻתָּרוֹת, לֹא סָרוּ עַתָּה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֶסְרוּ מִשֶּׁנִּבְנָה הַבַּיִת, וְהָיוּ עֲנוּשִׁים עָלֶיהָ כָּרֵת.
rashi.eng: *The high places he did not remove.* The private high places upon which they had become accustomed to sacrifice to Heaven since Shiloh had been destroyed until the Temple was built, when the high places were permissible, were not removed now. Even though they were forbidden when the Temple was built and the people were punished by premature death because of it.

notes.915: (tn, Heb): “and he brought the holy things of his father and his holy things (into) the house of the Lord, silver, gold, and items.” Instead of “his holy things,” a marginal reading (Qere) in the Hebrew text has “the holy things of [the house of the Lord].”

notes.916: (tn, Heb): “There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.”

notes.917: (tn, Heb): “and he built up Ramah so as to not permit going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.”

notes.919: (tn, Heb): “[May there be] a covenant between me and you [as there was] between my father and your father.”
notes.920: (tn, Heb): “so he will go up from upon me.”

notes.926: (tn, Heb): “and King Asa built with them.”

rashi.heb:
*אֵין נָקִי.* 
אֲפִלּוּ חָתָן מֵחֶדְרוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: נָקִי יִהְיֶה לְבֵיתוֹ שָׁנָה אֶחָת.
rashi.eng: *without exception.* [lit. no one was exempt.] Even a bridegroom concerning whom it is stated (Deut. 24:5) “He shall be free for his house one year.”

notes.927: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of all the events of Asa, and all his strength and all which he did and the cities which he built, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”
notes.928: (tn, Heb): “Yet in the time of his old age he became sick in his feet.”

rashi.heb:
*שְׁנָתַיִם.* 
הַשְּׁנִיָּה וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית לְאָסָא.
rashi.eng: *two years.* the second and the third year of Asa.

notes.931: (tn, Heb): “and he walked in the way of his father and in his sin which he made Israel sin.”

notes.932: (tn, Heb): “against him”; the referent (Nadab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.933: (tn, Heb): “and when he became king, he struck down all the house of Jeroboam; he did not leave any breath to Jeroboam until he destroyed him.”
notes.934: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke.”

notes.935: (tn, Heb): “because of Jeroboam which he committed and which he made Israel commit, by his provocation by which he made the Lord God of Israel angry.”

notes.936: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Nadab, and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

rashi.heb:
*בִּשְׁנַת שָׁלשׁ לְאָסָא מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה מָלַךְ בַּעְשָׁא.* 
שָׁנָה הַשְּׁלִישִׁית לְאָסָא, נִמְנֵית לְנָדָב וּלְבַּעְשָׁא.
rashi.eng: *During the third year of Asa, king of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah, reigned.* The third year of Asa is counted for Nadab and Baasha.

notes.938: (tn, Heb): “and he walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he made Israel sin.”

notes.939: (tn, Heb): “and the word of the Lord came to Jehu son of Hanani concerning [or “against”] Baasha, saying.”

notes.940: (tn): The Hebrew text has “because” at the beginning of the sentence. In the Hebrew text vv. 2-3 are one sentence comprised of a causal clause giving the reason for divine punishment (v. 2) and the main clause announcing the punishment (v. 3). The translation divides this sentence for stylistic reasons.
notes.941: (tn, Heb): “walked in the way of Jeroboam.”

notes.943: (tn): The traditional view understands the verb בָּעַר (ba’ar) to mean “burn.” However, an alternate view takes בָּעַר (ba’ar) as a homonym meaning “sweep away” (HALOT 146 s.v. II בער). In this case one might translate, “I am ready to sweep away Baasha and his family.” Either metaphor emphasizes the thorough and destructive nature of the coming judgment.
notes.944: (tc): The Old Greek, Syriac Peshitta, and some mss of the Targum have here “his house.”

notes.946: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Baasha, and that which he did and his strength, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

notes.948: (tn, Heb): “and also through Jehu son of Hanani the word of the Lord came concerning [or “against”] Baasha and his house, and because of all the evil which he did in the eyes of the Lord.”
notes.949: (tn, Heb): “angering him by the work of his hands, so that he was like the house of Jeroboam, and because of how he struck it down.”

rashi.heb:
*וְגַם בְּיַד יֵהוּא בֶן חֲנָנִי הַנָּבִיא דְּבַר ה' הָיָה אֶל בַּעְשָׁא.* 
כְּלוֹמַר הֲרֵי שֶׁמָּלַךְ אֵלָה בֶּן בַּעְשָׁא, וְאַף גַּם זֹאת דְּבַר ה' הָיָה בְּיַד יֵהוּא, שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְקַיֵּם מַלְכוּתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Nevertheless, in the hand of Jehu the son of Hanani, the prophet, was the word of the Lord concerning Baasha.* As though to say: Behold Elah reigned. Nevertheless, the word of the Lord was already in the hand of Jehu that his kingdom would not last.

rashi.heb:
*וְעַל אֲשֶׁר הִכָּה אוֹתוֹ.* 
הוֹאִיל וְגַם הוּא הָלַךְ בְּחַטֹּאתָיו, נִמְצָא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְהָרְגוֹ, לְכָךְ נֶעֱנַשׁ עַל הֲרִיגָתוֹ, וְכֵן מָצִינוּ: וּפָקַדְתִּי אֶת דְּמֵי יִזְרְעֶאל עַל בֵּית יֵהוּא, הוֹאִיל וְלֹא סָרוּ מִדַּרְכֵי אַחְאָב, נֶעֶנְשׁוּ עַל הֲרִיגָתָם.
rashi.eng: *and because he had slain him.* Since he too, committed the same sins, [lit. went in his sins,] it is found that he should not have slain him. He was, therefore, punished for his murder. So do we find in Hosea (1:4), “And I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu.” Since they did not turn away from Ahab’s ways, they were punished for their murder.

notes.950: (tn, Heb): “while he was drinking and drunken.”

rashi.heb:
*שַׂר מַחֲצִית הָרָכֶב.* 
הוּא וְאַחֵר הָיוּ שָׂרִים עַל הָרֶכֶב.
rashi.eng: *captain of half his chariots.* He and another were captains over the chariots.

notes.951: (tn, Heb): “and he became king in his place.”

notes.952: (tn, Heb): “and he did not spare any belonging to him who urinate against a wall, [including] his kinsmen redeemers and his friends.”

rashi.heb:
*וְגֹאֲלָיו וְרֵעֵהוּ.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) וּקְרִיבוֹהִי וְרִחֲמוֹהִי.
rashi.eng: *any males.* nor his kinfolk nor his friends.

notes.953: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke concerning [or “spoke against”]).”

notes.954: (tn, Heb): “angering the Lord God of Israel with their empty things.”

notes.955: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Elah, and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

notes.957: (tn, Heb): “and the people who were encamped heard.”
notes.958: (tn, Heb): “has conspired against and also has struck down the king.”

notes.959: (tn, Heb): “and he burned the house of the king over him with fire and he died.”

notes.961: (tn, Heb): “walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he did to make Israel sin.”

notes.962: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the events of Zimri, and his conspiracy which he conspired, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּמָת תִּבְנִי.* 
כְּשֶׁנָּשָׂא אָסָא בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל עָמְרִי לִיהוֹשָׁפָט בְּנוֹ, הָרְגוּ אֶת תִּבְנִי, כְּשֶׁרָאוּ חֲשִׁיבוּתוֹ שֶׁל עָמְרִי, בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם.
rashi.eng: *And Tibni died.* When Asa took Omri’s daughter in marriage for Jehoshaphat his son, they killed Tibni, when they saw Omri’s importance. In Seder Olam (Ch. 17).

rashi.heb:
*בִּשְׁנַת שְׁלשִׁים וְאַחַת שָׁנָה לְאָסָא וְגוֹ' מָלַךְ עָמְרִי.* 
מַלְכוּת שְׁלֵמָה, וַחֲמֵשׁ שָׁנִים הָיְתָה מַחֲלֻקְתּוֹ שֶׁל תִּבְנִי, מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְשֶׁבַע לְאָסָא, עַד שְׁלשִׁים וְאַחַת.
rashi.eng: *In the thirty-first year of Asa… Omri ruled.* a complete, [uncontested,] reign. Five years was [the duration] of his conflict with Tibni, from the twenty-seventh year of Asa until the thirty-first.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה.* 
סַךְ הַכֹּל, חָמֵשׁ בַּמַּחֲלֹקֶת וְשֶׁבַע בְּמַלְכוּת שְׁלֵמָה, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה בְּמַלְכוּת שְׁלֵמָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי אַחְאָב בְּנוֹ מָלַךְ בִּשְׁנַת שְׁלשִׁים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה לְאָסָא.
rashi.eng: *twelve years.* was the total, five years in conflict and seven with a complete reign. It is impossible to say [that he reigned] twelve years uncontested, for Ahab his son reigned in the thirty-eighth year of Asa.

rashi.heb:
*בְּתִרְצָה מָלַךְ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים.* 
עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּנָה אֶת שׁוֹמְרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *in Tirzah he ruled six years.* while he had not yet built Samaria.

notes.963: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
notes.964: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 150 pounds of silver.

notes.967: (tn, Heb): “walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin which he made Israel sin.”
notes.968: (tn, Heb): “angering the Lord God of Israel with their empty things.”
