notes.972: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

notes.974: (tn, Heb): “and he went and served Baal and bowed down to him.” The Canaanites worshiped Baal as a storm and fertility god.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעֲבֹד אֶת הַבַּעַל.* 
מוֹסִיף עַל עֲגָלִים שֶׁל יָרָבְעָם.
rashi.eng: *and worshipped the Baal.* in addition to Jeroboam’s calves.

notes.975: (tn, Heb): “Ahab”; the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֵׁרָה.* 
אִילָן הַנֶּעֱבָד.
rashi.eng: *And Ahab made the Asherah.* a tree that was worshipped.

notes.977: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.978: (tn, Heb): “with Abiram, his firstborn, he founded it.”
notes.979: (tn, Heb): “with Segub, his youngest, he set up its gates.”
notes.980: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke.”
notes.981: (sn): Warned through Joshua son of Nun. For the background to this statement, see Josh 6:26, where Joshua pronounces a curse on the one who dares to rebuild Jericho. Here that curse is viewed as a prophecy spoken by God through Joshua.

rashi.heb:
*חִיאֵל בֵּית הָאֱלִי.* 
חִיאֵל אֲשֶׁר מִבֵּית אֵל, כְּמוֹ: יִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי, וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר הַבֵּית לַחְמִי; וְכֵן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֵּית הַשִּׁמְשִׁי, בְּסֵפֶר שְׁמוּאֵל, וְלֹא הַבֵּית שִׁמְשִׁי; וְכֵן בְּעָפְרַת אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר הָאֲבִי עֶזְרִי. וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין: בֵּית הָאֱלִי, עַל שֶׁקִּבֵּל עָלָיו קִלְלוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אָרוּר הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יָקוּם וּבָנָה וְגוֹ'. אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ חִיאֵל מִשֶּׁל (בִּנְיָמִין) וִירִיחוֹ מִשֶּׁל יְהוֹשָׁפָט (בִּנְיָמִין) וּמִפְּנֵי מָה תְלָאוֹ בְּאַחְאָב, שֶׁתּוֹלִין אֶת הַקְּלָלָה בִּמְקֻלְקָל (סְפָרִים אֲחֵרִים: בִּמְקֻלָּל).
rashi.eng: *Hiel the Bethelite.* Heb. ביתהאלי, similar to “Jesse the Bethlehemite (ביתהלחמי)” (I Sam. 16:1), and it does not say הביתלחמי. And so, “Joshua the Bethshemeshite (ביתהשמשי)” in the Book of Sam. (I 6:14), and not הביתשמשי, and so, “In Ofrah of the Abiezerites (אבי העזרי)” (Jud. 6:25), and it does not say, האבי עזרי. Some interpret ביתהאלי [from the word אלה, a curse,] since he accepted upon himself Joshua’s curses, “Cursed be the man… that rises up and builds…” (Jos. 6:26). Our Rabbis stated, Hiel was of the tribe of Benjamin, and Jericho belonged to Jehoshaphat [king of Judea]. Why does Scripture relate him to Ahab [king of Israel]? For a curse is related to a cursed one.

rashi.heb:
*בַּאֲבִירָם בְּכֹרוֹ יִסְּדָהּ.* 
כְּשֶׁיִּסְדָהּ, מֵת בְּנוֹ בְּכוֹרוֹ, וְקָבַר וְהָלַךְ וְקָבַר כָּל בָּנָיו, עַד שֶׁמֵּת הָאַחֲרוֹן בְּהַצָּבַת דְּלָתוֹת, וְכֵן הוּא קְלָלוֹת שֶׁל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: בִּבְכוֹרוֹ יְיַסְּדֶנָּה וּבִצְעִירוֹ יַצִּיב דְּלָתֶיהָ.
rashi.eng: *with Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation.* When he laid its foundation, his firstborn son died, and he buried him and continued to bury all his sons until the last one died when he erected the portals. Now, these were Joshua’s curses, “With [the loss of] his firstborn shall he lay its foundation, and with [the loss of] his youngest son shall he set up its gates” (Jos. 6:26).

notes.983: (tn, Heb): “except at the command of my word.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּי.* 
מֵאֶרֶץ (סְפָרִים אֲחֵרִים: שֵׁם הָעִיר) שֶׁשְּׁמָהּ תּוֹשָׁב.
rashi.eng: *And Elijah the Tishbite.* from a land named Toshav.

rashi.heb:
*חַי ה'.* 
לָמָּה סְמָכוֹ כָּאן, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָלְכוּ אֵלִיָּהוּ וְאַחְאָב לְנַחֵם אֶת חִיאֵל בְּאֶבְלוֹ, אָמַר אַחְאָב לְאֵלִיָּהוּ: אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁקִּלְלַת הַתַּלְמִיד נִתְקַיְּמָה, וְקִלְלַת משֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ לֹא נִתְקַיְּמָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְסַרְתֶּם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם לָהֶם, וְחָרָה אַף ה' בָּכֶם וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמָיִם, וַהֲרֵי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹבְדִין עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְאֵין גְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִים, מִיָּד וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *As the Lord… lives.* Why was this placed here? For Elijah and Ahab went to console Hiel in his mourning. Said Ahab to Elijah, "Is it possible that the disciple’s curse was fulfilled while Moses our teacher’s curse was not fulfilled, as it is said: (Deut. 11:15) “And you will turn and worship other gods, and bow down to them, the Lord’s wrath will be kindled against you, and He will shut up the heaven.” Now, all Israel are worshipping idols, and the rains are not being withheld." Immediately, Elijah… said…

notes.984: (tn, Heb): “and the word of the Lord came to him, saying.”

rashi.heb:
*וְנִסְתַּרְתָּ.* 
מִפְּנֵי אַחְאָב וְאִיזֶבֶל.
rashi.eng: *and hide.* from Ahab and Jezebel.

notes.988: (tn, Heb): “And it came about at the end of days.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּבַשׁ הַנַּחַל.* 
כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּדַע צֹרֶךְ הַגְּשָׁמִים וְיַטְרִיחַ לְגַלּוֹת, שֶׁהָיָה קָשֶׁה בְּעֵינֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין בְּרָעָב.
rashi.eng: *the brook dried up.* in order that that he know the necessity of rain and trouble himself to go into exile, for it was displeasing to the Holy One, Blessed be He, that Israel should live in hunger.

notes.989: (tn, Heb): “And the word of the Lord came to him, saying.”

rashi.heb:
*צָרְפָתָה.* 
שֵׁם הָעִיר.
rashi.eng: *to Zarephath.* the name of a city.

rashi.heb:
*צִוִּיתִי שָׁם.* 
בְּפָמַלְיָא שֶׁלִּי, שֶׁתְּכַלְכֶּלְךָ שָׁם אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה.
rashi.eng: *Behold I have commanded there.* in My household that a widow shall feed you there.

rashi.heb:
*קְחִי נָא לִי מְעַט מַיִם.* 
הוּא לֹא הָיָה מַכִּיר בָּאַלְמָנָה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְלָמַד מֵאֱלִיעֶזֶר עֶבֶד אַבְרָהָם, וְאָמַר: אוֹתָהּ שֶׁתִּתֵּן לִי מַיִם לִשְׁתּוֹת, הִיא הָאַלְמָנָה.
rashi.eng: *Please take to me a little water.* He did not recognize the widow concerning whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, had told him. He learned from Eliezer, the servant of Abraham, (Gen. 24:15), and said, The one who gives me water is the widow.

notes.992: (tn): The Hebrew text also includes the phrase “in your hand.”

notes.993: (tn, Heb): “Look, I am gathering two sticks and then I will go and make it for me and my son and we will eat it and we will die.”

rashi.heb:
*מָעוֹג.* 
כְּמוֹ עוּגָה.
rashi.eng: *a cake.* Heb. מעוג [like עוגה, a cake].

rashi.heb:
*מְלֹא כַף.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: מְלֵי פִּיסַת יְדָא.
rashi.eng: *[nothing] but a handful.* Jonathan rendered: the palm of a handful.

rashi.heb:
*בַצַּפָּחַת.* 
ביטויל"א בְּלַעַ"ז (בַּקְבּוּקוֹן), כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּשָׁאוּל: צַפַּחַת הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר מֵרַאֲשׁוֹתָיו.
rashi.eng: *in a flask.* bouteille in French, [a bottle,] as it is stated regarding Saul, “the jug (צפחת) of water that was at his head” (I Sam. 26:16).

rashi.heb:
*וָמָתְנוּ.* 
מִשָּׁם וּלְהַלָּן נָמוּת בָּרָעָב.
rashi.eng: *and we will die.* From then on, we will die of hunger.

rashi.heb:
*עֻגָה קְטַנָּה בָרִאשֹׁנָה.* 
מִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה יֵשׁ, (לָמָּה בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה) בְּוַתֹּאמֶר לֵאָה בָּגָד.
rashi.eng: *but first make for me a small cake.* There is a Midrash Agadah in Gen. Rabbah (why he wanted his cake first) on the verse: "And Leah said, 'Good fortune has come'" (Gen. 30: 11).

notes.995: (tn, Heb): “and she ate, she and he and her house [for] days.”

notes.996: (tn, Heb): “out, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke.”

rashi.heb:
*חָלָה בֶּן הָאִשָּׁה.* 
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לְמַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁלתְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, כִּדְאִיתָא בְשִׁלְהֵי אַגַּדְתָּא דְּחֵלֶק.
rashi.eng: *the son of the woman.* became ill in order that he should need the key of Resurrection of the dead, as it is stated at the end of the Agadah of chapter Chelek (San. 113a).

notes.998: (tn, Heb): “What to me and to you, man of God, that you have come.”

rashi.heb:
*לְהַזְכִּיר אֶת עֲוֹנִי.* 
עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּאתָ אֵלַי, הָיוּ שׁוֹקְלִין מַעֲשַׂי וּמַעֲשֵׂה עִירִי, וְהָיִיתִי רְאוּיָה לְנֵס, מִשֶּׁבָּאתָ לְכָאן, לֹא נֶחְשַׁבְתִּי לִכְלוּם, וְאֵין צִדְקָתִי נִכֶּרֶת (סְפָרִים אֲחֵרִים: נִזְכֶּרֶת), וְכֵן בְּלוֹט הוּא אוֹמֵר: וְאָנֹכִי לֹא אוּכַל לְהִמָּלֵט הָהָרָה, אֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם, שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא זְכוּתִי נִזְכֶּרֶת אֶצְלוֹ.
rashi.eng: *to cause my sin to be remembered.* Before you came, the Heavenly Tribunal would weigh my deeds and the deeds of the people of my city, and I was worthy of a miracle. Since you have come, here, I am not counted as anything since my righteousness is not noticeable. And similarly, concerning Lot scripture states: “And I am not able to flee to the mountain” (Gen. 19:19) to Abraham, for my merit will not be remembered in comparison to his.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּתְמֹדֵד.* 
מִלְּשׁוֹן מִדָּה, נִשְׁתַּטַּח עָלָיו.
rashi.eng: *And he prostrated himself.* Heb. ויתמודד, from an expression of מדה, a measure, i.e., he prostrated himself upon him.

notes.1000: (tn, Heb): “you are a man of God and the word of the Lord is truly in your mouth.” This episode is especially significant in light of Ahab’s decision to promote Baal worship in Israel. In Canaanite mythology the drought that swept over the region (v. 1) would signal that Baal, a fertility god responsible for providing food for his subjects, had been defeated by the god of death and was imprisoned in the underworld. While Baal was overcome by death and unable to function like a king, Israel’s God demonstrated his sovereignty and superiority to death by providing food for a widow and restoring life to her son. And he did it all in Sidonian territory, Baal’s back yard, as it were. The episode demonstrates that Israel’s God, not Baal, is the true king who provides food and controls life and death. This polemic against Baalism reaches its climax in the next chapter, when the Lord proves that he, not Baal, controls the elements of the storm and determines when the rains will fall.

notes.1001: (tn, Heb): “the word of the Lord came to Elijah.”

notes.1002: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

notes.1003: (tn, Heb): “now Obadiah greatly feared the Lord.” “Fear” refers here to obedience and allegiance, the products of healthy respect for the Lord’s authority.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי בְּהַכְרִית אִיזֶבֶל.* 
לְהַגִּיד בָּא אֵיךְ הָיָה עוֹבַדְיָהוּ יָרֵא אֶת ה'.
rashi.eng: *And it was when Jezebel cut off.* [Scripture] comes to tell [us] how Obadiah feared the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*חֲמִשִּׁים אִישׁ בִּמְעָרָה אַחַת.* 
וַחֲמִשִּׁים אִישׁ בִּמְעָרָה אַחֶרֶת.
rashi.eng: *fifty men in a cave.* [i.e., fifty men in one cave] and fifty men in another cave.

rashi.heb:
*וְלוֹא נַכְרִית מֵהַבְּהֵמָה.* 
לֹא תִכָּרֵת כָּל בְּהֶמְתֵּנוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *and we will not lose all our beasts.* all our beasts will not be cut off from us.

notes.1007: (tn): The Hebrew text has “alone” here and again in reference to Obadiah toward the end of the verse.

notes.1011: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Obadiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*לַהֲמִיתֵנִי.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ וְאוֹמֵר: וְרוּחַ ה' יִשָּׂאֲךָ עַל אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֵדַע.
rashi.eng: *to kill me.* as he goes on to explain (v. 12) “And a wind from the Lord will carry you to a place I know not where.”

notes.1013: (tn, Heb): “he makes the kingdom or the nation swear an oath.”

rashi.heb:
*כִּי לֹא יִמְצָאֶכָּה.* 
שֶׁאֵין הָעָם יָכוֹל לִמְצֹא אוֹתְךָ.
rashi.eng: *that they did not find you.* [i.e., he made them swear] that the nation was unable to find you.

notes.1015: (tn, Heb): “to [a place] which I do not know.”
notes.1016: (tn, Heb): “and I will go to inform Ahab and he will not find you and he will kill me.”
notes.1017: (tn): The words “that would not be fair” are added to clarify the logic of Obadiah’s argument.
notes.1018: (tn, Heb): “has feared the Lord” (also see the note at 1 Kgs 18:3).

notes.1019: (tn, Heb): “Has it not been told to my master what I did…?” The rhetorical question expects an answer, “Of course it has!”

notes.1023: (tn, Heb): “Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.”

notes.1026: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.1028: (tn): The word “messengers” is supplied in the translation both here and in v. 20 for clarification.
notes.1029: (tn, Heb): “who eat at the table of Jezebel.”

notes.1030: (tn, Heb): “How long are you going to limp around on two crutches?” (see HALOT 762 s.v. סְעִפִּים). In context this idiomatic expression refers to indecision rather than physical disability.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁתֵּי הַסְּעִפִּים.* 
שְׁתֵּי הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת, שֶׁאֵינְכֶם מְבִינִים לְהַכְרִיעַ מִי הָאֱלֹהִים.
rashi.eng: *two ideas.* two thoughts, for you do not know to decide who is God.

rashi.heb:
*וְאִם הַבַּעַל.* 
הָאֱלֹהִים, לְכוּ אַחֲרָיו.
rashi.eng: *and if the Baal.* is God, go after him.

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא עָנוּ הָעָם אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.* 
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ יוֹדְעִין לְהַבְחִין.
rashi.eng: *And the people did not answer him a word.* because they did not know to distinguish.

notes.1033: (tn): Elijah now directly addresses the prophets.
notes.1035: (tn, Heb): “The matter [i.e., proposal] is good [i.e., acceptable].”

notes.1036: (tc): The last sentence of v. 25 is absent in the Syriac Peshitta.

notes.1037: (tn, Heb): “and they took the bull which he allowed them.”
notes.1038: (tn, Heb): “limped” (the same verb is used in v. 21).
notes.1039: (tc): The MT has “which he made,” but some medieval Hebrew mss and the ancient versions have the plural form of the verb.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָהֶם.* 
שֶׁהָיָה נִשְׁמַט מֵהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יִקָּרֵב לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּבָרַח לוֹ תַּחַת כְּנָפָיו שֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ, אָמַר לוֹ: לֵךְ, בִּשְׁנֵיכֶם יִתְקַדֵּשׁ הַמָּקוֹם.
rashi.eng: *that he gave them.* For he slipped away from them lest he be offered to the idol. He escaped under the skirt of Elijah’s cloak. He said to him, Go! Through both of you the Omnipresent will be sanctified.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּפְסְחוּ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וְאִשְׁתַּטּוּ, הָיוּ מְרַקְּדִין כְּמִשְׁפָּטָן עַל מִזְבְּחוֹתָם.
rashi.eng: *and they hopped on the altar that they had made.* Jonathan renders: And they raved. They were dancing according to their custom, on their altars.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּפְסְחוּ.* 
כְּמוֹ וַיִּפְסְעוּ.
rashi.eng: *and they hopped.* Heb. ויפסחו, like ויפסעו, and they stepped.

notes.1040: (sn): Elijah’s sarcastic proposals would have been especially offensive and irritating to Baal’s prophets, for they believed Baal was imprisoned in the underworld as death’s captive during this time of drought. Elijah’s apparent ignorance of their theology is probably designed for dramatic effect; indeed the suggestion that Baal is away on a trip or deep in sleep comes precariously close to the truth as viewed by the prophets.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי אֱלֹהִים הוּא.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) אֲרֵי אַתּוּן אָמְרִין דַּחֲלָא הוּא.
rashi.eng: *for he is a god.* for you say he is one to be feared.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי שִׂיחַ וְכִי שִׂיג לוֹ.* 
שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ לוֹ דָּבָר עִם יוֹעֲצָיו עַכְשָׁיו, אוֹ מַשִּׂיג וְרוֹדֵף הוּא עַכְשָׁיו בַּמִּלְחָמָה.
rashi.eng: *Perhaps he is talking or he is pursuing.* Perhaps he is having a conference with his advisors now, or he is overtaking and pursuing his enemies in war.

rashi.heb:
*וְכִי דֶרֶךְ לוֹ.* 
לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא.
rashi.eng: *or he is on a journey.* to the water closet.

notes.1042: (tn, Heb): “until blood poured out on them.” mutilated…covered with blood. This self-mutilation was a mourning rite designed to facilitate Baal’s return from the underworld.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּתְגֹּדְדוּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן שְׂרִיטָה בִּכְלִי, וְכֵן הָיָה נִימוּסֵיהֶן.
rashi.eng: *and gashed themselves.* an expression of tearing [the flesh] with an instrument. Such was their custom.

notes.1043: (tn, Heb): “when noon passed they prophesied until the offering up of the offering.”
notes.1044: (tc): The Old Greek translation and Syriac Peshitta include the following words here: “When it was time to offer the sacrifice, Elijah the Tishbite spoke to the prophets of the abominations: ‘Stand aside for the time being, and I will offer my burnt offering.’ So they stood aside and departed.” In 2 Kgs 4:31 the words “there was no sound and there was no response” are used to describe a dead boy. Similar words are used here to describe the god Baal as dead and therefore unresponsive.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּתְנַבְּאוּ.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) וְאִשְׁתַּטִּיאוּ.
rashi.eng: *and they feigned to prophesy.* and they raved.

notes.1045: (sn): Torn down. The condition of the altar symbolizes the spiritual state of the people.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְרַפֵּא אֶת מִזְבַּח ה' הֶהָרוּס.* 
בָּנָה מִזְבֵּחַ, וְהִזְכִּיר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת מִזְבַּח ה' עוֹלֶה עַל לִבָּם וְשָׁגוּר בְּפִיהֶם, שֶׁהָיָה הָרוּס וְנִפְגָּר וּבָטֵל שְׁמוֹ וְהַזְכָּרָתוֹ מִפִּי כָּל עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים, כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי פְּשׁוּטוֹ. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ שָׁמַעְתִּי, שֶׁשָּׁאוּל בָּנָה מִזְבֵּחַ בְּהַר הַכַּרְמֶל, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר: בָּא שָׁאוּל הַכַּרְמֶלָה וְהִנֵּה מַצִּיב לוֹ יָד, וּלְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר: וַיַּצֵּב שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ, וּמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרְסוּ כָּל הַמִּזְבְּחוֹת וְהַבָּמוֹת שֶׁבְּאַרְצָם שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, וּבָנָה אֵלִיָּהוּ מִזְבֵּחַ זֶה שֶׁל שָׁאוּל, שֶׁהָיָה הָרוּס.
rashi.eng: *and he repaired the torn down altar of the Lord.* He built an altar and reminded Israel that the altar of the Lord should enter their thoughts and should be spoken of with fluency, for it was torn down and destroyed and its name and its mention had ceased from the mouth of all the ten tribes. Thus I heard its simple interpretation. And its Midrashic interpretation I have heard, that Saul built an altar on Mt. Carmel. That is what [Scripture means when] it states: (I Sam. 15:12) “Saul has come to Carmel, and behold, he is setting up a place,” and there (Gen. 33:20) it says: “And he set up an altar there.” [By a gezerah shavah, analogous expression, we deduce that Saul too, set up an altar]. And the kings of Israel tore down all the altars and high places in their land that were made in the name of Heaven, and Elijah built this altar of Saul that was torn down.

notes.1046: (tn): The word “new” is implied but not actually present in the Hebrew text.
notes.1047: (sn): Israel will be your new name. See Gen 32:28; 35:10.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר הָיָה דְּבַר ה' אֵלָיו לֵאמֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה שְׁמֶךָ.* 
לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר כָּאן, לְפִי שֶׁבְּיוֹם שֶׁנִּגְלְתָה שְׁכִינָה עַל יַעֲקֹב בְּבֵית אֵל וּקְרָאוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל, בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם אָמַר לוֹ: גּוֹי וּקְהַל גּוֹיִם יִהְיֶה מִמֶּךָּ, עֲתִידִין בָּנֶיךָ לְהִקָּהֵל כִּשְׁאָר עַמִּים, וְלִבְנוֹת מִזְבֵּחַ לְהַקְטִיר עָלָיו בִּשְׁעַת אִסּוּר הַבָּמוֹת, וַאֲנִי מִתְרַצֶּה בַדָּבָר, בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה.
rashi.eng: *to whom the word of the Lord came, saying, “Israel shall be your name.”.* Why is this stated here? Because on the day that the Shechinah was revealed to Jacob in Bethel and called him Israel, on that day He said to him, “A nation and a congregation of nations will be from you” (Gen. 35:11). Your children are destined to congregate like other nations and build an altar to burn sacrifices on it during the time when the high places are proscribed. Nevertheless, I will consent to it (Gen. Rabbah 82:6).

notes.1048: (tn, Heb): “and he built the stones into an altar in the name of the Lord.”
notes.1049: (tn): A seah was a dry measure equivalent to about seven quarts.

rashi.heb:
*תְּעָלָה.* 
פושאד"ו בְּלַעַ"ז (חֲפִירָה).
rashi.eng: *a trench.* fosse in French.

rashi.heb:
*כְּבֵית סָאתַיִם.* 
רָחְבּוֹ בֵּית סָאתַיִם, מֵאָה עַל חֲמִשִּׁים, כַּחֲצַר הַמִּשְׁכָּן.
rashi.eng: *as great as would contain two se’ah.* Its width was as great as to hold two se’ah, one hundred cubits by fifty cubits like the court of the mishkan.

notes.1050: (tn): The words “when they had done so” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*כַּדִּים מַיִם.* 
לְהַגְדִּיל אֶת הַנֵּס.
rashi.eng: *pitchers of water.* to make the miracle greater.

rashi.heb:
*וְיִצְקוּ.* 
אֱלִישָׁע (יָצַק) עַל יָדָיו, וְנַעֲשׂוּ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו כְּמַעְיָנוֹת וְנִתְמַלְּאָה הַתְּעָלָה, הוּא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: פֹּה אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן שָׁפָט אֲשֶׁר יָצַק מַיִם עַל יְדֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ, וְנַעֲשָׂה נֵס בַּמַּיִם עַל יָדָיו, רָאוּי הוּא שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂה הַנֵּס בַּמַּיִם עַל יָדָיו.
rashi.eng: *and pour.* Elisha poured on his hands, and his fingers became like springs, and the trench became full. This is the meaning of what is stated (II Kings 3:11): “Here is Elisha the son of Shaphat who poured water on Elijah’s hands, and a miracle took place with the water through him.” He is fit that a miracle should take place with water through him.

notes.1051: (tn, Heb): “at the offering up of the offering.”
notes.1052: (tn): The words “the altar” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*וּבִדְבָרְךָ עָשִׂיתִי.* 
שֶׁהִקְרַבְתִּי בַּבָּמָה בִּשְׁעַת אִסּוּר הַבָּמוֹת.
rashi.eng: *and at Your word I have done.* that I sacrificed on a high place at the time of the prohibition of high places.

notes.1055: (tn, Heb): “that you are turning their heart[s] back.”

rashi.heb:
*עֲנֵנִי ה' עֲנֵנִי.* 
עֲנֵנִי בָּאֵשׁ, עֲנֵנִי בַּמָּטָר, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: עֲנֵנִי בָּאֵשׁ (וּבַמַּיִם), עֲנֵנִי שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ מַעֲשֵׂה כְשָׁפִים הֵם.
rashi.eng: *Answer me, O Lord, Answer me.* Answer me with fire, answer me with rain. So did Jonathan render this. Our Rabbis, however, said: Answer me with fire, answer me that they do not say that these deeds were accomplished by sorcery.

rashi.heb:
*וְיֵדְעוּ וְגוֹ' כִּי אַתָּה ה'.* 
וַאֲנִי עַבְדֶּךָ. וּכְשֶׁתִּשְׁלָחֵנִי לְבַשְּׂרָם לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, יַאֲמִינוּ בִּי אִם הַיּוֹם תַּעֲנֵנִי.
rashi.eng: *shall know that You are the Lord.* and I am Your servant, and when You send me to bring them tidings [of the forthcoming redemption], they will believe me if You answer me today.

rashi.heb:
*וְאַתָּה הֲסִבֹּתָ אֶת לִבָּם.* 
נָתַתָּ לָהֶם מָקוֹם לָסוּר מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ, וּבְיָדְךָ הָיָה לְהָכִין לְבָבָם אֵלֶיךָ. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: אִם לֹא תַּעֲנֵנִי, אַף אֲנִי אֶהְיֶה כּוֹפֵר וְאוֹמֵר, אַתָּה הֲסִבּוֹתָ אֶת לִבָּם, וְכֵן אָמַר משֶׁה: אִם כְּמוֹת כָּל הָאָדָם יְמוּתוּן אֵלֶּה, אַף אֲנִי כּוֹפֵר וְאוֹמֵר, לֹא ה' שְׁלָחַנִי לְדַבֵּר אֶת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְוֹת, וְכָךְ אָמַר מִיכַיְהוּ: אִם שׁוֹב תָּשׁוּב בְּשָׁלוֹם, לֹא דִּבֵּר ה' בִּי.
rashi.eng: *and You have turned their hearts backwards.* You have given them a place to turn away from following You, although You were able to direct their hearts toward You. And according to Midrash Agadah, if You do not answer me, I will deny and say, You turned their hearts. And so did Moses say (Num. 16:29), “If these people die the death of all men, I, too, will deny and I will say that the Lord did not send me to speak [the words of] the Torah and the commandments,” and so said Micaiah (below 22:28), “If you return safely, God did not speak through me.”

notes.1056: (tn): The words “from the sky” are added for stylistic reasons.

notes.1057: (tn, Heb): “the God” (the phrase occurs twice in this verse).

rashi.heb:
*ה' הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים.* 
וְלֹא הַבַּעַל הָאֱלֹהִים.
rashi.eng: *The Lord is God.* and the Baal is not God.

notes.1059: (tn, Heb): “for [there is] the sound of the roar of the rain.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּגְהַר אַרְצָה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) וּגְחִין לְאַרְעָא, לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים.
rashi.eng: *and he crouched on the ground.* And he crouched on the ground to pray for rain.

notes.1060: (sn): So he went on up, looked, and reported, “There is nothing.” Several times in this chapter those addressed by Elijah obey his orders. In vv. 20 and 42 Ahab does as instructed, in vv. 26 and 28 the prophets follow Elijah’s advice, and in vv. 30, 34, 40 and 43 the people and servants do as they are told. By juxtaposing Elijah’s commands with accounts of those commands being obeyed, the narrator emphasizes the authority of the Lord’s prophet.

rashi.heb:
*דֶּרֶךְ יָם.* 
אִם תִּרְאֶה עָנָן עוֹלֶה מִן הַיָּם.
rashi.eng: *toward the sea.* If you see a cloud ascending from the sea.

notes.1062: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the servant) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1063: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1064: (tn, Heb): “so that the rain won’t restrain you.”

rashi.heb:
*אֱסֹר וָרֵד.* 
אֱסֹר מַרְכְּבוֹתֶיךָ וְרֵד מַהֵר הַכַּרְמֶל לָשׁוּב לְבֵיתְךָ, פֶּן יִדְחַק אוֹתְךָ הַגֶּשֶׁם בַּדֶּרֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *Hitch up and descend.* Hitch up your chariots and descend quickly from Mt. Carmel, to return to your house, lest the rain oppress you on the way.

rashi.heb:
*עַד כֹּה וְעַד כֹּה.* 
בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁהָלַךְ הַשָּׁלִיחַ וּבְתוֹךְ שֶׁאָסַר הַמֶּרְכָּבָה, וְהַשָּׁמַיִם הִתְקַדְּרוּ.
rashi.eng: *Meanwhile.* While the messenger went, and while he hitched up the chariot, the heavens grew dark.

notes.1066: (tn, Heb): “and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah.”
notes.1067: (tn, Heb): “and girded up his loins.” The idea is that of gathering up the robes and tucking them into the sash or belt so that they do not get in the way of the legs when running (or working or fighting).

rashi.heb:
*וְיַד ה'.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) רוּחַ גְּבוּרָה מִן קֳדָם ה', נִתְלַבֵּשׁ כֹּחַ לָרוּץ לִפְנֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה בְּרַגְלָיו, שֶׁלֹּא יֵלֵךְ אַחְאָב יְחִידִי, שֶׁחָלַק כָּבוֹד לַמַּלְכוּת.
rashi.eng: *And a spirit of strength from the Lord.* A spirit of strength from before the Lord. He became invested with strength to run before the chariot on foot, so that Ahab would not go alone, for he paid regards to royalty.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְשַׁנֵּס מָתְנָיו.* 
כְּמוֹ וַיֶּאֱזֹר, וְאֵין לוֹ דִמְיוֹן, וְאַף הוּא לֹא בָּא אֶלָּא לְלַמֵּד לְשׁוֹן זֵרוּז, נִזְדָּרֵז כְּגִבּוֹר.
rashi.eng: *and he girded his loins.* Heb. וישנס, like ויאזר, yet there is no similar word [in the Bible], and even this one came only to teach us an expression of quickness, i.e., he was as quick as a strong man.

notes.1069: (tn, Heb): “So may the gods do to me, and so may they add.”
notes.1070: (tn, Heb): “I do not make your life like the life of one of them.”

rashi.heb:
*כֹּה יַעֲשׂוּן אֱלֹהִים.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשִׂיתָ לִנְבִיאֵי הַבַּעַל.
rashi.eng: *So may the gods do.* as you have done to the prophets of the Baal.

notes.1071: (tc): The MT has “and he saw,” but some medieval Hebrew mss as well as several ancient versions support the reading “he was afraid.” The consonantal text (וַיַּרְא, vayyar’) is ambiguous and can be vocalized וַיַּרְא (from רָאָה, ra’ah, “to see”) or וַיִּרָא (vayyira’, from יָרֵא, yare’, “to fear”).

notes.1073: (tn, Heb): “and asked with respect to his life to die.”

rashi.heb:
*רֹתֶם.* 
ייניבר"א בְּלַעַ"ז (עַרְעָר קוֹצָנִי).
rashi.eng: *genevrier.* or genievre in French, a juniper tree.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר רַב.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) סַגִּי לִי אַרְכָּא, עַד אֵימָתַי אֲנָא מַטְרַף כְּדֵין.
rashi.eng: *and requested that his soul die.* He said, "Enough. My long life is enough. Until when will I be confused like this?"

rashi.heb:
*רְצָפִים.* 
פֶּחָמִים, וְכֵן: וּבְיָדוֹ רִצְפָּה.
rashi.eng: *coals.* Heb. רצפים, charcoal, and similarly, (Isaiah 6: 6) “and in his hand was a coal (רצפה).”

notes.1078: (tn, Heb): “for the journey is too great for you.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶל הַמְּעָרָה.* 
הִיא נִקְרַת צוּר שֶׁעָמַד בָּהּ משֶׁה.
rashi.eng: *to the cave.* That is the cleft of the rock where Moses stood (Ex. 33:22).

notes.1079: (tn): Or “very zealous.” The infinitive absolute preceding the finite verb emphasizes the degree of his zeal and allegiance.
notes.1082: (tn, Heb): “and they are seeking my life to take it.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶת מִזְבְּחֹתֶיךָ הָרָסוּ.* 
בָּמוֹת יָחִיד הַנַּעֲשׂוֹת לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, שֶׁהֲרֵי מִזְבַּח בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם הָיָה.
rashi.eng: *They have torn down Your altars.* The private high places that were built in the Name of Heaven, for the altar of the Temple was in Jerusalem.

notes.1083: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1084: (tn, Heb): “tearing away the mountains and breaking the cliffs” (or perhaps, “breaking the stones”).

rashi.heb:
*וְרוּחַ גְּדוֹלָה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) מַשִּׁרְיַת מַלְאֲכֵי רוּחָא.
rashi.eng: *and a great… wind.* A camp of angels of the wind.

rashi.heb:
*בְּרַעַשׁ.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) מַשִּׁרְיַת מַלְאֲכֵי זִיעָא.
rashi.eng: *an earthquake.* A camp of angels of earthquake.

rashi.heb:
*אֵשׁ.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) מַשִּׁרְיַת מַלְאֲכֵי אֶשָּׁתָא.
rashi.eng: *a fire.* A camp of angels of fire.

rashi.heb:
*קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) קָל דִּמְשַׁבְּחִין בַּחֲשַׁאי, אֲבָל בִּנְבִיאֵי אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אוֹמֵר: דְּמָמָה וְקוֹל אֶשְׁמַע, דְּמָמָה הָיְתָה לְשַׁבֵּחַ. וַאֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי קוֹל הַבָּא מִתּוֹךְ הַדְּמָמָה, דטינטישמנ"ט בְּלַעַ"ז (הֵד), וְאֵין שׁוֹמְעִין הַקּוֹל מַמָּשׁ.
rashi.eng: *a still small sound.* A voice of those praising quietly, but concerning the prophets of the nations, Scripture states: (Job 4:16) “Silence and a voice I hear”; there was silence to the praising, but I heard the voice coming out of the silence, retentissement in O.F., resounding, but no one heard the voice itself.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּלֶט פָּנָיו.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) וְכָרִיךְ אַפּוֹהִי, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: לוּטָה בַשִּׂמְלָה.
rashi.eng: *he wrapped his face.* Jonathan renders: כריך אפוהי, and so Scripture says: “wrapped in a garment (לוטה בשמלה)” (I Sam. 21:10).

notes.1087: (tn): Or “very zealous.” The infinitive absolute preceding the finite verb emphasizes the degree of his zeal and allegiance.
notes.1090: (tn, Heb): “and they are seeking my life to take it.”

rashi.heb:
*תִּמְשַׁח לְנָבִיא תַּחְתֶּיךָ.* 
אִי אֶפְשִׁי בִּנְבִיאוּתְךָ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאַתָּה מְלַמֵּד קָטֵּיגוֹרְיָא עַל בָּנַי.
rashi.eng: *you shall anoint to be prophet in your stead.* I do not want your prophecy since you plead for the prosecution of My children.

rashi.heb:
*יָמִית אֱלִישָׁע.* 
לֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁהֵמִית אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁנַיִם יְלָדִים עַל יְדֵי הַדֻּבִּים בִּירִיחוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Elisha will kill.* We do not find that Elisha killed anyone except the forty-two children through the bears in Jericho (II Kings 2:24).

notes.1091: (tn, Heb): “I have kept in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and all the mouths that have not kissed him.”

notes.1092: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*לֵךְ שׁוּב.* 
מֵאַחֲרַי.
rashi.eng: *Go, return.* from following me.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי מֶה עָשִׂיתִי לָךְ.* 
שֶׁתָּבוֹא אַחֲרַי.
rashi.eng: *for what have I done to you.* that you should follow me.

notes.1093: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1094: (tn, Heb): “and with the equipment of the oxen he cooked them, the flesh.”

rashi.heb:
*בִּשְּׁלָם הַבָּשָׂר.* 
בִּשֵּׁל לָהֶם אֶת הַבָּשָׂר, כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּ דוֹנַ"שׁ וּמְנַחֵם, וְכֵן תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן בִּשְׁתֵּי תֵבוֹת (בָּשִׁיל לְהוֹן). וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, אֵין צָרִיךְ לְחַלְּקוֹ לִשְׁתֵּי תֵבוֹת, וּמַהוּ בִּשְּׁלָם הַבָּשָׂר, בִּשְּׁלָם לִשְׁנֵי הַשְּׁוָרִים אֶת הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁלָּהֶם, שֶׁהַצֶּמֶד אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם.
rashi.eng: *he cooked the meat for them.* Heb. בִּשְׁלָם הַבָּשָׂר. The mem of bishelam [is usually indicative of the direct object, to be rendered,] he cooked them. [In this case, however, since the object is] habassar, [the meat, we render:] he cooked for them the meat, so Dunash and Menahem (Machbereth Menahem, p. 48) explain, and so did Jonathan render this in two words. [‘bashilu lehon,’ he cooked for them.] I say, however, that it is unnecessary to divide it into two words [i.e., to add the preposition to]. Now what is the meaning of בִּשְׁלָם הַבָּשָׂר? He cooked the two oxen, their flesh; [i.e., he cooked them, viz. their flesh.] For the yoke is no fewer than two. [Therefore the plural suffix is used.]

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּתֵּן לָעָם.* 
מֵרֹב שִׂמְחָה עָשָׂה מִשְׁתֶּה.
rashi.eng: *and he gave the people.* Out of great joy, he made a feast.

notes.1095: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
notes.1096: (tn, Heb): “and he went up and besieged Samaria and fought against it.”

rashi.heb:
*כִּי שָׁלַחְתִּי אֵלֶיךָ וְגוֹ' לִי תִתֵּן.* 
יָדַעְתִּי כִּי תִתְּנֵם לִי, אֲבָל אַחֶרֶת אֲנִי גּוֹזֵר עָלֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *As I have sent to you, saying, Your silver… you shall give to me..* As I have sent to you… you will give to me I know that you will give to me, but another thing I am decreeing upon you.

notes.1098: (tn, Heb): “all that is desirable to your eyes they will put in their hand and take.”

rashi.heb:
*כָּל מַחְמַד עֵינֶיךָ יָשִׂימוּ בְיָדָם וְלָקְחוּ.* 
וַהֲלֹא כָּל הָרִאשׁוֹנִים דִּבְרֵי חֶמְדָּה הֵם, אֶלָּא מַהוּ מַחְמַד עֵינֶיךָ, חֶמְדָּה מִתּוֹךְ חֶמְדָּה, זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: הַנֶּחֱמָדִים מִזָּהָב וּמִפַּז רַב, אָמַר אַחְאָב בְּלִבּוֹ, דָּבָר גָּדוֹל זֶה מְבַקֵּשׁ, אֵין זֶה שֶׁלִּי לְבַדִּי, שֶׁל זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא, לְפִיכָךְ: וַיִּקְרָא לְכָל זִקְנֵי הָאָרֶץ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹבְדִין עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הָיוּ מְכַבְּדִין אֶת הַתּוֹרָה.
rashi.eng: *anything you prize.* [lit. anything desirable to your eyes.] Now were not the first things desirable things? What, then, is the meaning of “anything you prize” ? This means a prize within a prize [i.e., a possession prized more than any other prized possessions.] This is the sefer Torah, concerning which it is written, “… that are prized more than gold and much fine gold” (Ps. 19:11). Said Ahab to himself, He demands a great thing. This is not mine alone; this belongs to the elders of Israel. He, therefore, summoned all the elders of the land. Even though they worshipped idols, they respected the Torah.

notes.1100: (tn, Heb): “Know and see that this [man] is seeking trouble.”

notes.1101: (tn, Heb): “Do not listen and do not be willing.”

notes.1102: (tn, Heb): “all which you sent to your servant in the beginning I will do, but this thing I am unable to do.”

notes.1103: (tn, Heb): “So may the gods do to me, and so may they add.”
notes.1104: (tn, Heb): “if the dirt of Samaria suffices for the handfuls of all the people who are at my feet.”

rashi.heb:
*אִם יִשְׂפֹּק עֲפַר שֹׁמְרוֹן לִשְׁעָלִים וְגוֹ'.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) לְמֵיסַב בִּשְׁעוֹלֵי פַרְסַת רַגְלֵי עַמָּא דְעִמִּי, עָפָר שֶׁנִּדְבַּק בְּפַרְסַת רַגְלַיִם.
rashi.eng: *if the earth will suffice for the footsteps.* [Jonathan renders:] To take with the footsteps of all the people who are with me, i.e., earth that adheres to the sole of the feet for the footsteps.

rashi.heb:
*לִשְׁעָלִים.* 
לְשׁוֹן מִדְרַךְ כַּף רָגֶל, וְכֵן: בְּמִשְׁעוֹל הַכְּרָמִים; וְכֵן: מִי מָדַד בְּשָׁעֳלוֹ מַיִם, שֶׁדָּרַךְ בְּיַם סוּף, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר דָּרַכְתָּ בַּיָּם סוּסֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *the footsteps.* לשעלים is an expression of treading with the sole of the foot, similarly, (Num. 22:24) במשעול הכרמים, “in a path between the vineyards.” And similarly (Is. 40:12): מי מדד בשעלו מים, “Who measured the water with his step,” for he trod in the Sea of Reeds, as it is stated: (Hab. 3:15) “You trod in the sea with Your horses.”

rashi.heb:
*אִם יִשְׂפֹּק.* 
אִם יֵשׁ דַּי.
rashi.eng: *will suffice.* Heb. אם ישפק, if there is enough.

notes.1105: (sn): The point of the saying is that someone who is still preparing for a battle should not boast as if he has already won the battle. A modern parallel would be, “Don’t count your chickens before they’re hatched.”

rashi.heb:
*דַּבְּרוּ אַל יִתְהַלֵּל חִגֵּר כִּמְפַתֵּחַ.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) אֱמַרוּ לֵהּ, לָא יִשְׁתַּבַּח דְּמִזְדְּרֵז וְנָחִית בִּקְרָבָא, כִּגְבָר דְּנַצַּח וְסָלִיק מִנַּהּ. אַל יִתְהַלֵּל הַחוֹגֵר חַרְבּוֹ לָרֶדֶת לַמִּלְחָמָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם יְנַצַּח אִם לָאו.
rashi.eng: *Say, One who girds himself with the sword shall not boast as one who unties the sword.* Say to him, One who girds himself and goes down to war shall not boast like a man who has been victorious and is coming up from it. One who girds his sword to go down to war, who does not know whether he will be victorious or not, should not boast.

rashi.heb:
*כִּמְפַתֵּחַ.* 
חֲגוֹרַת חַרְבּוֹ, שֶׁעָלָה כְּבָר מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה וְנִצַּח, כָּךְ אֵין לַאֲדוֹנֵיכֶם לְהִתְהַלֵּל בִּדְבַר הֶעָתִיד.
rashi.eng: *as one who ungirds the girdle of his sword,.* who has already come up from the war victorious. Similarly, your master should not boast concerning a future thing.

notes.1107: (tn, Heb): “in the temporary shelters.” This is probably referring to tents.

rashi.heb:
*שִׂימוּ.* 
כְּלֵי הַמָּצוֹר עַל הָעִיר.
rashi.eng: *Lay on.* the implements of siege against the city.

rashi.heb:
*נָבִיא אֶחָד.* 
הוּא מִיכַיְהוּ בֶּן יִמְלָה.
rashi.eng: *a certain prophet.* That was Micaiah the son of Imlah.

notes.1109: (tn): The words “will this be accomplished” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1110: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*בְּנַעֲרֵי שָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת.* 
הֵם בְּנֵי הַתַּעֲרוֹבוֹת, שֶׁהָיוּ כָּל הַשָּׂרִים שֶׁל שְׁאָר הָאֻמּוֹת נוֹתְנִים בְּנֵיהֶם תַּחַת יָדוֹ עֲרֵבִים, שֶׁלֹּא יִמְרְדוּ בוֹ.
rashi.eng: *With the youths of the governors of the providence..* They are the hostages for all the princes of the other nations would give their children into his custody lest they rebel against him.

rashi.heb:
*מִי יֶאְסֹר הַמִּלְחָמָה.* 
יַעֲרֹךְ לְצַוּוֹת אוֹתָהּ.
rashi.eng: *Who will commandeer the war?.* Who will array [the battle] to command it.

rashi.heb:
*אָתָּה.* 
צֵא אַתָּה תְּחִלָּה וְכֹה תְמִיתֶנּוּ (וְעַתָּה תָּרִיעוּ).
rashi.eng: *You.* You go forth first and so you shall kill him. [According to Shem Ephraim, the reading is:] And you shall not wait, and you shall array [the battle].

notes.1111: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1112: (tn, Heb): “after them he assembled all the people, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand.”

rashi.heb:
*שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים.* 
אוֹמֵר אֲנִי, הֵם שֶׁאָמַר עֲלֵיהֶם: כָּל הַבִּרְכַּיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא כָרְעוּ לַבַּעַל שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים.
rashi.eng: *seven thousand.* I say that they are the ones concerning whom Scripture stated (above 19:18), “all the knees that did not kneel to the Baal, seven thousand.”

notes.1114: (tn, Heb): “in the temporary shelters.” This is probably referring to tents.

rashi.heb:
*בַּסֻּכּוֹת.* 
שֶׁעָשׂוּ לָהֶם מִפְּנֵי הַחַמָּה.
rashi.eng: *in the pavilions.* that they had made for themselves because of the sun.

notes.1115: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

notes.1116: (tn, Heb): “if they come in peace, take them alive; if they come for battle, take them alive.”

notes.1118: (tn, Heb): “struck down Aram with a great striking down.”

notes.1119: (tn): The definite article indicates previous reference, that is, “the prophet mentioned earlier” (see v. 13).
notes.1122: (tn, Heb): “at the turning of the year.”

rashi.heb:
*לִתְשׁוּבַת הַשָּׁנָה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) לִזְמַן סוֹפָא דְּשַׁתָּא.
rashi.eng: *at the return of the year.* at the time of the end of the year.

rashi.heb:
*וְשִׂים פָּחוֹת תַּחְתֵּיהֶם.* 
מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מִמִּשְׁפָּחָה רָמָה, יִתְּנוּ לֵב לְהִתְחַזֵּק, כְּדֵי לִמְצֹא חֵן.
rashi.eng: *and place officers in their place.* Since they are not of a highborn family, they will endeavor to exert themselves in order to find favor.

notes.1125: (tn, Heb): “And you, you muster an army like the one that fell from you, horse like horse and chariot like chariot.”
notes.1126: (tn, Heb): “he listened to their voice and did so.”

rashi.heb:
*אִם לֹא נֶחֱזַק מֵהֶם.* 
כְּלוֹמַר, וְתִרְאֶה אִם לֹא נֶחֱזַק מֵהֶם.
rashi.eng: *if we will not overpower them.* i.e., and you will see if we will not overpower them.

notes.1127: (tn, Heb): “at the turning of the year.”
notes.1129: (tn, Heb): “and went up to Aphek for battle with Israel.”

notes.1130: (tn): The noun translated “small flocks” occurs only here. The common interpretation derives the word from the verbal root חשׂף, “to strip off; to make bare.” In this case the noun refers to something “stripped off” or “made bare.” HALOT 359 s.v. II חשׂף derives the noun from a proposed homonymic verbal root (which occurs only in Ps 29:9) meaning “cause a premature birth.” In this case the derived noun could refer to goats that are undersized because they are born prematurely.

rashi.heb:
*וְכָלְכְּלוּ.* 
פַּרְנָסַת צֵדָה לַמִּלְחָמָה הִצְטַיְּדוּ, הֵם כְּלֵי זַיִן וְכָל צָרְכֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה.
rashi.eng: *and provisioned.* provided with supplies for the war; they armed themselves with weapons and all necessities of war.

rashi.heb:
*וְכָלְכְּלוּ.* 
נִתְכַּלְכְּלוּ.
rashi.eng: *and provisioned.* they were sustained.

rashi.heb:
*כִּשְׁנֵי חֲשִׂפֵי עִזִּים.* 
קְבוּצֵי עִזִּים, וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ בִּלְשׁוֹן גִּלּוּי, כְּמוֹ: מַחְשׂוֹף הַלָּבָן: חֶשְׂפִּי שׁוֹבֶל, וּלְשׁוֹן גִּלּוּי נוֹפֵל עַל עֶדְרֵי עִזִּים, כְּמוֹ: שֶׁגָּלְשׁוּ מֵהַר גִּלְעָד, כְּשֶׁיּוֹרְדִין מִן הָהָר, נִתְגַּלֶּה הָהָר.
rashi.eng: *like two flocks of goats.* Heb. עזים חשפי, flocks of goats, although there is no comparison [in the Bible]. Menahem, however, classifies this with the expression of revelation, like (Gen. 30:37) מַחשּׁוף הלבן“laying bare the white”; (Is. 47:2) חשפי שבל “uncover your locks.” The expression of revelation fits with flocks of goats, like (Song of Songs 4:1) “… who bared Mt. Gilead.” When they come down from the mountain, it is bared [or revealed].

notes.1132: (tn, Heb): “I will place all this great horde in your hand.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר וְגוֹ'.* 
אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיֹּאמֶר וַיֹּאמֶר, צָרִיךְ לִדְרשׁ. אֲמִירָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, אָמַר לוֹ וְנָתַתִּי אֶת כָּל הֶהָמוֹן הַזֶּה בְּיָדֶךָ, אֲמִירָה שְׁנִיָּה, אִם יִפֹּל בֶּן הֲדַד בְּיָדְךָ אַל תַחֲמֹל עָלָיו, לְפִיכָךְ כְּשֶׁחָמַל עָלָיו אָמַר לוֹ: יַעַן שִׁלַּחְתָּ אֶת אִישׁ חֶרְמִי מִיָּד וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *and said to the king of Israel. And he said.* Said R. Johanan: Every place wherein it is stated, And he said… and he said, must be expounded. The first saying [refers to what] he said to him, “… I will deliver all the great multitude into your hand…” The second saying [alludes to an admonition that], “if Ben-Hadad falls into your hands, show him no clemency.” Therefore, when he took pity on him, he said to him (v.42) “Since you released the man I had designated for destruction…”

notes.1133: (tn, Heb): “and the remaining ones fled to Aphek to the city and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand men, the ones who remained.”
notes.1134: (tn, Heb): “and Ben Hadad fled and went into the city, [into] an inner room in an inner room.”

notes.1136: (tn): Or “merciful.” The word used here often means “devoted” or “loyal.” Perhaps the idea is that the Israelite kings are willing to make treaties with other kings.
notes.1137: (sn): Sackcloth was worn as a sign of sorrow and repentance. The precise significance of the ropes on the head is uncertain, but it probably was a sign of submission. These actions were comparable to raising a white flag on the battlefield or throwing in the towel in a boxing match.

notes.1139: (sn): Your servant. By referring to Ben Hadad as Ahab’s servant, they are suggesting that Ahab make him a subject in a vassal treaty arrangement.
notes.1140: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1141: (sn): He is my brother. Ahab’s response indicates that he wants to make a parity treaty and treat Ben Hadad as an equal partner.

notes.1142: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Ahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*יְנַחֲשׁוּ וַיְמַהֲרוּ וַיַּחְלְטוּ הֲמִמֶּנּוּ.* 
יְנַחֲשׁוּ לְשׁוֹן מְנַחֵשׁ, אָמְרוּ כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּפְלוּ דִּבְרֵי שָׁלוֹם בְּפִיו אֲפִלּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִתְכַּוֵּן, סִימָן טוֹב הוּא זֶה, וַיְמַהֲרוּ לְהַחֲזִיק הַדָּבָר.
rashi.eng: *took it for an omen, and they hastened and caught it from him.* Heb. יְנַחֲשׁוּ is an expression of divining. They said: Since words of peace fell from his mouth, even inadvertently, it is a good sign, and they hastened to confirm the matter.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּחְלְטוּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן: צְמִיתוּת, כָּרְתוּ הַדָּבָר מִפִּיו שֶׁלֹּא יַחֲזֹר בּוֹ, וְהַהֵ"א שֶׁל הֲמִמֶּנּוּ נוֹטֶה בְּמָסֹרֶת לִשְׁתֵּי הַתֵּבוֹת, כְּאִלּוּ נִכְתַּב וַיַּחְלְטוּהָ מִמֶּנּוּ, אִם מִמֶּנּוּ יֵצֵא הַדָּבָר בְּכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב.

notes.1143: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Ben Hadad) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1144: (tn, Heb): “streets,” but this must refer to streets set up with stalls for merchants to sell their goods. See HALOT 299 s.v. חוּץ.
notes.1145: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
notes.1146: (tn, Heb): “I will send you away with a treaty.” The words “Ahab then said” are supplied in the translation. There is nothing in the Hebrew text to indicate that the speaker has changed from Ben Hadad to Ahab. Some suggest adding “and he said” before “I will send you away.” Others prefer to maintain Ben Hadad as the speaker and change the statement to, “Please send me away with a treaty.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו.* 
בֶּן הֲדַד, הֶעָרִים אֲשֶׁר לָקַח אָבִי מֵאֵת אָבִיךָ עָמְרִי, אָשִׁיב לְךָ.
rashi.eng: *And he said to him.* i.e., Ben-Hadad said to Ahab, The cities that my father took from your father Omri, I will return to you.

rashi.heb:
*וְחוּצוֹת תָּשִׂים לְךָ בְדַמֶּשֶׂק.* 
וּתְהִי מוֹשֵׁל בָּהּ, וְהִיא רֹאשׁ לְמַלְכוּתִי.
rashi.eng: *and you shall make streets for yourself in Damascus.* and rule therein, although it is the capital of my kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂם אָבִי בְּשֹׁמְרוֹן.* 
עִירְךָ עַל כָּרְחֲךָ, וְכָל זֶה הָיָה אוֹמֵר מִיִּרְאָה, אָמַר לוֹ אַחְאָב, וַאֲנִי בַּבְּרִית הַזֹּאת אֲשַׁלְּחֶ§.
rashi.eng: *as my father had made in Samaria.* your city against your will. He was saying all this out of fear. Said Ahab to him, And I will, with this treaty, release you.

notes.1147: (tn, Heb): “Now a man from the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the Lord, ‘Wound me.’”

rashi.heb:
*הַכֵּנִי נָא.* 
סִימָן זֶה רַע עַל אַחְאָב, שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַנָּבִיא עַל פִּי הַגְּבוּרָה לְהַכּוֹת אֶת בֶּן הֲדַד וְלֹא הִכָּהוּ. וְאַף זֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַנָּבִיא בִּדְבַר ה' הַכֵּנִי, וְלֹא הִכָּהוּ, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּפְרַע מִזֶּה, יִפָּרַע מֵאַחְאָב.
rashi.eng: *Strike me now.* This sign was bad for Ahab, for the prophet said to him by the word of the Lord to kill Ben-Hadad, and he did not kill him. Also, this one to whom the prophet said by the word of the Lord, “Strike me,” and he did not strike him, just as He punished him, he would punish Ahab.

rashi.heb:
*בִּדְבַר ה'.* 
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר שֶׁתַּכֶּה אוֹתִי.
rashi.eng: *By the word of the Lord.* The Holy One, blessed be He, said that you shall strike me.

notes.1148: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.1149: (tn, Heb): “and the man wounded him, wounding and bruising.”

rashi.heb:
*וּפָצֹע.* 
מַכַּת חַבּוּרָה.
rashi.eng: *and wounding him.* [He struck him] a wounding blow.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ בָּאֲפֵר.* 
שִׁנָּה אֶת מַעְפָּרְתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּהוּ, כָּל שִׁנּוּי בְּגָדִים הוּא לְשׁוֹן חִפּוּשׂ.
rashi.eng: *and he disguised himself with his headband.* He changed his headband so that they would not recognize him. Any change of clothes is an expression of disguise.

rashi.heb:
*בָּאֲפֵר.* 
תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן: בְּמַעֲפָרָא, הוּא סוּדָר.
rashi.eng: *with his headband.* Heb. באפר. Jonathan rendered this במעפרה, [that is] a headband.

notes.1151: (tn, Heb): “man” (also a second time later in this verse).
notes.1152: (tn, Heb): “if being missed, he is missed.” The emphatic infinitive absolute before the finite verbal form lends solemnity to the warning.
notes.1153: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 75 pounds of silver.
notes.1154: (tn, Heb): “your life will be in place of his life, or a unit of silver you will pay.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ סָר.* 
מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֵלַי.
rashi.eng: *and behold, a man turned aside.* from the road to me.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּבֵא אֵלַי אִישׁ.* 
שָׁבוּי מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה.
rashi.eng: *and he brought to me a man.* a prisoner of war.

rashi.heb:
*אִם הִפָּקֵד יִפָּקֵד.* 
אִם יִבְרַח, לְשׁוֹן: לֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ, לְשׁוֹן חִסָּרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *if he will be missing.* If he escapes, an expression similar to (Num. 31: 49) “and no man was missing from us (ולא נפקדו);” an expression of a lack.

notes.1155: (tn, Heb): “so [i.e., in accordance with his testimony] is your judgment, you have determined [it].”

rashi.heb:
*וְהוּא אֵינֶנּוּ.* 
בָּרַח לוֹ.
rashi.eng: *and he was gone.* He ran away.

rashi.heb:
*אַתָּה חָרַצְתָּ.* 
אוֹ נֶפֶשׁ, אוֹ כִּכַּר כֶּסֶף.
rashi.eng: *you have pronounced it.* Either your life or a talent of silver.

notes.1156: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.1157: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1158: (tn, Heb): “Because you sent away the man of my destruction [i.e., that I determined should be destroyed] from [my/your?] hand, your life will be in place of his life, and your people in place of his people.”

rashi.heb:
*אִישׁ חֶרְמִי.* 
אִישׁ מִלְחַמְתִּי, לְשׁוֹן חֵירוּם, וּלְשׁוֹן חֵירוּם נוֹפֵל בְּמִלְחָמָה, וְכֵן: עַל אֱדוֹם תֵּרֵד וְעַל עַם חֶרְמִי. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה כַּמָּה מְצוּדוֹת וַחֲרָמִים פָּרַשְׂתִּי לְךָ עַד שֶׁנָּפַל בְּיָדְךָ.
rashi.eng: *the man whom I designated for destruction.* the man of My war, an expression of חרם, strife. Now, the expression of strife fits with war, and similarly, (Is. 34:5) “… on Edom it will descend and on the nation with whom I war (חרמי).” [Thus we render, “the man with whom I war.” [According to the] Midrash Aggadah: Many traps and nets have I spread for you until he fell into your hand.

notes.1159: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

rashi.heb:
*סָר וְזָעֵף.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) נְסִיס וְדַוָּי, רוּחוֹ סָרָה מִמֶּנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *sad and upset.* Heb. סר וזעף. [Jonathan renders:] נסים ודוי, his spirit turned away from him. [These are expressions of sadness.] His spirit turned away from him.

notes.1160: (tn, Heb): “after these things.” The words “the following episode took place” are added for stylistic reasons.
notes.1161: (sn): King Ahab of Samaria. Samaria, as the capital of the northern kingdom, here stands for the nation of Israel. For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה.* 
עוֹד אַחֶרֶת לְקָרֵב מִיתָתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And it was after these happenings.* [lit. after these things,] still another incident to bring his death close.

notes.1162: (tn, Heb): “if it is good in your eyes.”
notes.1163: (tc): The Old Greek translation includes the following words: “And it will be mine as a garden of herbs.”

rashi.heb:
*מְחִיר זֶה.* 
הַכֶּרֶם הַזֶּה.
rashi.eng: *its worth.* [lit. the worth of this, i.e.,] the worth of this vineyard.

notes.1164: (tn, Heb): “Far be it from me, by the Lord, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you.”

notes.1165: (tn, Heb): “on account of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite spoke to him.”
notes.1166: (tn, Heb): “I will not give to you the inheritance of my fathers.”

notes.1168: (tn, Heb): “While I was talking…, I said…, he said….” Ahab’s explanation is one lengthy sentence in the Hebrew text, which is divided in the English translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.1169: (tn, Heb): “You, now, you are exercising kingship over Israel.”
notes.1170: (tn, Heb): “so your heart [i.e., disposition] might be well.”

notes.1175: (tn, Heb): “to the nobles who were in his city, the ones who lived with Naboth.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶל הַזְּקֵנִים.* 
זִקְנֵי אַשְׁמַאי, סָבֵי דְבַהֲתָא.
rashi.eng: *to the elders.* wicked and ignorant elders, elders of shame.

notes.1176: (tn, Heb): “she wrote on the scrolls, saying.”

rashi.heb:
*קִרְאוּ צוֹם.* 
וּבְיוֹם צוֹם דַּרְכָּם לִבְדֹּק בַּעֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדָם.
rashi.eng: *Proclaim a fast.* On a fast day it was their custom to search for the sins in their hands.

notes.1179: (tn, Heb): “and the nobles who were living in his city.”
notes.1180: (tn, Heb): “did as Jezebel sent to them, just as was written in the scrolls which she sent to them.”

notes.1182: (tn, Heb): “and they stoned him with stones and he died.”

rashi.heb:
*בֵּרַךְ נָבוֹת.* 
חִלּוּף שֶׁל קְלָלָה, וְתַרְגּוּם: גָּדִיף נָבוֹת קֳדָם ה' וּמַלְכָּא לָט.
rashi.eng: *Naboth cursed.* Heb. ברך, [lit. blessed, a euphemism for קללה,] curse. The Targum renders: Naboth blasphemed against God and cursed the king.

notes.1183: (tn, Heb): “Naboth was stoned and he died.” So also in v. 15.

notes.1184: (tn, Heb): “Jezebel”; the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“she”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*קוּם רֵשׁ.* 
יֵשׁ מֵחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת נִכְסֵיהֶם לַמֶּלֶךְ, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן אוֹמְרִים: בֶּן אֲחִי אָבִיו הָיָה, וְאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו הָרַג, וְרָאוּי לְיָרְשׁוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Get up and take possession.* Some of our Sages say that the property of those executed by the king belong to the king. And some of them say that he [Ahab] was the son of his [Naboth’s] father’s brother. He killed him and his children [as well], and was therefore fit to inherit his [property].

notes.1185: (tc): The Old Greek translation includes the following words here: “he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. After these things.”

notes.1186: (tn, Heb): “the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite.”

notes.1187: (tn, Heb): “and Ahab said to Elijah.” The narrative is elliptical and streamlined. The words “when Elijah arrived” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1188: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*הִתְמַכֶּרְךָ.* 
מָכַרְתָּ אֶת עַצְמְךָ לְהַכְעִיס אֶת בּוֹרַאֲךָ. הִתְמַכֶּרְךָ כְּמוֹ: וְהִתְמַכַּרְתֶּם שָׁם לְאוֹיְבֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *you sold yourself.* You sold yourself to anger your Creator. Heb. התמכרך, you sold yourself [reflexive form] like (Deut. 28:68) והתמכרתם, “and you will sell yourselves there to your enemies.”

notes.1191: (tn): The introductory formula “the Lord says” is omitted in the Hebrew text, but supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.1192: (sn): Disaster. There is a wordplay in the Hebrew text. The word translated “disaster” (רָעָה, ra’ah) is similar to the word translated “evil” (v. 20, הָרַע, hara’). Ahab’s sins would receive an appropriate punishment.
notes.1193: (tn, Heb): “I will burn after you.” Some take the verb בָּעַר (ba’ar) to mean here “sweep away.” See the discussion of this verb in the notes at 14:10 and 16:3.
notes.1194: (tn, Heb): “and I will cut off from Ahab those who urinate against a wall, [including both those who are] restrained and let free [or “abandoned”] in Israel.” The precise meaning of the idiomatic phrase עָצוּר וְעָזוּב (’atsur v�’azuv, translated here “weak and incapacitated”) is uncertain. For various options see HALOT 871 s.v. עצר and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 107. The two terms are usually taken as polar opposites (“slaves and freemen” or “minors and adults”), but Cogan and Tadmor, on the basis of contextual considerations (note the usage with אֶפֶס (’efes), “nothing but”) in Deut 32:36 and 2 Kgs 14:26, argue convincingly that the terms are synonyms, meaning “restrained and abandoned,” and refer to incapable or incapacitated individuals.

notes.1196: (tn, Heb): “because of the provocation by which you angered [me], and you caused Israel to sin.”

notes.1197: (tc): A few Hebrew mss and some ancient versions agree with 2 Kgs 9:10, 36, which reads, “the plot [of ground] at Jezreel.” The Hebrew words translated “outer wall” (חֵל, khel, defectively written here!) and “plot [of ground]” (חֵלֶק, kheleq) are spelled similarly.

rashi.heb:
*בְּחֵל יִזְרְעֶאל.* 
בְּבִקְעַת יִזְרְעֶאל, בְּחֵל, תַּרְגּוּמוֹ שֶׁל גַּיְא.
rashi.eng: *in the valley of Jezreel.* Heb. חל, the Aramaic translation of valley.

notes.1198: (tn): “Dogs will eat the ones who belonging to Ahab who die in the city.”

notes.1201: (tn, Heb): “like Ahab…whom his wife Jezebel incited.”

rashi.heb:
*רַק לֹא הָיָה כְאַחְאָב.* 
הַכָּתוּב מֵעִיד עָלָיו, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בַּמְּלָכִים כְּמוֹתוֹ, שֶׁיָּרָבְעָם וְכָל אֲשֶׁר אַחֲרָיו, עָבְדוּ אֶת הָעֲגָלִים מִיִּרְאָה, אִם יַעֲלֶה הָעָם יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, תָּשׁוּב הַמַּמְלָכָה לְבֵית דָּוִד, וְזֶה הוֹסִיף הַבַּעַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָה לְהַכְעִיס.
rashi.eng: *But there was none like Ahab.* The Scripture testifies concerning him that there was none among the kings like him, for Jeroboam and all those after him worshipped the calves out of fear that if the people would go up to Jerusalem, the kingdom would return to the house of David, but this one [Ahab] added the Baal and the Asherah to anger God.

rashi.heb:
*הִתְמַכֵּר.* 
נִמְכַּר לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. רָאִיתִי בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי חִיאֵל בֵּית הָאֱלִי שׁוֹשְׁבִינוֹ הָיָה, וּבְכָל יוֹם שָׁם דָּמָיו וְנָתַן לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
rashi.eng: *sold himself.* was sold to idolatry. I saw in Yerushalmi that Hiel was his counselor, and every day he [Hiel] would estimate his [Ahab’s] value and he [Ahab] would give it to the pagan deities.

notes.1202: (tn): The Hebrew word used here, גִלּוּלִים (gillulim) is always used as a disdainful reference to idols. It is generally thought to have originally referred to “dung pellets” (cf. KBL 183 s.v. גִלּוּלִים). It is only one of several terms used in this way, such as אֱלִילִים (’elilim, “worthless things”) and הֲבָלִים (havalim, “vanities” or “empty winds”).
notes.1203: (tn, Heb): “He acted very abominably by walking after the disgusting idols, according to all which the Amorites had done.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהַלֵּךְ אַט.* 
יָחֵף.
rashi.eng: *and put sackcloth on his flesh, and he fasted.* he walked barefoot.

notes.1204: (tn, Heb): “the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite.”

notes.1205: (tn): Or “humbles himself.” The expression occurs a second time later in this verse.
notes.1206: (tn, Heb): “I will not bring the disaster during his days, [but] in the days of his son I will bring the disaster on his house.”

rashi.heb:
*לֹא אָבִיא הָרָעָה.* 
רָעַת בֵּיתוֹ לֹא אָבִיא בְּיָמָיו, אֲבָל גְּזֵרַת יָלֹקּוּ הַכְּלָבִים אֶת דָּמוֹ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָבֹא בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ, אֶלָּא עָלָיו.
rashi.eng: *I will not bring the disaster.* i.e., the disaster of his house I will not bring in his days, but the decree that the dogs will lick his blood is impossible to come in the days of his son, but upon him.

notes.1207: (tn, Heb): “and they lived three years without war between Aram and Israel.”

notes.1208: (tn): The word “visit” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁלִישִׁית.* 
שֶׁשָּׁלַח אֶת בֶּן הֲדַד.
rashi.eng: *in the third year.* since he had released Ben-Hadad.

notes.1209: (tn, Heb): “Do you know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us, and we hesitate to take it from the hand of the king of Aram?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course, you must know!”

rashi.heb:
*וַאֲנַחְנוּ מַחְשִׁים.* 
מִתְעַצְּלִים, סיאמ"ו פיגר"י בְּלַעַ"ז (לְהַחֲרִישׁ).
rashi.eng: *and we do nothing.* We are lazy [siamo pigri in Italian].

notes.1210: (tn, Heb): “Like me, like you; like my people, like your people; like my horses; like your horses.”

notes.1211: (tn, Heb): “and Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel.”
notes.1212: (tn, Heb): “the word of the Lord.” Jehoshaphat is requesting a prophetic oracle revealing the Lord’s will in the matter and their prospects for success. For examples of such oracles, see 2 Sam 5:19, 23-24.

notes.1213: (tn, Heb): “Should I go against Ramoth Gilead for war or should I refrain?”
notes.1214: (tn): Though Jehoshaphat requested an oracle from “the Lord” (יְהוָה, Yahweh), they stop short of actually using this name and substitute the title אֲדֹנָי (’adonai, “lord; master”). This ambiguity may explain in part Jehoshaphat’s hesitancy and caution (vv. 7-8). He seems to doubt that the four hundred are genuine prophets of the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*הַאֵין פֹּה נָבִיא לַה' עוֹד.* 
מְקֻבְּלַנִי אֵין שְׁנֵי נְבִיאִים מִתְנַבְּאִים בְּלָשׁוֹן אֶחָד, וְאֵלֶּה כֻּלָּם לָשׁוֹן אֶחָד אוֹמְרִים.
rashi.eng: *Is there no other prophet of the Lord here?.* I have a tradition that no two prophets prophesy with one expression, and these are all saying the same expression.

notes.1215: (tn, Heb): “to seek the Lord from him.”
notes.1217: (tn): The words “his name is” are supplied for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי אִם רָע.* 
לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר: יַעַן שִׁלַּחְתָּ אֶת אִישׁ חֶרְמִי וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *only bad.* For he said to me, Since you released the man whom I designated for destruction…

notes.1218: (tn, Heb): “were sitting, a man on his throne.”
notes.1219: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

notes.1220: (tn, Heb): “the words of the prophets are [with] one mouth good for the king.”
notes.1221: (tn, Heb): “let your words be like the word of each of them and speak good.”

notes.1222: (sn): “Attack! You will succeed; the Lord will hand it over to the king.” One does not expect Micaiah, having just vowed to speak only what the Lord tells him, to agree with the other prophets and give the king an inaccurate prophecy. Micaiah’s actions became understandable later, when it is revealed that the Lord desires to deceive the king and lead him to his demise. The Lord even dispatches a lying spirit to deceive Ahab’s prophets. Micaiah can lie to the king because he realizes this lie is from the Lord. It is important to note that in v. 14 Micaiah only vows to speak the word of the Lord; he does not necessarily say he will tell the truth. In this case the Lord’s word itself is deceptive. Only when the king adjures him to tell the truth (v. 16), does Micaiah do so.

rashi.heb:
*עֲלֵה וְהַצְלַח.* 
לֹא אָמַר לוֹ בְּשֵׁם ה'.
rashi.eng: *Go up and triumph.* He did not say it to him in the name of the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*וְנָתַן ה'.* 
הַלְוַאי יִתֵּן בְּיַד הַמֶּלֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *and may the Lord deliver it.* If only the Lord deliver it into the king’s hand.

notes.1224: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*לֹא אֲדֹנִים לָאֵלֶּה.* 
אַתָּה לְבַדְּךָ תָּמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: לֹא תִּלָּחֲמוּ אֶת קָטֹן וְאֶת גָּדוֹל כִּי אִם אֶת מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַדּוֹ. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְעַמְּךָ תַּחַת עַמּוֹ, טִפָּה שֶׁיָּצְאָה מֵאוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק מִיכָיְהוּ, שֶׁהִכָּהוּ חֲבֵרוֹ הַכֵּה וּפָצוֹעַ, הָיְתָה כַּפָּרָה עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל. כָּךְ מְפֹרָשׁ בָּאַגָּדָה.
rashi.eng: *These have no master.* You alone will perish in the war, as it is stated below (v. 31), “Do not battle with great or small, except with the king of Israel only.” Even though it was stated, (above 20:42) “and your people instead of his people,” the drop of blood that came out of the righteous man, Micaiah, whose friend struck him, striking and wounding him, was an atonement for all Israel. So it is explained in the Aggadah.

notes.1225: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*מִימִינוֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.* 
וְכִי יֵשׁ שְׂמֹאל לְמַעְלָה, וַהֲלֹא נֶאֱמַר: יְמִין ה' רוֹמֵמָה יְמִין ה' עוֹשָׂה חָיִל: יְמִינְךָ ה' נֶאְדָּרִי בַכֹּחַ יְמִינְךָ ה' תִּרְעַץ אוֹיֵב, אֶלָּא אֵלּוּ מַיְמִינִים וְאֵלּוּ מַשְׂמְאִילִים, מַיְמִינִים מְלַמְּדִים זְכוּת, מַשְׂמְאִילִים מְלַמְּדִים חוֹבָה.
rashi.eng: *On His right and on His left.* Now is there left in Heaven? It is not stated, (Ps. 118:16) “The right hand of the Lord is exalted; the right hand of the Lord does valiantly;” (Ex. 15:6) “Your right hand, O Lord, is mighty with power; Your right hand, O Lord, dashes the foe?” But rather, the passage means that these would stand on the right and these would stand on the left. Those who stand on the right present the case for the defense and those who stand on the left present the case for the prosecution.

notes.1227: (tn, Heb): “the spirit.” The significance of the article prefixed to רוּחַ (ruakh) is uncertain, but it could contain a clue as to this spirit’s identity, especially when interpreted in light of v. 24. It is certainly possible, and probably even likely, that the article is used in a generic or dramatic sense and should be translated, “a spirit.” In the latter case it would show that this spirit was vivid and definite in the mind of Micaiah the storyteller. However, if one insists that the article indicates a well-known or universally known spirit, the following context provides a likely referent. Verse 24 tells how Zedekiah slapped Micaiah in the face and then asked sarcastically, “Which way did the spirit from the Lord (רוּחַ־יְהוָה, [ruakh-Yahweh], “the spirit of the Lord”) go when he went from me to speak to you?” When the phrase “the spirit of the Lord” refers to the divine spirit (rather than the divine breath or mind, Isa 40:7, 13) elsewhere, the spirit energizes an individual or group for special tasks or moves one to prophesy. This raises the possibility that the deceiving spirit of vv. 20-23 is the same as the divine spirit mentioned by Zedekiah in v. 24. This would explain why the article is used on רוּחַ; he can be called “the spirit” because he is the well-known spirit who energizes the prophets.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֵּצֵא הָרוּחַ.* 
רוּחוֹ שֶׁל נָבוֹת.
rashi.eng: *And a certain spirit came forth.* The spirit of Naboth.

notes.1228: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.1229: (tn): The Hebrew text has two imperfects connected by וְגַם (v�gam). These verbs could be translated as specific futures, “you will deceive and also you will prevail,” in which case the Lord is assuring the spirit of success on his mission. However, in a commissioning context (note the following imperatives) such as this, it is more likely that the imperfects are injunctive, in which case one could translate, “Deceive, and also overpower.”

rashi.heb:
*אֵי זֶה עָבַר רוּחַ ה'.* 
אֵי זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ עָבַר, וַהֲרֵי זֶה מִקְרָא קָצָר, בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים כְּתִיב: אֵי זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ עָבַר וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *Which did the spirit of the Lord pass.* Which way did it pass? This is an abbreviated verse. In II Chron. 18:23, it is written: “which way (דרך) did… pass.”

notes.1230: (tn, Heb): “the bread of affliction and the water of affliction.”
notes.1231: (tn, Heb): “come in peace.” So also in v. 28.

notes.1233: (tn): The Hebrew verbal forms could be imperatives (“Disguise yourself and enter”), but this would make no sense in light of the immediately following context. The forms are better interpreted as infinitives absolute functioning as cohortatives. See IBHS 594 �35.5.2a. Some prefer to emend the forms to imperfects.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל יְהוֹשָׁפָט הִתְחַפֵּשׂ וָבֹא בַמִּלְחָמָה.* 
לְהִתְחַפֵּשׂ וְלָבֹא, אֲנִי אֶתְחַפֵּשׂ, אֲשַׁנֶּה בִגְדֵי מַלְכוּתִי שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּנִי, שֶׁאִם יַכִּירוּנִי יָסוּרוּ אֵלַי לְהִלָּחֵם.
rashi.eng: *And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself and go into battle.* [lit. disguise and go into battle. He told Jehoshaphat of his plans] to disguise himself and go [into battle]. I will disguise myself I will change my regal garb, lest they recognize me, for if they recognize me, they will turn to me to attack me.

rashi.heb:
*וְאַתָּה לְבַשׁ בְּגָדֶיךָ.* 
שֶׁעָלֶיךָ, שֶׁלֹּא מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל אָתָּה, אֶלָּא מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה, וְעִמְּךָ אֵין לָהֶם תְּגָר.
rashi.eng: *and you wear your regal garb.* that you are wearing, for you are not the king of Israel, but the king of Judah, and with you they have no conflict.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּזְעַק יְהוֹשָׁפָט.* 
לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
rashi.eng: *and Jehoshaphat cried out.* to the Holy One, Blessed be He.

notes.1235: (tn, Heb): “now a man drew a bow in his innocence” (i.e., with no specific target in mind, or at least without realizing his target was the king of Israel).
notes.1236: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וְאִישׁ מָשַׁךְ.* 
זֶה נַעֲמָן.
rashi.eng: *A man drew.* This was Naaman.

rashi.heb:
*לְתֻמּוֹ.* 
לֹא יָדַע שֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
rashi.eng: *innocently.* not knowing that he was the king of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*בֵּין הַדְּבָקִים וּבֵין הַשִּׁרְיָן.* 
יֵשׁ שִׁרְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם עֲשׂוּיִין קְלִפִּים קְלִפִּים, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְשִׁרְיוֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂים, וְהַקְּלִפִּים נוֹפְלִים עַל נִקְבֵי הַשִּׁרְיוֹן וְסוֹתְמִין אוֹתָן, וְהֵם קְרוּיִין דְּבָקִים.
rashi.eng: *between the scales and the coat of mail.* Some coats of mail are made of layers of scales, in the manner it is stated (I Sam. 17:5) “and a coat of mail,” and the scales fall on the holes of the coat and close them, and they are called דבקים.

rashi.heb:
*מַעֳמָד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה.* 
מִתְחַזֵּק וְעוֹמֵד, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַכָּתוֹ וְיִבְרְחוּ, וּתְחִלַּת נְפִילָה נִיסָה.
rashi.eng: *was standing in the chariot.* He exerted himself to remain standing so that the Israelites would not become aware of his wound and flee, for flight is the beginning of defeat.

notes.1238: (tn, Heb): “and the king died and he came to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.”

notes.1240: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּלֹקּוּ הַכְּלָבִים אֶת דָּמוֹ.* 
וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי, שֶׁשָּׁם נֶהֱרַג נָבוֹת, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמַר הַנָּבִיא בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר לָקְקוּ הַכְּלָבִים אֶת דַּם נָבוֹת וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *and the dogs licked his blood.* I say that Naboth was killed there, for the prophet said, “In the place that the dogs have licked the blood of Naboth…” (21:19).

rashi.heb:
*וְהַזֹּנוֹת רָחָצוּ.* 
וּכְלֵי הַזַּיִן רָחֲצּוּ שָׁם מִן הַדָּם, כָּךְ תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ אַחְאָב מְצֻנָּן הָיָה, וְעָשְׂתָה לּוֹ אִיזֶבֶל דְּמוּת שְׁתֵּי זוֹנוֹת בְּמֶרְכַּבְתּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *and they washed the weapons there of the blood.* Jonathan rendered it in this manner. Our Rabbis said, [however, rendering ‘zonoth’ as harlots,] “Ahab was a cold person [who disliked sexual relations” (San. 39b)]. Therefore, Jezebel made for him the image of two harlots in his chariot to stimulate him. [When the chariot was washed, these two images were washed in the pool of Samaria.]

notes.1241: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the acts of Ahab and all that he did, and the house of ivory which he built and all the cities which he built, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

rashi.heb:
*וּבֵית הַשֵּׁן.* 
שֵׁן דְּפִיל.
rashi.eng: *the ivory palace.* Heb. ביתהשן, lit. the palace of the tooth, i.e.,] elephant tooth.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּשְׁלֵם יְהוֹשָׁפָט עִם מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
לְפִי שֶׁמִּלְחָמָה הָיְתָה בֵּין אָסָא אָבִיו וּבֵין בַּעְשָׁא מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל, הֻזְקַק לוֹמַר כֵּן.
rashi.eng: *Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.* Since there was war between Assa his father and Baasha the king of Israel, it was necessary to say this.

notes.1247: (tn, Heb): “and the rest of the male cultic prostitutes who were left in the days of Asa his father, he burned from the land.” Some understand the verb בִּעֵר (bi’er) to mean “sweep away” here rather than “burn.” See the note at 1 Kgs 14:10. Despite Asa’s opposition to these male cultic prostitutes (see 1 Kgs 15:12) some of them had managed to remain in the land. Jehoshaphat finished what his father had started.

rashi.heb:
*וְיֶתֶר הַקָּדֵשׁ.* 
נוֹהֲגִין נִאוּף בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא.
rashi.eng: *The remainder of the prostitutes.* who fornicated in public.

notes.1248: (tn, Heb): “a fleet of Tarshish [ships].” This probably refers to large ships either made in or capable of traveling to the distant western port of Tarshish.

rashi.heb:
*וּמֶלֶךְ אֵין בֶּאֱדוֹם.* 
בִּימֵי דָוִד, הַנָּצִיב הוּא הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְכָאן נִכְתַּב, לְפִי שֶׁבִּימֵי יְהוֹרָם בְּנוֹ שֶׁקִּלְקֵל, בְּיָמָיו פָּשַׁע אֱדוֹם וַיַּמְלִיכוּ לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ, אֲבָל בִּימֵי יְהוֹשָׁפָט עֲדַיִן הָיוּ כְּפוּפִין לוֹ.
rashi.eng: *There was no king in Edom.* Since the time of David, the governor was the king This was written here because in the days of Jehoram his son who sinned, in his days Edom rebelled and crowned a king for themselves, but in the time of Jehoshaphat they were still subordinate to him.

notes.1249: (tn, Heb): “Let my servants go with your servants in the fleet.”

rashi.heb:
*כִּי נִשְׁבְּרוּ אֳנִיּוֹת.* 
לְפִי שֶׁנִּתְחַבֵּר עִם אֲחַזְיָהו בָּזֹאת, לְכָךְ נִשְׁבְּרוּ. וְכֵן אָמַר לוֹ הַנָּבִיא בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים: בְּהִתְחַבֶּרְךָ עִם אֲחַזְיָהוּ פָּרַץ ה' אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ.
rashi.eng: *since the ships were broken.* Since he joined Ahaziah in this undertaking, therefore, they were broken. And so did the prophet say to him in II Chron. (20:37), “Because you have joined a wicked man (sic), the Lord has caused a breach in your undertaking.”

rashi.heb:
*בִּשְׁנַת שְׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה לִיהוֹשָׁפָט.* 
יֵשׁ מַתְמִיהִים עַל הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה, לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַחְאָב שֶׁמָּלַךְ עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם, וּבִיהוֹשָׁפָט נֶאֱמַר שֶׁעָמַד בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאַחְאָב, נִמְצָא שֶׁכָּלוּ יְמֵי אַחְאָב בִּשְׁנַת תְּשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה לִיהוֹשָׁפָט, וְכָאן הוּא אוֹמֵר שֶׁמָּלַךְ אֲחַזְיָה בִּשְׁנַת שְׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה לִיהוֹשָׁפָט. אַךְ בָּדַקְתִּי וּמָצָאתִי בְּדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְדַקְדֵּק בְּמִנְיַן שְׁנוֹתֵיהֶם, וְאִם עָמַד בְּסוֹף שָׁנָה, מוֹנֶה אוֹתָהּ לוֹ בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ מוֹנֶה אוֹתָהּ לוֹ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, לְכָךְ אֲנִי אוֹמֵר, בִּשְׁנַת אַרְבַּע לְאַחְאָב שֶׁאָמַר בַּעֲמִידָתוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹשָׁפָט, לֹא נִמְנֵית עִמּוֹ שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל אַחְאָב, וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא בְּרֻבָּם, וְגַם שָׁנָה שֶׁעָמַד יְהוֹשָׁפָט, לֹא נִמְנֵית בִּשְׁנַת שְׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה הַלָּלוּ.
rashi.eng: *in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat.* Some wonder about this verse, since it is stated concerning Ahab that he reigned twenty-two, and concerning Jehoshaphat it is stated that he became king in the fourth year of Ahab. It is found that Ahab’s rule ended in the nineteenth year of Jehoshaphat. Yet here [Scripture states that Ahaziah became king in the seventeenth year of Jeohshaphat. However, I searched and found that concerning most kings of Israel [Scripture] is not exact in the number of their years, and if one became king at the end of a year, he counts it at the beginning, but he does not count it elsewhere. Therefore, I say that “in the fourth year of Ahab” (v. 41) that is mentioned in reference to Jehoshaphat’s becoming king, does not count with it Ahab’s first year. And so you find in the majority of cases. Also, the year in which Jehoshaphat became king is not included in these seventeen years.
